papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ULTRA-LOW-DOSE CT VS. STANDARD-DOSE CT FOR PULMONARY NODULE DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
authors: KHALED BONNA , RASHA GALAL ELSAFTY , NORA EID ALANAZI , RANIN JABER M ALMAJRASHI AHLAM ALI Y ASIRI , WALEED MUFAREH ALSHAHRANI , SOMAYYAH SOHAIL MITHA , SHOUG NASSER ALKHAMMASH , BANDAR SAAD ALSHREEF
papers.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
papers.abstract: Background: Standard dose computed tomography (CT) is a primary modality for detecting pulmonary nodules (PNs), but the health risk from cumulative radiation exposure has prompted the emergence of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) as an alternative to reduce this dose, because its diagnostic accuracy remains variable, this systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the existing evidence to determine the diagnostic accuracy and effective radiation dose of ULDCT for pulmonary nodule detection. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Ovid MEDLINE for original research published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ULDCT for PN detection, for which a meta-analysis using random-effects models was performed to calculate the pooled sensitivity for nodule detection and the pooled mean effective radiation dose, with a subgroup analysis conducted to assess the impact of different reconstruction algorithms. Results: Forty-two studies comprising 15,792 patients were included, from which a meta-analysis of 11 studies demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 91.9% (95% CI: 84.6%–97.1%) for PN detection with heterogeneity (I²=93.0%), and a pooled mean effective dose from 12 studies of 0.22 mSv (95% CI: 0.11–0.33 mSv), a level comparable to standard chest radiography, while subgroup analysis revealed a trend towards higher sensitivity with advanced reconstruction algorithms (96.7%) compared to standard iterative reconstruction (87.9%) that was not statistically significant (p=0.091), and a narrative synthesis confirmed ULDCT's accuracy for solid nodules but identified reduced sensitivity for subsolid, ground-glass, and small (<6 mm) nodules, with performance limited in patients with a high body mass index (BMI). Conclusion: ULDCT combined with advanced reconstruction techniques offers high diagnostic accuracy for the detection of solid pulmonary nodules and reduces radiation exposure to levels approaching that of a chest X-ray, but its utility is limited for detecting subsolid and small nodules and in obese patients, making protocol standardization and patient-specific considerations essential to optimize its clinical implementation.

papers.title: Efficient deoxygenation of palm oil to green diesel using a metal oxide catalysts supporting on ZrO2-enhanced graphene oxide
papers.journal: Universiti Putra Malaysia Institutional Repository (Universiti Putra Malaysia)
papers.abstract: NiO, Fe2O3, and bimetallic oxide NiFe2O4 catalysts supported on graphene oxide and promoted with ZrO2 were synthesized via wet-impregnation approach. A systematic characterization of the catalysts physicochemical properties was evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), Temperature-programmed desorption CO2 (TPD-CO2), Brunaur-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area, Field emission Scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis. The catalysts were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts in the deoxygenation (DO) of palm oil for green diesel production under varying operating conditions. Among the catalysts tested, Fe2O3/ZrO2-GO (calcined at 400 °C for 4 h, 5 wt% loading) demonstrated superior catalytic activity, achieving a maximum hydrocarbon yield (HC%) of 98.0%, bio-jet fuel (BJF) selectivity of 40%, and kerosene yield of 86%. The exceptional performance is attributed to the catalyst’s large BET surface area (18.64 m2/g), substantial pore volume (0.027 cm3 /g), and moderate surface basicity (3234.65 μmol/g), which collectively facilitate efficient deoxygenation via decarboxylation (DCO2) and decarbonylation (DCO) pathways while suppressing undesired cracking. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited remarkable stability and reusability over four consecutive reaction cycles, retaining 92% hydrocarbon yield and 80.9% kerosene yield, with BJF selectivity increasing to 84%. The gradual decline in performance is attributed to carbon deposition (coke formation), pore blockage, and sintering-induced degradation of the mesoporous network, as confirmed by post-reaction XRD and BET analysis.

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Reconfigurable Computing for Accelerated Matrix Computations in High-Performance Embedded Systems
papers.journal: SCCTS Journal of Embedded Systems Design and Applications
papers.abstract: The emergence of data-hungry systems in the form of artificial intelligence, real-time signal processing, and scientific computing systems inside embedded systems has set extremely high requirements to the computational capabilities, electrical energy efficiency and flexibility. The computational backbone of many of these applications is matrix computations, that typically face bottlenecks in traditional processor architectures because of individual resources having no parallelism, and a lack of dynamism in resource allocation. In order to overcome such limitations, this paper introduces a new reconfigurable computing implementation, called Quantum-Inspired Matrix Engine (QIME) that emulates all three of these important quantum computing concepts of superposition, parallelism, and entanglement in a classical hardware setting. The system of the proposal will be applied to the Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), and here, the system will be used to incorporate a pseudo-quantum state encoding process that enables the representation and processing of multiple matrix states simultaneously. QIME also has dynamic partial reconfiguration (DPR) so as to further have flexibility and efficiency in matching the architecture in real time with the nature and the complexity of the operations performed in the matrix. Also, there is approximate computing, where computational precision is traded off against performance where the tradeoff is allowed to increase energy profiles under workload variability. Experimental analysis of some typical benchmarks on matrices, including multiplication, decomposition, and convolution, shows that for representative operations QIME provides up to 6.3x speedup and 4.1x energy efficiency improvements over typical matrix co-processors and embedded GPUs. These findings will support the viability of quantum-inspired design paradigms in moving forward the performance and scalability of high-performance embedded systems, especially in the edge, and constrained circumstances where conventional quantum hardware is infeasible.

papers.title: Active Visual Perception: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.abstract: Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired. However, differences in how studies define active perception and evaluate its benefits make approaches difficult to compare across tasks. This review first clarifies the field’s functional scope by examining whether an action is selected for its expected effect on subsequent visual evidence and whether the resulting observation informs a later decision. This definition distinguishes active observation acquisition from processing fixed inputs and guides the selection of representative literature. Within this scope, this review develops an analytical framework organized around four questions. It begins with what evidence the task requires, examines which actions can obtain that evidence and how a candidate observation should be valued, and considers how the next sensing action should be selected and executed. New observations then update the perceptual state and guide subsequent decisions, forming a closed loop that provides a common basis for comparing methods across applications. To examine how their benefits can be demonstrated, this review assesses whether existing datasets support observation selection, how interactive environments enable controlled comparisons, and what physical platforms reveal about execution feasibility. It further examines how baseline comparisons can establish whether adapting observations is necessary and whether informed selection offers benefits beyond simpler sensing strategies. These considerations underpin an evaluation framework that links improvements in visual evidence to downstream task outcomes while accounting for acquisition costs and risks. Its core value is to help isolate the contribution of sensing decisions and determine whether their benefits justify the resources required. The analysis concludes that predicted observation value does not guarantee that useful evidence can be acquired through feasible actions, while task success alone cannot establish the benefit of active observation selection. Further progress requires reliable value estimation and planning over longer decision sequences under physical and resource constraints. It also requires grounding semantic reasoning in acquired evidence and maintaining effective collaboration under imperfect communication, with these capabilities verified through reproducible evaluation of the complete perception and action loop.

papers.title: Superconducting half-dome in bilayer nickelates
papers.abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges and collapses in correlated electron systems remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics. As a recently discovered member of the high temperature superconductor family, bilayer nickelates provide a new opportunity for examining this problem. Their pronounced sensitivity to oxygen stoichiometry, while posing challenges for stabilizing superconductivity, simultaneously offers an effective control parameter for tuning electronic phases. Here we report a superconducting half-dome in compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films as a function of continuous tuning of oxygen stoichiometry. Starting from an optimally superconducting state, increasing oxygen stoichiometry gradually suppresses superconductivity toward a metallic phase, whereas decreasing oxygen stoichiometry drives a granular superconductor-to-insulator transition while leaving the superconducting onset intact. This half-dome structure can be understood to arise from the contrasting roles played by interstitial oxygen versus oxygen vacancies - namely the dominance of doping versus scattering. Notably, the half-dome emerges consistently across samples with different rare-earth combinations, with or without alkaline-earth doping, revealing a general feature of the bilayer nickelate phase diagram.

papers.title: Supercurrent-driven Néel torque in superconductor/altermagnet hybrids
papers.abstract: We predict a supercurrent-driven Néel spin-orbit torque in a superconductor/$d$-wave altermagnet heterostructure, associated with the emergence of spin-triplet correlations. The effect can be understood as a consequence of the supercurrent-induced spin polarization, owing to the interplay between spin orbit coupling and momentum-dependent spin splitting, as found, for example, in altermagnets. Remarkably, the supercurrent can be tuned by the Néel-vector direction, and the supercurrent-induced torque can both propel magnetic domain walls and reverse the Néel-vector orientation within a domain wall. These findings establish superconductor/altermagnet heterostructures as a versatile platform for the {supercurrent-driven} control of the Néel vector, with potential applications in racetrack memory, dissipationless superconducting electronics, and unconventional computing.

papers.title: The association between diabetic retinopathy and cognitive impairment in patients with diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a recognized microvascular complication of diabetes in which neurovascular and neurodegenerative mechanisms may also contribute. This systematic review evaluated the association between DR and cognitive impairment or dementia, including Alzheimer’s disease and vascular dementia, using evidence from cross-sectional and longitudinal observational studies. Methods We searched for relevant articles up to December 2025 from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. Two independent reviewers extracted data from the selected studies, including baseline information and outcomes. All quantitative syntheses were conducted using R version 4.4.1. Results Fourteen studies with reported study populations totaling 2,871,847 participants were included. Seven studies contributed to the crude dichotomous synthesis, which did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between diabetic retinopathy and cognitive impairment or dementia (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.94–1.23; p=0.310; I 2 =52.3%). Seven studies contributed adjusted longitudinal estimates for incident dementia; diabetic retinopathy was associated with a higher incidence of dementia (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.19–2.02; p=0.001; I 2 =97.8%; 95% prediction interval 0.65–3.68). Evidence concerning Alzheimer’s disease and vascular dementia remained inconsistent. Conclusion Longitudinal evidence suggests that diabetic retinopathy is associated with a higher incidence of dementia, although substantial heterogeneity and the observational evidence base limit confidence in the pooled estimate. Evidence concerning Alzheimer’s disease and vascular dementia remains inconclusive. Systematic review registration https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/YS462 , identifier YS462.
papers.summary: Background Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a recognized microvascular complication of diabetes in which neurovascular and neurodegenerative mechanisms may also contribute. This systematic review evaluated the association between DR and cognitive impairment or dementia, including Alzheimer’s disease and vascular dementia, using evidence from cross-sectional and longitudinal observational studies. Conclusion Longitudinal evidence suggests that diabetic retinopathy is associated with a higher incidence of dementia, although substantial heterogeneity and the observational evidence base limit confidence in the pooled estimate.

papers.title: Perspective: Quantum Computing on Magnetic Racetrack
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic domain walls have long been pursued as carriers of classical information for storage and processing. With the ability to create, control, and probe domain walls at the nanoscale, they are recently recognized as an ideal platform for studying macroscopic quantum effects and provide a natural blueprint for building scalable quantum computing architectures. In particular, the experimentally demonstrated high mobility of domain walls makes them not only suitable as stationary qubits but also as flying qubits, which may offer advantages over currently explored quantum computing platforms. In this Perspective, we outline our current understanding of the essential ingredients and key requirements for realizing universal quantum computation based on magnetic domain walls. We highlight promising concrete material platforms and identify the experiments that are still needed to advance this concept. We also discuss the potential challenges and point to new opportunities in this emerging research direction at the interface between magnetism and quantum information science.

papers.title: Metropolis-scale resilient and trustworthy traffic flow inference using multi-source data
papers.journal: Transportation Research Part C Emerging Technologies
papers.abstract: Inferring network-wide traffic states from sparse observations with high accuracy and trustworthy uncertainty quantification is essential for intelligent transportation systems, yet it remains challenging due to the underdetermined nature of the problem, multifaceted disturbances in sensing networks, and the inherent conflicts among multiple inference subtasks when modeled jointly. We propose the Task-Aware Attentive Neural Process (TA-ANP), a unified probabilistic framework for resilient and trustworthy global traffic state inference (GTSI) by fusing floating car data (FCD) with sparse fixed-detector measurements. By casting GTSI as a stochastic process, TA-ANP leverages the meta-learning properties of neural processes to adapt rapidly to changes in sensing configurations without retraining. A task-aware multi-query attention module with distinct spatiotemporal inductive biases is introduced to jointly handle three GTSI subtasks—real-time estimation at unobserved locations, forecasting at both observed and unobserved locations—while mitigating cross-task interference. For uncertainty quantification, we combine neural processes with Monte Carlo Dropout to capture both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. To support metropolis-scale evaluation, we construct the Metropolitan Multi-Source Traffic Dataset (MMTD), integrating fixed-loop sensor measurements, FCD statistics, and OpenStreetMap road-network data over an urban network of 26,166 road segments, including 2371 fixed-sensor-equipped segments used for quantitative evaluation. Experiments across multiple independently generated sensor configurations show that TA-ANP achieves best performance across all subtasks under deterministic and probabilistic metrics. The resulting well-calibrated uncertainties enable more efficient fixed-sensor placement with fewer sensor deployments. Under a Damage–Repair–Addition sensing lifecycle, TA-ANP demonstrates superior resilience in terms of disturbance absorption, performance recovery, and adaptability to unseen sensing configurations.The code and processed datasets are publicly available on GitHub and Zenodo , respectively.

papers.title: Quaternion Dirac–Coulomb–Breit integral transformation for relativistic four-component correlated electronic structure theory
papers.abstract: High-accuracy correlated four-component relativistic electronic structure methods are typically formulated in terms of integrals over molecular orbitals (MOs). Consequently, an efficient and scalable strategy is required to deal with the complexity of transforming relativistic two-electron integrals from the atomic orbital (AO) to the MO basis. The transformation bottleneck is particularly acute for approaches that include Breit interaction integrals, whose computational and memory demands further exacerbate the transformation cost. To overcome this challenge, we develop a quaternion-based, AO-driven direct integral transformation scheme. The method operates on scalar AO integrals and combines quaternion density-based contractions with direct Cauchy–Schwarz screening to systematically exploit integral locality. As a result, the proposed framework substantially lowers the practical computational scaling and provides an efficient, memory-conscious, and highly parallelizable pathway for the routine inclusion of relativistic Dirac–Coulomb–Breit integrals in large-scale four-component correlated calculations.

papers.title: Dark matter in composite Higgs models with a scotogenic EFT
papers.abstract: We discuss a class of Composite Higgs models with a fermionic UV completion that can explain the dark matter relic density. The resulting low-energy theory resembles so-called scotogenic models. A residual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry implies that one of the pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone bosons is stable and therefore is a viable dark matter candidate. As a concrete example, we take a model based on the $\mathrm{SU}(6)/\mathrm{Sp}(6)$ coset, which in principle contains four dark matter candidates. However, only three of them can produce a relic density consistent with observations. We perform a MCMC study focusing on dark matter observables to explore the available parameter space of the effective theory. In particular, we find that spin-1 resonances play an important role in a substantial part of the parameter space. Finally, we comment on possible LHC signatures of this model class.

papers.title: Understanding spatial and temporal evolution of progressive excavation damage zone in granitic rocks – development of a novel mine-by and laboratory experimental framework at the BedrettoLab
papers.abstract: Abstract. The brittle damage around tunnels in the form of spalling is common in massive crystalline rocks subjected to high in-situ stresses. Understanding the short-term development and long-term evolution of the Excavation Damage Zone (EDZ) is particularly important for deep geological repositories (DGRs) for heat-generating nuclear waste, as the EDZ may provide preferential pathways for radionuclide migration. This paper presents an overview of the PRECODE mine-by experiment at BedrettoLab, a newly developed underground research laboratory (URL) in southern Switzerland designed to investigate brittle fracturing and EDZ evolution in crystalline rocks under repository-relevant conditions. The PRECODE tunnel was excavated in Rotondo Granite using both controlled drill-and-blast (D&B) and line-drilling and rock-breaking (LDRB) methods to evaluate the influence of excavation technique on EDZ characteristics. The experiment combines multidisciplinary in-situ monitoring including acoustic emission, distributed acoustic and strain sensing, hydraulic monitoring, electrical resistivity tomography, and terrestrial laser scanning with laboratory-based fracture mechanics and time-dependent testing under varying environmental conditions. The main objectives are to characterize short-term EDZ formation, investigate long-term crack growth and stress corrosion processes, quantify permeability evolution, and assess the interaction between excavation-induced damage and nearby fault zones. Preliminary results indicate clear differences in AE activity and EDZ development between excavation methods, while observations from the mature EDZ of the more than 40-year-old Bedretto Tunnel suggest ongoing time-dependent brittle fracturing. The coupled in-situ and laboratory datasets provide a unique basis for improving predictive models and long-term safety assessments for nuclear waste repositories in crystalline rocks.

papers.title: Turning Readily Available Acrylates into Cyclic Xanthates for Radical Ring-Opening Polymerizations
papers.abstract: Abstract Cyclic sulfur-containing monomers represent a promising class of comonomers for radical ring-opening polymerization, but only a limited number of examples have been reported to date. Here, the cyclic xanthate tert-butyl 2-thioxo-1,3-oxathiolane-5-carboxylate (Oxa) was synthesized from readily available tert-butyl acrylate via epoxidation and subsequent ring extension with carbon disulfide. While homopolymerization was not observed, efficient copolymerization with vinyl acetate yielded copolymers containing dithiocarbonate units in the polymer backbone. Reactivity ratio analysis revealed a preference for heteropropagation, enabling efficient incorporation of dithiocarbonate units with Oxa contents of up to 40 mol %, at which compositions the copolymers displayed a tendency toward an alternating microstructure. The resulting copolymers were highly transparent and colorless and exhibited molar masses and glass transition temperatures comparable to those of poly(vinyl acetate). The incorporated dithiocarbonate units enabled selective backbone cleavage by aminolysis, base-mediated hydrolysis, or oxidative degradation, whereas acidic conditions (0.5 M HCl) did not affect the polymers. Copolymers containing at least 25 mol % Oxa generated low-molar-mass degradation products, confirming the efficient incorporation of degradable units into the polymer chains. These results establish cyclic xanthates derived from a readily accessible acrylate precursor as a versatile platform for introducing chemically degradable dithiocarbonate functionalities into vinyl acetate-based polymers.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT AND PHARMACOKINETIC EVALUATION OF AN IMMEDIATE-RELEASE TABLET FORMULATION OF ENZALUTAMIDE
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is a major global health concern, with GLOBOCAN 2022 reporting 1,467,854 new cases and 397,430 deaths worldwide. Enzalutamide, a second-generation androgen receptor inhibitor, is widely used for advanced prostate cancer; however, its extremely poor aqueous solubility limits dissolution and oral availability. This study aimed to develop an optimized immediate-release Enzalutamide tablet using hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetate succinate (HPMCAS) as a concentration-enhancing polymer. Preformulation studies, including solubility, UV spectrophotometry, DSC, FTIR, particle size, and flow properties, were performed. Nine formulations (EF1–EF9) containing 40 mg Enzalutamide were prepared and evaluated. EF4 showed satisfactory tablet properties, with 99.67 ± 0.94% drug content, 2.49 ± 0.14 min disintegration, and 0.21% friability. It demonstrated rapid dissolution, releasing 97.4 ± 0.8% drug at 30 min and 99.8 ± 0.3% at 45 min. Pharmacokinetic evaluation showed enhanced Cmax and AUC with EF4 compared with the comparator. Accelerated stability testing indicated minimal changes over three months. Thus, EF4 represents a promising immediate-release formulation for improving the oral performance of poorly water-soluble Enzalutamide.

papers.title: Reviving Time-Degraded Cement: Sustainable Performance and Structural Resilience of Concrete with Hybrid Admixtures
papers.abstract: Long storage of cement under humid or improperly controlled conditions may lead to pre-hydration, particle agglomeration, and loss of reactivity, which lead to material wastage and economic loss.This study explores the possibility of using time degraded cement in M25 grade concrete with the addition of Glass powder, Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag (GGBS), Silica fume and Chemical admixtures.Four mixtures were created: a fresh PPC control mixture and three mixtures with varying amounts of time degraded cement and supplementary cementitious materials.Workability was determined by slump-cone test and compressive strength was determined at 7, 14 and 28 days.Selected mixtures were also tested by Ultrasonic Pulse Velocity and carbonation-depth tests.The slump values measured were between 70 and 93 mm, which is satisfactory but not the desired workability.The 28-day values for the control mixture, glass-powder mixture and GGBS-based mixture were 29.20, 30.50 and 30.60 MPa, respectively.The mixture with GGBS and silica fume had 24.90 MPa.Hence, the maximum strength was achieved using 10% time degraded cement and GGBS.The results show the potential of recovering partially degraded cement with the hybrid binder systems, with the need for replicate testing and long-term durability testing prior to structural application.

papers.title: Sustainable agro-waste ash reinforced aluminium matrix composites with emerging potential of nano-banana peel ash in Al7075
authors: Ch. V S R Satya Prasad
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of sustainable aluminium matrix composites using agricultural waste-derived reinforcements provides an alternative approach to utilizing biomass residues in advanced engineering materials. In this study, nanoscale banana peel ash (Nano-BPA) was synthesized through dehydration, calcination, and high-energy ball milling and incorporated into an Al7075 alloy by stir casting. Nano-BPA was characterized using particle size analysis (PSA), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The Al7075 base alloy and composites containing 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA were fabricated and evaluated under dry sliding wear, Charpy impact, and immersion corrosion conditions. Particle size analysis yielded a D50 value of 20.2 nm, with D10 and D90 values of 12.4 and 33.8 nm, respectively. The specific wear rate decreased from 1.160 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for Al7075 to 8.456 × 10⁻⁵ and 3.315 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m) for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA composites, respectively. The absorbed impact energy increased from 5.5 ± 0.20 J for Al7075 to 7.0 ± 0.25 and 8.0 ± 0.30 J for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA composites, respectively. After 72 h of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, the measured corrosion rate decreased from 0.649 ± 0.027 mm/year for Al7075 to 0.460 ± 0.027 and 0.203 ± 0.014 mm/year for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA composites, respectively. Among the investigated compositions, the 4 wt% Nano-BPA composite exhibited the best overall measured performance. These results demonstrate the feasibility of Nano-BPA as a sustainable reinforcement for improving the experimentally evaluated wear, impact, and corrosion performance of Al7075 composites.

papers.title: Monomer Sequence Architecture Tunes the Performance of Poly(octadecyl acrylate- co -styrene) Pour Point Depressants in Waxy Oils
papers.abstract: Abstract Monomer sequence architecture is an underexplored design parameter for polymeric pour point depressants (PPDs). Here, octadecyl acrylate-styrene (OA-St) copolymers with statistical, block, and gradient architectures were synthesized by free-radical and reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerization. Time-resolved 1H NMR spectroscopy and GPC supported the progressive compositional and molar-mass evolution expected for the intended gradient architecture for P(OA-g-St) 3:1. The prepared copolymer series exhibited distinct low-temperature behavior of both model wax oil and Daqing crude oil. The gradient copolymer with an OA/St ratio of 3:1 showed the best overall performance, reducing the model-oil pour point from 26.0 to 7.0 °C and the viscosity at 10 °C by approximately 97%. It also decreased the pour point of Daqing crude oil from 32.0 to 25.0 °C. DSC and quantitative microscopy showed that the gradient architecture weakened wax crystallization and produced compact, uniformly dispersed wax crystals. These observations are consistent with, but do not directly establish, a working model in which the programmed OA/St distribution regulates wax association, crystal growth, and wax-network organization. Within the investigated OA/St system, the results identify programmed monomer distribution as a promising design variable for PPD performance.

papers.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Poly (Vinyl Alcohol) Biofilms Reinforced With Alkali‐Treated Sapindus mukorossi Shell Filler
papers.journal: Journal of Vinyl and Additive Technology
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer films composed of biodegradable polymers containing lignocellulosic fillers have been identified as good candidates for substitution for conventional petroleum‐derived packaging materials. In the current study, polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) biofilms containing 5–25 wt% alkali‐treated Sapindus mukorossi shell filler (at. SMSF) were synthesized through the solution casting method. The objective of this study is to explore the structure of PVA biofilms, thermal behavior, mechanical behavior, optical, surface, and antibacterial properties. The removal of amorphous parts through alkali treatment exposed cellulose‐filled microfibrils, resulting in the development of strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds with the PVA matrix. FTIR showed improvement in interfacial compatibility without the creation of any new chemical bond. On the other hand, XRD analysis depicted an increase in crystallinity from 32.5% to 54.8% and crystallite size from 18.2 to 31.3 nm. Thermal analysis proved that the biofilms exhibited good thermal stability and high degradation temperatures, along with a reduction in heat flow and an increase in char formation. SEM and surface roughness analysis depicted uniform dispersion of fillers and compact morphology, especially in the case of medium loading of fillers. There was significant enhancement in mechanical properties, where tensile strength and Young's modulus increased from 23.5 to 46.8 MPa and from 29.5 to 62.3 MPa, respectively. The contact angle of water increased from 51.3° to 92.5°, showing remarkable improvement in water repellence. Moreover, PVA/25 wt% at. SMSF showed significant UV‐blocking efficiency and very good antibacterial properties toward Escherichia coli and Bacillus cereus . The results showed that alkaline‐treated SMSF can be a very good bio‐component to develop mechanically tough, thermally stable, moisture‐resistant, and antibacterial PVA biofilm for use as a packaging material.

papers.title: Formulation of Co-crystals of Lopinavir using Co-former to Enhance Solubility and Bioavailability
papers.journal: Journal of Drug Delivery and Therapeutics
papers.abstract: The poor aqueous solubility and limited oral bioavailability of many antiviral drugs, particularly lopinavir, present major challenges to effective oral drug delivery. Lopinavir exhibits low solubility, poor intestinal permeability, and variable absorption, resulting in reduced therapeutic efficacy. The present study aimed to develop and evaluate pharmaceutical cocrystals of lopinavir using pharmaceutically acceptable coformers to enhance its physicochemical and biopharmaceutical properties without altering its pharmacological activity. Cocrystals were prepared using crystal engineering techniques, including solvent evaporation, slurry conversion, and solvent-assisted grinding. The prepared formulations were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), to confirm cocrystal formation and investigate structural modifications. Solubility, dissolution, and stability studies were conducted to compare the optimized cocrystals with pure lopinavir. The results demonstrated a marked improvement in aqueous solubility and dissolution rate, attributed to the formation of a modified crystal lattice and intermolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions between lopinavir and the selected coformer. The optimized cocrystals also exhibited satisfactory physicochemical stability while maintaining the therapeutic integrity of the drug. These findings suggest that pharmaceutical cocrystal engineering is a promising, scalable, and regulatory-acceptable approach for enhancing the oral bioavailability and therapeutic performance of poorly soluble antiviral drugs such as lopinavir. Improved dissolution characteristics may contribute to reduced dose variability, enhanced patient compliance, and better clinical outcomes. Keywords: Pharmaceutical cocrystals; Antiviral drugs; Solubility enhancement; Bioavailability; Coformers; Dissolution rate; Drug delivery; Crystal lattice modification

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERISATION OF QUERCETIN PHYTOSOMES FOR ENHANCED ANTIOXIDANT ACTIVITY
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Quercetin is a naturally occurring flavonoid with well-established antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and therapeutic potential; however, its clinical application is significantly limited by poor aqueous solubility, low oral bioavailability, and rapid metabolism. The present study aimed to develop and optimize a quercetin phytosomal formulation using phosphatidylcholine to enhance its physicochemical characteristics and antioxidant performance. Quercetin phytosomes were prepared by the solvent evaporation (thin-film hydration) technique, and formulation variables including phospholipid concentration, drug concentration, and stirring time were systematically Optimised. The Optimised formulation (P6) with a drug-to-phospholipid ratio of 1:2 exhibited the most desirable physicochemical characteristics, including a particle size of 218.4 ± 12.6 nm, zeta potential of −29.6 ± 1.7 mV, porosity of 61.8 ± 2.5%, and an entrapment efficiency of 93.8 ± 1.9%, indicating efficient molecular complexation and excellent colloidal stability. Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) demonstrated the disappearance of the characteristic crystalline melting peak of quercetin, confirming successful formation of the quercetin–phosphatidylcholine molecular complex and reduced drug crystallinity. In vitro drug release studies revealed a sustained release profile, achieving 82.9% cumulative drug release over 24 h, with release kinetics best described by the Higuchi diffusion model and Korsmeyer–Peppas analysis indicating a nonFickian diffusion mechanism. Furthermore, the Optimised phytosomal formulation exhibited concentrationdependent antioxidant activity, demonstrating significantly greater free radical scavenging than free quercetin at equivalent concentrations, with 72.80 ± 0.65% DPPH inhibition at 100 µg/mL compared with 65.40 ± 0.75% for free quercetin. The enhanced antioxidant activity was attributed to improved aqueous dispersibility, higher drug entrapment, and sustained release from the phospholipid matrix. Overall, the developed quercetin phytosomal system effectively overcame the inherent limitations of quercetin by improving drug encapsulation, physicochemical stability, controlled release, and antioxidant efficacy. These findings demonstrate the potential of phytosomal technology as a promising lipid-based delivery platform for enhancing the therapeutic performance of poorly water-soluble flavonoids and support its further evaluation for pharmaceutical applications.

papers.title: Interpretable surrogate modeling for load-aware thermal risk assessment of bolted switchgear busbar joints using electro-thermal simulation
papers.abstract: Thermal-risk assessment of bolted busbar joints is complicated by the coupled effects of electrical loading, contact condition, and heat dissipation. This study develops an interpretable forward-surrogate framework based on three-dimensional electro-thermal finite-element simulation. Physics enters through finite-element generation of the training data, physically defined input variables, and post hoc consistency checks, rather than through constraints embedded in the learning algorithm. Five prescribed inputs were considered: load current, contact resistance, effective contact ratio, ambient temperature, and convective heat-transfer coefficient. The effective-contact heating power was checked against P ≈ I 2 R c , with a maximum relative deviation of 0.173% across 400 simulated cases; 382 cases were retained within the intended applicability domain. Four candidate models were compared using 5 × 10 repeated cross-validation. The XGBoost regressor achieved R 2 = 0.990 ± 0.005 , R M S E = 1.877 ± 0.542 , and M A E = 1.042 ± 0.198 K , with performance comparable to random forest. For four-class simulation-oriented thermal-risk classification, XGBoost achieved an accuracy of 0.938 ± 0.026 and a macro F1-score of 0.941 ± 0.033 . SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified load current and prescribed contact resistance as the dominant contributors, while convection, ambient temperature, and effective contact ratio produced smaller, condition-dependent effects. The lower global importance of effective contact ratio reflects the area-averaged temperature-rise target and does not imply that current constriction is physically unimportant. Across three threshold schemes, all out-of-fold errors were between adjacent classes. The framework is geometry-specific and has not been experimentally validated. It predicts internal effective-contact temperature rise; relating this quantity to infrared surface measurements requires further validation.

papers.title: Structure–Property Relationships of PAM/CMC-Based Semi-IPN Hydrogels: Influence of APS/ANI Ratio on Swelling, Electrical, Thermal, and Morphological Properties
papers.abstract: Abstract In this work, semi-interpenetrating network (semi-IPN) hydrogels based on polyacrylamide (PAM)/CMC matrices incorporating polyaniline (PANI) were synthesized to investigate the influence of the ammonium persulfate/aniline (APS/ANI) ratio on structure–property relationships. Hydrogels were prepared via free radical polymerization of PAM/CMC followed by in situ polymerization of aniline within the preformed matrix, yielding composites with systematically varied APS/ANI ratios. Swelling studies in 1.0 mol L–1 HCl revealed that the incorporation of PANI reduced the equilibrium electrolyte swelling degree relative to PAM/CMC hydrogels, yet promoted specific ionic interactions with Cl– ions, strongly dependent on the oxidant/monomer ratio. Electrical conductivity analysis reached values up to 10–2 S·cm–1, with the highest performance observed for hydrogels synthesized at intermediate APS/ANI ratios. Morphological (SEM/EDX) and structural (FTIR, UV–Vis, XRD) analyses demonstrated that PANI formed dendritic-like microstructures distributed within the CMC-containing matrix, while XRD results correlated crystallinity variations with electrical performance. Thermal analysis (TGA) indicated differences in the thermal degradation behavior of the composites compared with the PAM/CMC matrix. These findings highlight the central role of the APS/ANI ratio in modulating the swelling, structural organization, and electroactive properties of PAM/CMC/PANI semi-IPN hydrogels, providing insights for the design of polysaccharide-based conductive materials with potential applications in electroactive devices.

papers.title: Stress Regulation through Precursor Chemistry: From Synthesis to Cycling Stability in O3‐Type Layered Oxide Cathodes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered oxide cathode materials have broad application prospects in sodium‐ion batteries. However, conventional oxide solid‐state synthesis route, transition metal oxides slowly participate in the reaction step by step, causing residual stress accumulation and cycling degradation. Herein, a synthesis strategy utilizing low‐melting‐point metal salt precursors is proposed. Leveraging their synchronous decomposition and liquid‐like characteristics, a uniform chemical environment is generated, fundamentally suppressing the uneven accumulation of residual stress. Thermal analysis and kinetic calculations demonstrated that the reaction activation energy of the metal salt system (NFM‐A) was significantly reduced and exhibited a more stable variation profile. This effectively circumvented the asynchronous reaction process caused by diffusion kinetic differences inherent to the traditional oxide route (NFM‐O). Multiple experimental characterizations consistently confirmed that the residual stress of NFM‐A was low and uniformly distributed. After prolonged cycling, NFM‐A maintained a uniform lattice strain distribution with complete and dense particle morphology, while continuous stress concentration, interlayer slip, and particle cracking occurred in NFM‐O. Combined with in situ XRD and finite element simulations, the critical role of the initial stress distribution in maintaining structural integrity during electrochemical cycling is revealed. This establishes stress regulation as a key criterion for designing layered oxide cathode materials with high structural stability.

papers.title: Isothermal Crystallization Behavior of Polypropylene/Polyolefin Elastomer with β -Nucleating Agent
papers.journal: Journal of Macromolecular Science Part B
papers.abstract: The effect of β-nucleating agent (β-NA) and polyolefin elastomer (POE) on the crystal structure and isothermal crystallization of polypropylene (PP) was studied by using polarized optical microscopy (POM), scanning electron microscope (SEM), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and rheological measurements. The results indicated that the self-assembled needlelike β-NA significantly promoted the crystallization process of the PP matrix, which accelerated the crystalline transformation from α-crystal to β-crystal in DSC cyclic scans. Owing to the POE improved the dispersion of β-NA in polymer matrix, the half crystallization time and activation energy of the PP/POE/β-NA blend were the lowest among all PP specimens. Furthermore, the values of Avrami exponent were less than 2 for PP/β-NA and PP/POE/β-NA blends, which is much lower than that of pure PP.

papers.title: Hierarchical Ion-Conducting Materials Based on Polymer-Aligned Nanoparticles within Poly(vinyl benzyl methoxy poly(ethylene oxide) ether)- block -polystyrene Diblock Copolymer
papers.abstract: Abstract Solid polymer electrolytes based on poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) are promising alternatives to liquid electrolytes for safer lithium-ion batteries. Here, we report hierarchical solid polymer electrolytes obtained by selectively incorporating lithium sulfonamide-functionalized polymer nanoparticles (LiNPs) into a microphase-separated poly(vinyl benzyl methoxy poly(ethylene oxide) ether)-block-polystyrene block copolymer. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) demonstrate that the phase-segregated lamellar morphology of the block copolymer is preserved upon nanoparticle incorporation. Notably, the LiNPs preferentially localize within the poly(ethylene glycol)-rich lamellae, generating hierarchical structures with ordering across multiple length scales arising from block copolymer self-assembly, selective nanoparticle organization, and poly(ethylene glycol) crystallization. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) reveals that the crystallinity of the poly(ethylene glycol) phase depends strongly on nanoparticle loading and plasticizer content. These hierarchical electrolytes exhibit high ionic conductivity, which is further enhanced by the addition of sulfolane as a plasticizer. These results elucidate the interplay between hierarchical morphology, phase crystallinity, and ion transport in block copolymer-based solid electrolytes, providing design guidelines for mechanically robust solid electrolytes with enhanced transport performance.

papers.title: Performance and Interaction Mechanisms of Bitumen Modified with Devulcanized Rubber-Recycled Polymer Composites
papers.abstract: The accumulation of end-of-life tires and post-consumer polyolefin waste is a growing environmental burden, and their reuse as bitumen modifiers offers a sustainable, large-volume outlet in road construction. This study investigated paving-grade bitumen modified with four pre-compounded, partially devulcanized rubber (DVR)-recycled-polymer composites, differing in polymer type and, for two of the systems, in styrene–butadiene–styrene (SBS) chain architecture (linear or radial), added at 9–15 wt.%. The modified binders were characterized by penetration, softening point, elastic recovery, force ductility, low-temperature brittleness, and dynamic shear rheometry (DSR), together with FTIR, TGA, and fluorescence microscopy. All four composites improved binder stiffness, elasticity, and high-temperature rheology relative to the unmodified bitumen, with the two SBS-containing systems performing best overall. At the highest modifier content, the best-performing composite roughly halved the penetration and raised both the softening point and the higher critical temperature or rutting parameter by approximately 28–30 °C, while also markedly improving elastic recovery and low-temperature flexibility relative to the base bitumen. These findings indicate that SBS-containing devulcanized-rubber/recycled-polymer composites are promising sustainable modifiers for producing high-performance bituminous binders from waste-derived materials.

papers.title: Valorization of molecularly imprinted polymer for the rapid and selective detection of levofloxacin in milk
papers.abstract: Levofloxacin (LFX) is widely used in the dairy industry, which raises serious concerns about its residues in dairy products. Herein, we report the synthesis of a magnetically separable molecularly imprinted polymer (MMIP) for the selective extraction of LFX from milk samples. MMIP was prepared by surface imprinting polymerization and characterized by fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM). The MMIP presented high adsorption capacity, fast binding kinetics and good selectivity for LFX, with a recovery of 92.6% under the optimized conditions. The developed method showed excellent linearity from 0.1–0.50 µg L −1 , high precision and a low relative standard deviation (RSD) of 2.20%. High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis confirmed the efficient extraction of LFX residues from milk samples. The MMIP showed an imprinting factor of 2.12, which indicated higher selective recognition than the non-imprinted polymer. Furthermore, the MMIP exhibited better reusability, maintaining the structural and functional integrity in five successive adsorption–desorption cycles. Although the developed platform showed efficient extraction of LFX from milk matrices, further studies involving structurally related antibiotics, biological validation and large-scale application are needed.

papers.title: Unleashing Platinum‐Sulfur Synergy in Ultranano‐Structured Conjugated Porous Polymers Based on Thiazole for Efficient Hydrogen Generation
authors: Víctor A. de la Peña O’Shea
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The molecular design of conjugated porous polymers (CPPs) offers a powerful strategy to control their optoelectronic properties and interactions with semiconductor and metallic cocatalyst interfaces. Here, we develop an ultrananostructured thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole (TzTz)‐based CPP (UN_IEP‐48), whose sulfur‐containing units provide favourable sites for interaction with Pt. High‐performance microfluidic processing enables its intimate integration with TiO 2 , yielding an optimized UN_IEP‐48@T3 hybrid containing only 3 wt.% polymer. Photoluminescence and transient absorption spectroscopy reveal efficient charge separation consistent with a direct Z‐scheme mechanism, directing the reduction pathway toward the CPP. Remarkably, photodeposition of only 0.5 wt.% Pt increases the H 2 evolution rate from 3.0 to 94.3 mmol g −1 h −1 , corresponding to a 30‐fold enhancement and a photonic efficiency of 34.91%. Increasing Pt loading to 1 wt.% provides essentially no further improvement, highlighting efficient noble‐metal utilization. Microscopy reveals preferential Pt localization on polymer‐rich regions, while FTIR, XPS, and electrochemical impedance measurements support strong Pt–TzTz interactions and facilitated electron transfer. These results demonstrate how molecular engineering of CPPs can couple nanoscale heterojunction formation with cocatalyst interfacial chemistry, maximizing photocatalytic H 2 production while minimizing noble‐metal loading.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence as academic infrastructure: governance, administrative intelligence, and AI fluency in Kazakhstan’s higher education sector
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly part of higher education's institutional infrastructure, extending beyond teaching and learning to governance, administration, and student support. This study examines how AI Governance Readiness (AIGR) influences Administrative Efficiency through AI (AEAI), AI Fluency Orientation (AIFO), and Student Retention Intentions (SRI), while assessing the mediating roles of AEAI and AIFO and the moderating role of Equity Perception (EPS) in Kazakhstan's higher education sector. Drawing on Dynamic Capability Theory and Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study develops and empirically tests an institutional capability model using 935 valid responses from students, faculty, academic administrators, and digital administration staff across public and private universities. The scholars analyzed the data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.0, supported by RStudio. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity, while the structural model showed adequate explanatory and predictive performance. We assessed common method bias through procedural safeguards and full-collinearity diagnostics, and identified no substantive concerns. The findings show that AIGR is positively associated with AEAI and AIFO, while both constructs positively influence SRI. AEAI and AIFO also significantly mediate the relationship between AIGR and SRI. However, EPS does not significantly moderate the relationships between AI-enabled institutional capabilities and retention intentions. The findings position AI governance as a strategic institutional capability through which universities can improve administrative responsiveness, develop AI-related competencies, and support student continuity. The study contributes empirical evidence from Kazakhstan to the growing literature on responsible AI governance and digital transformation in higher education.

papers.title: Protein-like Behavior of Statistical VCL-VI Block Copolymers
papers.abstract: Abstract Amphiphilic copolymers of N-vinylcaprolactam (VCL) and N-vinylimidazole (VI) were synthesized via free-radical copolymerization in bulk. The phase behavior was systematically investigated using a combination of nephelometric methods, dynamic light scattering, UV spectroscopy, and high-sensitivity differential scanning calorimetry. These copolymers undergo a coil-to-globule conformational transition in aqueous solutions upon heating to 65 °C, while maintaining complete optical homogeneity and avoiding macroscopic phase separation. To better understand our results, model copolymers were obtained within the framework of reactive dissipative particle dynamics simulations under conditions reproducing the experimental synthesis. Overall, the model copolymers exhibit, on the one hand, the monomer unit distribution statistics characteristic of random copolymers and, on the other hand, a nonuniform gradient distribution type. In a selective solvent mimicking water above the lower critical solution temperature of poly-VCL, they form core–shell nanostructures, with solvophilic VI units comprising the outer shell. A strikingly unexpected result of the modeling was the conclusion that the distinct protein-like behavior of the experimentally synthesized polymers can be explained using models of copolymer chains with an apparently statistical nature and a gradient distribution of monomer units. Thus, the biomimetic behavior in our experimentally synthesized VI–VCL copolymers may be rationalized by a finely tuned balance between the average lengths of VCL- and VI-rich sequences along the chain, which can be governed by the reactivity ratios of the comonomers and the initial monomer feed composition.

papers.title: Contrasting microbiomes in deep-sea scleractinian and octocoral species from the South Atlantic Ocean
papers.abstract: Abstract Deep-sea corals (DSC) are ecologically important, yet their microbiomes’ composition, structure, and host specificity remain largely unresolved in the South Atlantic, especially for octocorals. Here, we provide a comprehensive characterisation of DSC microbiomes, spanning Hexacorallia (Desmophyllum pertusum, Solenosmilia variabilis) and Octocorallia (Candidella imbricata, three Malacalcyonacea species), collected at ∼710 m depth in the Campos Basin, an active oil- and gas-producing region. Abiotic characterisation revealed total hydrocarbon concentrations. Seawater and sediment samples provided further environmental context. Amplicon sequencing (16S rRNA gene), combined with alpha and beta diversity analyses, differential abundance analysis, and indicator species analysis, revealed that each coral species harboured a microbial community structure distinct from the surrounding environment, with host specificity varying along a continuum. C. imbricata was the individually resolved coral species with the most specialised microbiome, dominated by Endozoicomonadaceae, the lowest Shannon diversity, the highest intragroup homogeneity, and the largest number of indicator amplicon sequencing variants (ASVs). D. pertusum showed no exclusive indicators, overlapping broadly with environmental communities, but selectively enriched the potentially hydrocarbon-degrading family Halieaceae. To our knowledge, these findings establish the first microbial baseline for DSC holobionts in this region, documenting contrasting host-specificity across scleractinian and octocoral taxa.

papers.title: Regulatory mechanism of M2d tumor-associated macrophage-derived exosomal apolipoprotein E on platinum resistance in ovarian cancer
papers.abstract: Background Platinum-based chemotherapy plus cytoreductive surgery represents the standard first-line therapy for ovarian cancer (OC), which yields robust early therapeutic responses in most patients. However, platinum resistance is a formidable clinical hurdle, and how macrophages mediate drug resistance within the OC tumor microenvironment remains poorly understood. Methods We cultured SKOV3 OC cells and THP-1 monocytes, induced THP-1 differentiation into M2d tumor-associated macrophages. Stable apolipoprotein E (ApoE) -overexpressing SKOV3 cell lines were constructed via lentiviral transfection and puromycin screening. We established nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models with mixed tumor cells and M2d macrophages, administered cisplatin treatment and collected tumor tissues after sacrifice by cervical dislocation. RNA was extracted from tumor samples to conduct RT-qPCR for gene expression detection. Tumor tissue sections were prepared for HE staining, TUNEL apoptosis staining, and Western blot analysis to detect ApoE and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway protein expression. Results Using nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models, we demonstrated that M2d-type tumor-associated macrophages (M2d TAMs) promote platinum resistance and elevate tumoral ApoE levels. In OC xenografts with stable ApoE overexpression, cisplatin-induced apoptosis was profoundly repressed, resulting in reduced cisplatin sensitivity, while this inhibitory effect was not observed in the empty vector control group. Mechanistically, ApoE activates the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling cascade to counteract cisplatin cytotoxicity by suppressing cell death and sustaining pro-survival signals. Conclusions Overall, this study reveals that M2d TAMs induce platinum resistance in OC cells via exosomes carrying ApoE.

papers.title: FORMULATION OPTIMIZATION AND EVALUATION OF CHLORPHENIRAMINE MALEATE ORODISPERSIBLE FILMS PREPARED BY SOLVENT CASTING FOR RAPID DRUG RELEASE
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Orodispersible films (ODFs) have gained considerable attention as patient-centric drug delivery systems owing to their rapid disintegration, ease of administration, and improved compliance, particularly among pediatric, geriatric, and dysphagic patients.The selection of an appropriate film-forming polymer is a critical determinant of the mechanical strength, disintegration, and drug release characteristics of ODFs.Objective: This study aimed to develop and optimize chlorpheniramine maleate-loaded ODFs using different viscosity grades of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC E3, HPMC E6, and HPMC E15) prepared by the solvent casting method and to evaluate their physicochemical, mechanical, and in vitro performance.Methods: Eighteen formulations were prepared using varying concentrations of HPMC with polyethylene glycol 400 and propylene glycol as plasticizers.The films were evaluated for appearance, thickness, weight variation, folding endurance, tensile strength, percentage elongation, drug content, disintegration time, and dissolution profile.Drug-excipient compatibility was investigated using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), while surface morphology was characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).Accelerated stability studies were performed in accordance with ICH guidelines.Results: All formulations exhibited acceptable physicochemical and mechanical properties.Polymer viscosity significantly influenced film performance, with formulation F2 demonstrating rapid disintegration, excellent mechanical characteristics, and 99.53 ± 1.80% drug release within 10 min.FTIR, DSC, and SEM analyses confirmed drug compatibility and uniform drug distribution.The optimized formulation remained stable under accelerated storage conditions.Conclusion: The optimized HPMC-based chlorpheniramine maleate ODF represents a promising patient-friendly alternative to conventional tablets, with polymer viscosity playing a key role in determining film quality and drug release behavior.

papers.title: Multifunctional UV-curable carbon nanofiber coatings on hemp/viscose nonwovens: electrostatic dissipation, thermal stability, and electromagnetic shielding behavior
papers.journal: Journal of Coatings Technology and Research
papers.abstract: Abstract Natural fiber-reinforced composites are widely studied as sustainable alternatives to synthetic materials due to their lightweight and renewable nature. In this study, a hemp/viscose spunlace nonwoven was coated with a UV-curable elastomeric resin containing carbon nanofibers (CNF) and acid-activated carbon nanofibers (ACNF) at 0.75, 1.5, and 3 wt%. Acid activation introduced oxygen-containing functional groups, improving nanofiller dispersion and interfacial adhesion. The composites were characterized by FTIR, RAMAN, TGA, XRD, contact angle, surface resistivity, and EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) analyses. Microscopy confirmed successful nanofiller incorporation, particularly in ACNF-modified samples. Surface resistivity results showed a concentration-dependent decrease in resistivity, indicating a shift toward electrostatic dissipative behavior. ACNF samples exhibited lower resistivity than untreated CNF systems. Thermal analysis revealed enhanced thermal stability and higher char residue in reinforced composites. Although measurable attenuation was observed, the SE values (<5 dB) indicate that a fully developed conductive network was not established within the investigated filler range. These findings suggest that the current formulations primarily provide electrostatic dissipation rather than effective electromagnetic shielding. Overall, UV-curable CNF/ACNF coatings improved surface functionality and thermal performance, but low filler contents limited electromagnetic shielding efficiency.

papers.title: Anti-obesogenic potential of curcumin, disulfiram, and their synergistic effects in HFD-fed obese Swiss albino mice
papers.abstract: Aims This study aimed to investigate the preventive anti-obesogenic effects of disulfiram and curcumin, including their potential synergistic effects, in a high-fat diet-induced obese and diabetic mouse model by evaluating body weight gain, food intake, glycaemic control, lipid profile, insulin and leptin levels, liver injury markers, and histopathological changes. Diabetes and obesity are dual pandemics affecting millions of people worldwide. Curcumin, commonly used in Indian kitchens, and the repurposed drug Disulfiram, previously used for other purposes, are evaluated to assess their anti-obesogenic properties. Materials and methods Inducing obesity and diabetes through an HFD in Swiss albino mice provides a suitable strategy for testing the preventive effects of supplements or drugs against obesity. To achieve this, we established five groups: one fed a control diet, one fed an HFD, and three treatment groups that received curcumin, Disulfiram, or both simultaneously by oral gavage. We measured food intake, weight gain, the Lee obesity index, lipid profiles, liver injury enzymes, insulin and leptin levels, and liver histopathological changes. Results These results suggest that treating high-fat diet (HFD)- fed mice with either Curcumin or Disulfiram alone, or combining both simultaneously, for 12 weeks effectively controls weight gain, improves glucose metabolism, reverses abnormal lipid profiles, and reduces Insulin and Leptin resistance. Conclusion The combination treatment with Curcumin and Disulfiram shows a synergistic effect and a significantly enhanced anti-obesogenic effect. However, treatment with Curcumin alone also shows greater effectiveness compared to Disulfiram alone.

papers.title: Outbreak and suppression of a self-coup in a consolidated democracy: South Korea’s 2024 experience
papers.abstract: Abstract This essay examines the outbreak and suppression of a self-coup in South Korea in 2024. It focuses on the critical period between the declaration of martial law on the night of December 3 and its termination in the early hours of December 4, explaining the background, outbreak, and suppression of the self-coup through the strategic actions of actors and the historical legacies. The self-coup emerged in the context of a narrowing political base of the presidency, deteriorating everyday economic conditions, and changes in presidential control over the military. Following electoral defeat and growing political pressure, the president declared martial law by mobilizing military forces. Its suppression resulted from a cumulative interaction between coup-initiating and opposing actors. Opposition politicians and citizens rapidly gathered at the National Assembly, enabling the vote that legally and institutionally terminated martial law. The coup initiators chose a time and date that facilitated resistance, while military units showed limited compliance when confronted with unarmed civilians. The abolition of the garrison decree after the 2016 impeachment left an institutional legacy, while the historical legacy of the 1980 Gwangju Democratic Uprising provided politicians and citizens with an interpretive and normative resource for understanding the situation and acting despite risks.

papers.title: Fused Granulate Fabrication of Virgin and Reprocessed PLA/Silicon Dioxide Nanocomposites: Processing, Mechanical Integrity, and Soil Microbial Respiration Response
papers.journal: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing
papers.abstract: This study evaluates processing via fused granulate fabrication (FGF) of nanocomposites based on virgin polylactic acid (PLA) and thermomechanically reprocessed polylactic acid (rPLA), incorporated with 0 wt%, 5 wt%, and 10 wt% of silicon dioxide (SiO2) nanoparticles. Rheological analysis revealed that rPLA exhibited a 42.4 % increase in melt flow rate compared to PLA, which can be attributed to thermomechanical chain scission occurring during reprocessing. At 10 wt% filler loading, the tensile strength along the XZ build direction tended to decrease. Scanning electron microscopy analysis suggests that this trend is related to nanoparticle agglomeration. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that adding 5–10 wt% SiO2 restored the lower initial thermal degradation onset of rPLA (T5%loss=313°C) to values equal to or exceeding PLA (323–324°C), while overall crystallinity remained near 0% owing to rapid convective cooling during FGF printing. Short-term soil respirometry trials using extruded granule samples revealed that rPLA exerted a temporary respirometric inhibition, reducing soil basal respiration by 22.5%. The incorporation of 10 wt% SiO2 recovered 96.3% of the native soil metabolic activity by increasing extruded granules surface wettability and water availability at the particle interface. These findings demonstrate that the control of SiO2 loading enables the tuning of mechanical performance, establishing a framework for sustainable, large-format PLA components with tailored end-of-life properties.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, Structural Characterization, β-LactamaseResponsive Polymeric Nanoformulation, and Experimental Pharmacological Evaluation of Novel Ceftriaxone–Quercetin Hybrid Molecules for the Treatment of Multidrug-Resistant Bacterial Infections
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial pathogens has become a major global health concern due to the declining effectiveness of conventional antibiotics. β-lactamase-mediated resistance significantly limits the therapeutic efficacy of β-lactam antibiotics such as ceftriaxone, necessitating the development of innovative antimicrobial strategies. The present study aimed to design a novel ceftriaxonequercetin hybrid molecule and incorporate it into a β-lactamase-responsive polymeric nanoformulation to enhance antibacterial activity against MDR bacterial infections. Methods: Ceftriaxone–quercetin hybrid molecules were synthesized using carbodiimide-mediated coupling chemistry and characterized by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), UV–Visible spectroscopy, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR), Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS), and HighPerformance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC). The optimized hybrid compound was encapsulated into βlactamase-responsive poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles using the solvent evaporation method. The nanoformulation was evaluated for particle size, zeta potential, morphology, encapsulation efficiency, and enzyme-responsive drug release. Antibacterial activity was assessed against multidrug-resistant bacterial strains, including Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Cytotoxicity was evaluated using the MTT assay on HEK293 and L929 cell lines. Results: The hybrid molecule was successfully synthesized with a yield of 78.6% and a purity of 98.4%. Structural characterization confirmed successful conjugation of ceftriaxone and quercetin. The prepared nanoparticles exhibited an average particle size of 176.8 ± 8.5 nm, zeta potential of −24.8 ± 1.6 mV, encapsulation efficiency of 87.9 ± 2.3%, and drug loading of 15.8 ± 0.7%. The nanoformulation demonstrated β-lactamase-responsive drug release, achieving 91.4% cumulative drug release within 48 hours in the presence of the enzyme. Compared with ceftriaxone alone, the hybrid-loaded nanoparticles showed significantly enhanced antibacterial activity, producing larger zones of inhibition and lower minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values against all tested MDR bacterial strains. Cytotoxicity studies indicated high biocompatibility, with cell viability remaining above 85% at therapeutic concentrations. Conclusion: The findings demonstrate that the ceftriaxone–quercetin hybrid incorporated into β-lactamaseresponsive polymeric nanoparticles provides a promising therapeutic strategy for combating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The combination of molecular hybridization and enzyme-responsive nanotechnology Design, Synthesis, Structural Characterization, β-Lactamase-Responsive Polymeric Nanoformulation, and Experimental Pharmacological Evaluation of Novel Ceftriaxone–Quercetin Hybrid Molecules for the Treatment of Multidrug-Resistant Bacterial Infections improved antibacterial efficacy, targeted drug delivery, and biocompatibility, highlighting its potential as a nextgeneration antimicrobial formulation. Further in vivo investigations and clinical studies are warranted to establish its translational potential.
