The optimized hybrid compound was encapsulated into βlactamase-responsive poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles using the solvent evaporation method. papers.title: Unraveling the K+ transporter gene family in rice: evolution, subcellular localization, K+ uptake activity, and transcriptional responses to salt stress
papers.abstract: Rice is a global staple food crop, and its yield is seriously limited by soil salinity. The high-affinity K + transporter/K + uptake permease/K + transporter (HAK/KUP/KT) family of potassium transporters plays a pivotal role in K + homeostasis and plant salt tolerance. However, their systematic characterization and functional relevance to salt tolerance in rice have not been clarified. Here, we conducted genome-wide identification and structural characterization of the HAK/KUP/KT family, assessed their expression profiles under salt stress, and examined their K + transport function. In total, 27 OsHAK genes were identified in the rice genome, most of which exhibited salt-responsive expression. Yeast functional complementation assays confirmed that OsHAK11, OsHAK13, OsHAK23, OsHAK24, OsHAK25, and OsHAK26 can mediate K + absorption. Among them, OsHAK11 and OsHAK25 showed relatively strong K + uptake ability. Subcellular localization analysis revealed that OsHAK11 and OsHAK25 were located in the plasma membrane. Our research systematically analyzed the sequence characteristics of the rice HAK gene family, examined their transcriptional responses to salt stress, and further evaluated the K + uptake capacity of HAK proteins. These results provide a foundation for further elucidating the function of OsHAKs in plant salt tolerance.

papers.title: Flexural, viscoelastic, and wear behavior of fly ash cenosphere filled polyester resin composites
papers.journal: Journal of Reinforced Plastics and Composites
papers.abstract: The current study deals with the comprehensive analysis of flexural, viscoelastic, and wear properties of industrial waste fly ash cenosphere (FAC). The average particle size (D 50 ) of FAC is 63 µm. Fly ash cenosphere content is varied from 0, 5, 10, 20, and 40% by weight. Ball-on-disc tribometer is used for evaluating friction and wear properties of the composites at a speed of 200 rpm with an applied normal load of 15 N. Flexural modulus increased with an increase in the filler content by 50% at 40 wt%. Improved FAC dispersion in the polymer matrix was seen through flexural fractured scanning electron micrographs. A 54% increase is also seen in the storage modulus. Matrix-filler compatibility has been studied through dynamic mechanical thermal analysis parameters. No direct correlation between friction and wear was observed. The coefficient of friction of neat resin stands at 0.33, reaching 0.58 for 40 wt% FAC content and the specific wear rate (W s ) decreased up to 20 wt% of FAC content. At 40 wt% FAC loading, specific wear rate increased due to accumulation of FAC particles at the wear interface leading to increased particle-particle interaction resulting in particle-matrix debonding. Abrasive wear is the dominating wear mechanism as per worn surface morphology analyzed through SEM.

papers.title: Optimized microstructure and enhanced multifunctional properties of Sn-25Bi solder alloys reinforced with exfoliated Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of Ti3C2Tx MXenes incorporation on the structural, mechanical, thermal, electrical and wettability characteristics of the Sn-25Bi binary solder alloy. Design/methodology/approach Sn-25Bi-mTi3C2Tx nanocomposite solder alloys (m = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 Wt.%) were developed by blending Sn and Bi powders with Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets. The mixtures were compacted into disc-shaped pellets using a 12 mm diameter steel die and a manual hydraulic press with a 5-tonne jack, which ensured uniform densification and adequate green strength. Findings The incorporation of 0.4 Wt. % of Ti3C2Tx significantly enhances Vickers microhardness (Hv) and elastic modulus (Y), achieving values of 40.5 MPa and 0.67 GPa, respectively, which corresponds to about a 97% increase compared to the Ti3C2Tx-free alloy. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) indicated a decreased melting temperature of 194.99°C and a constricted mushy zone of ΔT = 11.29°C, implying enhanced thermal stability and consistent phase transition behavior at 0.4 Wt.%. Moreover, the solder’s wettability was improved, demonstrated by a minimum contact angle of 20.7° and a maximum spreading area of 0.773 cm2 at the identical composition. Electrical characterization demonstrated a substantial reduction in electrical resistivity (ρ) by approximately 35% and a notable increase in free electron concentration (N) and Fermi velocity (Vf). However, excessive MXene loading beyond 0.4 Wt.% resulted in agglomeration-induced performance degradation across all investigated properties. Research limitations/implications The results are confined to the Sn-25Bi/Ti3C2Tx formulations examined. Further microstructural examination is necessary to enhance comprehension of the distribution of MXene nanosheets and their interactions with the solder matrix. Further investigations ought to concentrate on the enduring thermal and electrical dependability of the fortified alloys under pertinent operational settings to clarify the mechanisms responsible for property improvements and assess the practical soldering utility of the optimized composition. Originality/value This study explores the development of MXene-reinforced Sn-25Bi solder alloys with optimized microstructure and enhanced multifunctional properties.

papers.title: Machine learning–driven strength prediction and optimal waste glass powder dosage for concrete exposed to high temperatures
papers.abstract: This study explores the synergistic effects of the addition of waste glass powder (WGP) and elevated temperatures on the mechanical behavior of concrete, and proposes a machine-learning-based framework for mixture design optimization. Six concrete mixtures containing 0–50% WGP were tested for compressive, flexural, and splitting tensile strengths over the temperature range 24–600 °C, and the results consistently showed an optimal WGP dosage of 10–20% at room temperature and a pronounced degradation in these strengths above 400 °C. To model the strength evolution across the entire WGP-temperature space, a physics-aware data augmentation method and a multi-output Random Forest surrogate model are developed and validated using mixture-wise three-fold cross-validation, parity plots, Y-randomization tests, SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification. The validated surrogate is then combined with NSGA-II to determine WGP dosages that simultaneously maximize room-temperature strength, high-temperature residual capacity, and material efficiency. Both prospective within-domain experimental validation showed close agreement between the surrogate predictions and independently measured responses. Contour maps and optimization results also consistently show that the 10–20% WGP dosage offers the best trade-off between initial strength and thermal resilience. The results demonstrate the two-fold role of WGP as a micro-filler in improving ambient performance and as a thermally sensitive phase governing degradation mechanisms at elevated temperatures. Therefore, this work presents a validated ML-based framework and practical design charts for optimizing WGP-modified concrete for fire-exposed or high-temperature applications. SEM analyses of the glass powder-reinforced concrete sample exposed to 600 °C showed an increase in cracks and voids in the microstructure; EDX results indicated Ca enrichment with the dominance of O (51.49%), Ca (20.78%), and Si (8.17%); FT-IR spectrum showed the disappearance of the ~ 3400 and ~ 1650 cm⁻¹ bands and the weakening of the ~ 950–1000 cm⁻¹ band, confirming C–S–H degradation; and XRD analysis revealed a decrease in amorphous humps and the prominence of crystalline peaks, indicating that the structure became more crystalline and brittle at high temperature. TGA results indicated that room-temperature-cured samples exhibited higher mass loss and progressive degradation at low temperatures, whereas samples pre-exposed to 600 °C exhibited reduced mass loss and enhanced thermal stability, owing to prior dehydration and microstructural reorganization.

papers.title: Gut microbial metabolism in aging: from metabolite production to organ-specific immunometabolic effects
papers.abstract: Age-related changes in gut microbiota metabolism are heterogeneous across populations and pathways, and their relationships with immunometabolism and organ phenotypes should be interpreted in the context of health status and disease. Microbial abundance or the concentration of a single metabolite does not, by itself, capture microbial production, host exposure, or effects in target tissues. This narrative review summarizes upstream influences, including gastrointestinal physiology, dietary substrates, comorbidities, and medications, and discusses the origins and host processing of major metabolites, their immunometabolic effects, and associated organ phenotypes. Studies in some older populations report lower fecal short-chain fatty acid concentrations. Microbiota-derived indole derivatives and host-synthesized, microbiota-modified bile acids show molecule- and population-specific patterns. Circulating concentrations of some host–microbe co-metabolites are higher in selected older or disease populations, but are also shaped by host biotransformation and clearance. Human evidence is predominantly observational and links metabolic features to health status or clinical phenotypes, whereas animal and cell studies support effects on barrier function, inflammation, and cellular metabolism under specific experimental conditions. Personalized nutrition, metabolite supplementation, selective targeting of microbial enzymes, and multi-omics-based responder stratification are promising research directions; prospective evidence that these strategies improve functional outcomes in older adults remains limited.

Personalized nutrition, metabolite supplementation, selective targeting of microbial enzymes, and multi-omics-based responder stratification are promising research directions; prospective evidence that these strategies improve functional outcomes in older adults remains limited.

papers.title: Formulation Development, Characterization And In Vitro Anticancer Evaluation Of Tamoxifen Citrate-Loaded Plga Nanoparticles Against Mcf-7 Breast Cancer Cells
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, necessitating the development of more effective and targeted drug delivery systems.The present study was designed to formulate and optimize tamoxifen-loaded poly(D,L-lactide-co-glycolide) (PLGA) nanoparticles for sustained drug delivery and enhanced in vitro anticancer activity against MCF-7 breast cancer cells.Nanoparticles were prepared by the nanoprecipitation method and optimized using a 3² factorial design by varying PLGA and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) concentrations.The optimized formulation exhibited a nanoscale particle size of approximately 187 nm, a polydispersity index below 0.20, zeta potential of -28.7 mV, and an entrapment efficiency exceeding 90%.FTIR and DSC analyses suggested successful encapsulation of tamoxifen without significant drug-excipient incompatibility, while SEM demonstrated spherical nanoparticles with smooth surfaces.The formulation exhibited a biphasic release profile with sustained drug release over 48 h and release kinetics consistent with diffusion-controlled behaviour.In vitro studies demonstrated enhanced cytotoxicity of tamoxifen-loaded PLGA nanoparticles compared with free tamoxifen, together with improved cellular uptake and increased apoptotic cell death in MCF-7 cells.Blank PLGA nanoparticles exhibited negligible cytotoxicity, indicating satisfactory biocompatibility.These findings illustrate the potential advantages of PLGA nanoparticles as a sustained drug delivery platform for tamoxifen and provide a framework for further studies.

papers.title: Comparative Screening of Stearate-Based Additives as Polylactide Clarifiers
papers.journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
papers.abstract: Abstract A variety of stearate-based additives are tested for their clarifying properties in polylactide (PLA) compounds. The tested fatty acid derivatives include metallic soaps, stearate esters and fatty acid amides. PLA exhibits favorable optical properties in its amorphous state, rendering it a viable biobased and biodegradable alternative to conventional transparent polymers. However, its crystallization induces pronounced light scattering, thereby limiting the application temperature of transparent PLA components to their glass transition temperature of 55–60 °C. While the clarifying properties of fatty acid amides in PLA are known, the potential of structurally related stearate-based additives has not yet been comparatively assessed. PLA compounds with 0.5 wt% of stearate-based additives are prepared with standard injection molding procedures, ensuring consistency with industrial processing. Samples are temperature treated at nominal oven temperature of 65 °C to examine crystallization. UV/Vis spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, polarized optical microscopy, and X-ray diffraction are applied to assess optical haze, crystallization kinetics, morphology, and crystal structure. The fatty acid amides show the strongest clarifying effect. Among the non-amide additives, zinc and glycerol distearate exhibit notable effects on haze formation and crystallization behavior. In contrast, sucrose distearate delays PLA crystallization. The results demonstrate that stearate-based additives can substantially modify PLA crystallization kinetics and optical properties, but also show that efficient PLA clarification is strongly dependent on additive chemistry. This comparative screening therefore provides insight into structure-dependent effects of fatty-acid-derived additives in PLA and identifies promising directions for further formulation development.

This comparative screening therefore provides insight into structure-dependent effects of fatty-acid-derived additives in PLA and identifies promising directions for further formulation development.

papers.title: In-flight receiver calibration of the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) by passive Earth observations
papers.abstract: Abstract. Post-launch characterization of the receiver telescope of the laser altimeter is essential for achieving precise georeferenced planetary measurements and for radiometric calibration to passively measure surface reflectance. For the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) aboard the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice), such in-flight calibration was originally planned during a lunar flyby but could not be performed due to an unexpected reboot of the instrument. Instead, this study reports a passive noise measurement acquired during the Earth-farewell campaign on 9 September 2024 as an alternative opportunity for in-flight calibration. Using temporal variations in the GALA noise level as a proxy for photon flux incident on the GALA detector, we combine a theoretical noise model with Earth images obtained by the Jovis Amorum ac Natorum Undique Scrutator (JANUS) imager to constrain the GALA receiver boresight direction. By comparing the timing, magnitude, and temporal pattern of noise variations between observations and simulations, we find that the pre-launch boresight vector is inconsistent with the Earth-farewell observations. Our results further suggest that the GALA receiver boresight may have experienced a post-launch offset over 700 μrad, although a definitive conclusion can be drawn only with additional cruise-phase data. The methodology developed in this study offers a framework for in-flight alignment calibration of GALA during future flybys, which is also broadly applicable to other planetary laser altimeters. The radiometric calibration performed in study is also prerequisite for the interpretation of passive albedo measurements of Jupiter and the Galilean moons.

papers.title: Systematic Literature Review: Pengaruh Manajemen Operasi Bisnis terhadap Kinerja Organisasi Bisnis di Indonesia
papers.journal: Jurnal Ilmu Sosial, Manajemen, Akuntansi dan Bisnis.
papers.abstract: This systematic literature review examines the impact of business operations management on organizational business performance in Indonesia during 2015-2025. From 37 peer-reviewed articles analyzed using qualitative and quantitative approaches, research findings demonstrate that business operations management, particularly supply chain management, quality management, and digital transformation, significantly influence organizational performance in Indonesia across operational, financial, and strategic dimensions. The study identifies competitive advantage, organizational innovation, and supply chain integration as strong mediating variables in the relationship between operations management practices and organizational performance. Additionally, the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies such as IoT, artificial intelligence, and big data analytics shows substantial positive impacts on operational efficiency. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the mechanisms through which business operations management enhances organizational performance in the Indonesian and ASEAN context. Practical implications include recommendations for managers and policymakers to integrate sustainable operations management practices with digital technology investments to achieve long-term competitive advantage.

papers.title: Passive ankle exoskeleton assistance selectively modulates triceps surae neural control during balance
papers.journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
papers.abstract: Wearable assistive devices have potential to improve human balance, but their effectiveness remains limited by an incomplete understanding of how mechanical assistance influences neuromuscular control. This study aimed to determine the neural adaptations in the control of lower leg muscles in response to passive ankle exoskeleton assistance during standing balance tasks with varying levels of difficulty. Lower limb kinematics and kinetics were recorded to assess changes in joint dynamics and balance performance. Neural drive to the muscles was assessed by decomposing high-density electromyography signals into motor unit spike trains. Ankle exoskeleton assistance, provided by a simple spring-loaded passive device, did not alter or improve balance performance and had minimal effects on lower limb kinematics. However, exoskeleton assistance affected triceps surae neural control, but only in the soleus, by reducing neural drive, while the gastrocnemii showed no detectable changes in neural control. Together, these results demonstrate that passive exoskeleton assistance alters neural control of the triceps surae in a muscle-specific manner during balance. Understanding muscle-specific adaptations can support more effective exoskeleton design and the development of their control strategies informed by myoelectrical signals.
papers.summary: Wearable assistive devices have potential to improve human balance, but their effectiveness remains limited by an incomplete understanding of how mechanical assistance influences neuromuscular control. Together, these results demonstrate that passive exoskeleton assistance alters neural control of the triceps surae in a muscle-specific manner during balance. Understanding muscle-specific adaptations can support more effective exoskeleton design and the development of their control strategies informed by myoelectrical signals.

papers.title: Biomechanical analyses point to dense collagen fibre architecture in an Ediacaran frond
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
papers.abstract: Ediacaran macrofossils record the earliest large and complex organisms on Earth. Despite extensive study, fundamental aspects of their internal anatomy and tissue composition remain poorly known, limiting understanding of how these organisms were constructed and functioned, as well as how their complex anatomies evolved. Here, we establish a new quantitative biomechanical framework to infer tissue properties in the Ediacaran frond Charniodiscus. Analyses of fossil morphology, numerical simulations and dimensional analysis indicate that the commonly preserved twisted forms reflect three-dimensional torsional deformation driven by turbidity flow-induced instability. By mapping deformation modes in dimensionless phase space, we calculate a Young's modulus consistent with densely aligned collagen fibres, under a eumetazoan framework. These results point to the presence of a load-bearing stem and substantial functional specialization. The inferred mechanical properties are largely incompatible with non-animal, sponge or placozoan tissues, and independently strengthen the proposal that Charniodiscus was a total-group eumetazoan. The presence of these tissues marked a foundational evolutionary step, providing the scaffolding for increased size, complexity and innovation in early animals.

papers.title: The Role of BaCO3 on Ni-BaZrO3 Catalysts for Efficient NH3 Decomposition
papers.abstract: Abstract Barium zirconate (BaZrO3) is a versatile material that has recently gained attention as a catalyst support for ammonia decomposition. In this study, an innovative synthesis strategy for BaZrO3 is combined with a solvent-free dry-milling method to deposit nickel onto its surface. The resulting Ni-BaZrO3 catalyst exhibited superior performance in ammonia decomposition for COx-free hydrogen production, outperforming both traditionally synthesized BaZrO3-based systems and more conventional Ni-supported catalysts. Comprehensive material characterization─using XRD, N2 adsorption–desorption, ATR, and Raman spectroscopy─confirmed that the new synthesis route improves the structural and chemical properties of the perovskite compared to conventional methods. H2-TPR and CO2-TPD analyses revealed that exploiting superficial BaCO3 reduction to BaO enhanced surface defectivity, and a high density of basic sites interacting with Ni nanoparticles can be obtained, facilitating electron exchange between the support and the metal. The mechanism of BaO formation and interaction with CO2 in TPD was deeply analyzed using in situ characterization techniques. Further mechanistic insights into product formation and release were obtained via TPSR and DRIFTS, emphasizing the critical role of metal-support interaction through the formation of Ni-BaO entities on the catalyst surface. Overall, this work demonstrates a sustainable and scalable route for producing high-performance Ni-BaZrO3 catalysts and advances the understanding of their reactivity, focusing on the importance of the metal-support interplay and reinforcing their potential in green hydrogen production through ammonia decomposition.

papers.title: Energy-saving hydrogen production coupled with PET-derived ethylene glycol oxidation: Reaction mechanisms, catalyst design, and reactor engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract The growing accumulation of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste and the increasing demand for clean hydrogen call for integrated electrochemical strategies. Ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), derived from PET hydrolysis, offers a thermodynamically favorable alternative to the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and can be coupled with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) to simultaneously produce value-added chemicals and H2. This review provides a system-level overview of EGORHER paired electrolysis, spanning reaction fundamentals, catalyst design, cell configuration, and future challenges. First, the competing EGOR pathways toward C1 products (such as formate/formic acid) and C2 products (such as glycolate/glycolic acid) are discussed. Key energetic descriptors, including cell voltage, overpotential, Faradaic efficiency, and energy efficiency, are then summarized to clarify the advantages of replacing OER with EGOR. Recent advances in catalysts, including precious metals, transition-metal compounds, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), organic catalysts, and hybrid systems, are reviewed with attention to their bifunctional or compatible activity for EGOR and HER. Reactor design is further discussed by comparing single-cell and dual-cell H-type reactors with membrane-free and membrane-separated flow-cell reactors, emphasizing their different roles in mass transport, product separation, and scale-up feasibility. Finally, remaining challenges and future directions are proposed, including C1/C2 selectivity, downstream separation, impurity tolerance, catalyst durability, and practical reactor optimization. This review aims to guide the development of efficient EGOR-assisted hydrogen production systems for sustainable PET electro-upcycling.

Finally, remaining challenges and future directions are proposed, including C1/C2 selectivity, downstream separation, impurity tolerance, catalyst durability, and practical reactor optimization. This review aims to guide the development of efficient EGOR-assisted hydrogen production systems for sustainable PET electro-upcycling.

papers.title: Microbiome-mediated resilience and cross-generational consequences in male Drosophila exposed to combined environmental stressors
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
papers.abstract: Climate change exposes organisms to multiple, interacting stressors, yet their joint effects on reproduction and inheritance remain poorly understood. This study investigated the interactive effects of acute heat stress and sublethal imidacloprid exposure on the reproductive success of male Drosophila melanogaster and the subsequent fitness of their offspring. We manipulated the gut microbiome of male flies (germ-free or colonized with one or five bacterial species) and subjected them to individual or combined stress. We show that combined stressors act synergistically to reduce male fitness traits, an effect that is partially buffered by higher microbiome diversity. Paternal stress exposure further reduced offspring fertility, demonstrating cross-generational fitness costs largely independent of microbial transmission. Our results underscore the gut microbiome as an important, but stress-sensitive, contributor to host resilience, and demonstrate how multi-stressor interactions can amplify reproductive failure, with broad implications for population persistence and biodiversity loss in a warming, chemically altered world.

papers.title: New use of mononuclear Mn/Co/Ni/Cu complexes of symmetric N2O2-type Schiff base as hydrogen-evolving catalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract Development of sustainable hydrogen production methods is crucial for the future hydrogen economy. Hence, designing cheap, stable and efficient catalysts for hydrogen generation is important. Here, we present the use of the family of eight Schiff base ligand-based transition metal complexes [MnIII(Salen)Cl] 1/[CoII(Salen)], 2/[NiII(Salen)], 3/[CuII(Salen)], 4/[MnIII(CH3Salen)Cl], 5/[CoII(CH3Salen)], 6/[NiII(CH3Salen)], 7/[CuII(CH3Salen)] and 8 (Salen/N,N′-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine/H2L1; CH3Salen/N,N′-bis(o-hydroxyacetophenone)ethylenediamine/H2L2) as hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts. Electrochemical studies for the complexes (in CH3CN) were carried out in the absence and presence of acids. Catalytic parameters of turnover frequency/overpotential were calculated for the electrocatalytic process. All complexes were found to be efficient HER catalysts in the presence of acids and Co/Ni/Cu complexes were more stable than the Mn complexes. The stability and efficiency order of the catalysts was 2, 4 > 6 > 7 > 3 > 8 (acetic acid); 1 > 5 (trifluoroacetic acid). Density functional theory studies provided detailed insight into the metal- versus ligand-centred redox transitions and the HER mechanism for all complexes. Successive events of electrochemical reduction (E) and protonation (C) along the HER paths were investigated, and thermodynamically feasible routes were assigned. This work provides insights into the effect of a series of earth-abundant transition metal complex structures, the performance of this series of metal centres on electrocatalysis, and the effect of pKa on reactivity. Hence, it will be of value to develop novel and promising catalysts for HER in the future.

papers.title: From General-Purpose Large Language Models to Domain-Specific Financial Models: A Structured Review and Comparative Case Analysis
papers.abstract: The use of large language models (LLMs) in finance has expanded rapidly, yet general-purpose systems face recurring problems in high-risk and regulated applications: Unsupported factual generation, weak reasoning across text, tables, charts, and numerical data, and limited traceability of model-assisted decisions. This study conducts a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta Analyses (PRISMA)-informed structured review of 67 studies, principally published between January 2020 and March 2026, with three foundational pre-2020 studies retained through backward citation tracking. It develops a qualitative analytical and diagnostic framework with three pathways: Specialized knowledge modeling, task-constrained multimodal reasoning, and Trust-by-Design. A study-level evidence map and an explicit coding protocol show how the pathways were derived. The framework is used to compare BloombergGPT, FinGPT, FinTral, Fin-o1, Fin-R1, and Agentar-Fin-R1 through common criteria for knowledge controls, modality handling, lifecycle governance, evidence quality, and deployment maturity. The case analysis distinguishes model-paper design descriptions, developer reported benchmark results, platform-level deployment reports, and prospective applications. The analysis indicates that financial LLMs differ materially in how they organize domain knowledge, coordinate heterogeneous inputs, and govern model use across the lifecycle. Agentar-Fin-R1 illustrates the framework; the case does not validate the framework or establish independently observed production performance. The paper provides a structured basis for assessing domain-specific financial LLMs and connects responsible model design with sustainable financial innovation through durable governance arrangements, controlled model and compliance risk, responsible scaling, financial inclusion, and institutional resilience. Received: 1 April 2026 | Revised: 2 September 2026 | Accepted: 20 September 2026 Conflicts of Interest The authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest to this work. Data Availability Statement Tables S1–S4 in the Supplementary Materials provide the prospective replication protocol, the study-level evidence map for the 67-study corpus, the code-to-pathway derivation and threshold rationale, and the register of seven sources outside the review corpus. The original query-level exports, source-specific yields, and coder-level screening logs were not retained. Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study. papers.title: Recent Advances in Vitamin B12 Oral Dispersible Film Formulations for Enhanced Patient Compliance
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is a highly debilitating metabolic microvascular complication frequently worsened by metformin-induced vitamin B12 malabsorption.To address this clinical challenge, this study presents the systematic design, mechanical optimization, and biopharmaceutical evaluation of a novel, taste-masked vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) oral dispersible film (ODF) formulated using a blended natural polymer matrix.To suppress the characteristic metallic taste of cyanocobalamin, the drug was microencapsulated into calcium alginate beads via external ionotropic gelation, utilizing sodium alginate and calcium chloride cross-linking.These beads were subsequently dispersed in an aqueous film-forming blend of pullulan, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), and guar gum, plasticized with glycerol, and fabricated using the solvent casting technique.Physicochemical characterization of the optimized film formulation (F3) revealed excellent visual elegance, an average weight of 48.8±0.4"mg" , and a uniform thickness of 0.183±0.003"mm" .Mechanical analysis demonstrated superior resilience, with a tensile strength of 4.0±0.1 〖" N/mm" 〗^2, a percentage elongation of 50.0±1.2%,and a folding endurance of 248±5 folds, preventing mechanical failure during handling.Surface pH was physiologically compatible at 6.9±0.1, mitigating the risk of papers.title: Analysis of pathogenesis-related factors of Streptococcus mutans from the oral cavity of patients with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis
papers.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) comprises non-alcoholic fatty liver (NAFL), which rarely progresses, and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), which may progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Previous studies have shown that Streptococcus mutans positive for collagen-binding protein (Cnm) and the 190-kDa cell surface protein antigen (PA) may be involved in NASH progression. In this study, we analyzed saliva samples obtained from patients with NAFL and NASH, and investigated the involvement of these proteins in NASH development by administrating clinical isolates to a mouse model. There was no significant difference in the detection rate of S. mutans between the NAFL and NASH patient groups; however, Cnm + /PA + S. mutans strains were more frequently detected in patients with NASH. Furthermore, patients with NASH with Cnm + /PA + S. mutans showed significantly higher levels of type IV collagen 7S, a biomarker of liver fibrosis, compared to patients with NASH without these strains. Adiponectin, an anti-inflammatory cytokine mainly secreted by adipocytes, was significantly lower. The collagen-binding ability of Cnm + /PA + S. mutans strains was significantly higher than that of other S. mutans strains without both proteins. Cnm + /PA + S. mutans showed significantly higher binding ability to type IV collagen than to type I collagen. RT-qPCR analysis revealed that pac expression was significantly higher in Cnm + /PA + S. mutans isolated from the NASH group. Administration of Cnm + /PA + S. mutans into a NASH mouse model via the jugular vein caused NASH-like pathology in mouse liver tissues. These results suggest that Cnm + /PA + S. mutans is associated with NASH aggravation.

papers.title: Functionalization of Metal-Enriched Pleurotus Biomass with γ-Poly-Glutamic Acid for Cytoprotective and Antimicrobial Wound Care
papers.abstract: Objectives: Chronic wound dressings require active components that support moisture management, biocompatibility, and local bioburden control. Therefore, in this study, freeze-dried biomass of Pleurotus ostreatus (Po) and Pleurotus djamor (Pdj) was cultivated in vitro under mineral-enriched conditions (calcium, magnesium, zinc) and subsequently modified with poly(γ-glutamic acid) (γ-PGA) to develop a bioactive fungal matrix intended as a functional additive for future wound-care biomaterials. Methods: The elemental content of the biomass was determined using atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS), and the resulting biomaterial underwent physicochemical analyses—including scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), wettability measurements, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and thermogravimetric analysis (TG)—as well as biological performance assessments using a disk diffusion assay and cytotoxicity analysis. Results: Mineral enrichment enhanced Pleurotus spp. biomass production and metal accumulation, while γ-PGA coating altered surface properties and cytocompatibility. Zinc supplementation significantly promoted biomass formation in both Pleurotus species, while metal accumulation depended on the specific element and fortification regime. γ-PGA modification reduced the accessible BET surface area and formed a denser polymer-associated layer, confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. While the unmodified Po biomass exhibited the strongest in vitro antibacterial activity against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, it also displayed dose-dependent cytotoxicity toward HaCaT keratinocytes at high concentrations. The addition of γ-PGA moderately reduced the in vitro bacterial inhibition zones but provided a critical cytoprotective effect, mitigating the cytotoxicity of the concentrated fungal extracts and rescuing HaCaT-cell viability to meet ISO 10993-5 safety thresholds. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that γ-PGA-modified, metal-enriched Pleurotus biomass exhibits a distinct in vitro trade-off between absolute antimicrobial potency and cellular safety, supporting its further investigation as a biocompatible ingredient for multifunctional wound-dressing systems.

papers.title: Composition‐Dependent Mechanical, Thermal, and Surface Properties of Stereolithography‐Printed TPU / PMMA Photopolymer Blends
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocurable thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) blends were formulated for stereolithography (SLA) to examine how blend composition affects intermolecular interactions, phase morphology, thermal behavior, mechanical response, and surface wettability of photocured networks. TPU‐based photocurable resin, PMMA‐based photocurable resin, and four intermediate blends (TPU: PMMA = 9:1, 7:3, 1:1, and 3:7, w/w) were printed under a single optimized, fully dense (100% infill) parameter set. FTIR spectroscopy confirmed that all compositions remained physically blended, with carbonyl‐ and amide‐band positions consistent with composition‐dependent urethane–carbonyl hydrogen bonding. FE‐SEM surface‐morphology imaging of the as‐printed surfaces showed a shift from fibrous, textured features in TPU‐rich compositions to denser, smoother features as PMMA content increased. Differential scanning calorimetry of the two most contrasting compositions (7:3 and 1:1) showed a sharp sub‐ambient thermal event, tentatively attributed to a melting‐type transition of ordered TPU soft‐segment domains rather than a glass transition, shifting from −14°C (7:3) to −11°C (1:1) with increasing PMMA content; this assignment remains provisional given the proximity to the lower instrumental limit and the two‐composition dataset. Thermogravimetric analysis across all six compositions showed that thermal stability generally increased with PMMA content, with the 3:7 blend showing the highest onset decomposition temperature and char yield. Static contact angle and swelling measurements identified the 7:3 composition as the most hydrophilic (37.4°) and most swollen (2.37% at 18 h) in the series. Tensile testing showed PMMA‐based photocurable resin to be the strongest and stiffest composition (30.5 MPa, 17.2 MPa modulus) and TPU‐based photocurable resin the most extensible (96.5% elongation), while the 3:7 blend offered the best overall strength–stiffness–ductility balance among the blended compositions (14.2 MPa, 12.2 MPa modulus, 70.3% elongation); the 7:3 and 1:1 compositions are lower‐modulus, elastomer‐dominated formulations rather than high‐performance structural materials. Collectively, these results provide composition‐dependent structural observations for photocurable TPU/PMMA blends and illustrate compositional control as an accessible route for tuning the mechanical, thermal, and surface behavior of SLA‐printed polymer networks.

papers.title: Mechanical and Thermomechanical Performance Evaluation of CFRP Sandwich Structures with Additively Manufactured Composite Cores
papers.abstract: This study experimentally evaluates how various 3D-printed gyroid core materials influence the mechanical and thermo-mechanical performance of lightweight carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) sandwich structures. Three gyroid core configurations were considered: short-carbon-fiber-reinforced polyphthalamide (PPA-CF), continuous-carbon-fiber-reinforced nylon (ONYX-R), and nylon short-carbon-fiber-reinforced (ONYX), all combined with similar 0/90° carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer composite (CFRP) face sheets. The sandwich specimens were manufactured using a one-step co-curing process and characterized by flatwise compression, three-point bending, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). The PPA-CF-CFRP sandwich configuration exhibited the highest flexural performance, with a maximum flexural stress of 148–156 MPa, approximately 39% higher than that of ONYX-R-CFRP, and the highest mean compression modulus of approximately 87 MPa. However, ONYX-R-CFRP achieved the highest mean compressive strength of 12.84 MPa, compared with 11.85 MPa for PPA-CF-CFRP. These findings indicate that the mechanical response depends on the loading mode and is influenced by the combined effects of the thermoplastic matrix, carbon-fiber reinforcement architecture, and the resulting structural characteristics of the printed gyroid cores. DMA revealed that the PPA-CF-CFRP sandwich achieved a storage modulus of ~9 GPa at 30 °C, outperforming the ONYX-R-CFRP configuration by approximately 70%. Conversely, ONYX-R-CFRP exhibited the highest damping capacity, with a maximum tan δ of approximately 0.16, about 60% higher than the PPA-CF-CFRP configuration. The ONYX-CFRP sandwich configuration displayed the lowest mechanical and thermo-mechanical performance, demonstrating that the stiffness, deformation capacity, damping response, and temperature-dependent mechanical behavior of these sandwich structures can be tailored through the selection of the additively manufactured core configuration.

papers.title: Highly Efficient Non‐Doped Blue Electro‐Fluorescence With Fast Carrier Mobilities: Hybrid Local and Charge‐Transfer (HLCT) Excited State and Regularly Stacked Aggregate
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐doped organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) offer simpler fabrication and lower manufacturing costs than traditional doped OLEDs, attracting increasing attention in both scientific research and industrial applications. However, aggregation‐caused quenching (ACQ) and unbalanced carrier transport remain major bottlenecks to achieving efficient non‐doped OLEDs, especially the primary‐blue fluorescent OLEDs. Herein, we report three novel blue or deep‐blue emitters with excellent non‐doped OLED performance of near 15% external quantum efficiency (EQE), which can be assigned to the synergistic contributions of intramolecular hybrid local and charge‐transfer (HLCT) excited state character and intermolecular aggregation pattern. The incorporation of a fluorene π‐bridge in the three molecules not only contributes to the high photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), high blue color purity and satisfactory exciton utilization efficiency (EUE), but also to the regulated π‐stacking that gives rise to both light outcoupling efficiency, with horizontal dipole orientation factor (Θ // ) exceeding 90%, and boosted carrier mobilities (at 5.0 × 10 5 V·m −1 , hole: ∼ 2.76 × 10 −5 cm 2 ·V −1 ·s −1 ; electron: ∼ 2.51 × 10 −4 cm 2 ·V −1 ·s −1 ) in non‐doped OLEDs.

papers.title: Development of novel dental composites integrated with MSN–TQ systems
papers.abstract: Thymoquinone (TQ), recognized for its potent antibacterial capabilities, is a promising compound for both preventive and therapeutic applications in various diseases. In this study, TQ molecules were successfully loaded onto biocompatible, easily synthesized, and cost-effective MSN, creating the MSN–TQ system, which was subsequently incorporated into the synthesis of a novel series of dental composites. The chemical characterization of both the MSN–TQ system and the resulting S series dental composites was carried out using FTIR, SEM, XRD, TGA, and DSC. The antibacterial activity of MSN–TQ nanoparticles were assessed by MIC and MBC assays against E. coli , S. aureus , E. faecalis , and P. aeruginosa . MSN–TQ showed selective efficacy against E. faecalis (MIC/MBC: 7.5–10 μg/mL); no activity against E. coli , S. aureus , or P. aeruginosa within 2.5–20 μg/mL. Compared to resin without MSN-TQ, the surface bacterial metabolic activity was found to be lowest in S4 composite (49.28%) among S series dental composites. The S4 dental composite exhibited the maximum water solubility value (5,72*10 -3 mg/mm 3 ), whereas the S0 control composite (lowest filler content) demonstrated the highest water sorption value (73,04*10 -2 mg/mm 3 ). Furthermore, following exposure to the Fenton chemical challenge, the maximum material loss due to degradation was recorded in the S3 composite, reaching 0.020%. These findings position MSN-TQ composites as a scientifically promising direction requiring further work: cytotoxicity (ISO 10993-5), aging, wear, fatigue, and bond strength studies are needed before any clinical consideration. • MSN–TQ synthesized and incorporated into dental composites • Selective antibacterial effect vs E. faecalis (7.5–10 μg/mL) • S4 composite showed lowest surface bacterial metabolic activity • S3 achieved highest compressive strength (184.64 MPa)

papers.title: Morphology evolution and compaction behavior of gangue particles under abrasion: an experimental study
papers.abstract: Backfill mining is widely used to control strata movement and mitigate rockburst hazards in deep coal mines, and its effectiveness strongly depends on the compaction behavior of the backfill material. However, how abrasion that gangue particles experience during transport modifies their morphology and, in turn, governs their subsequent compaction response has received little systematic attention. In this study, gangue particles sized 10–30 mm were subjected to Los Angeles abrasion tests at 5 revolution levels (0, 250, 500, 750, and 1,000 r). Three-dimensional scanning was used to extract morphological parameters - flatness and sphericity - followed by confined compression tests to evaluate compaction performance. The results suggest that the abrasion loss increases approximately linearly with revolution count. After 1,000 r, the mass proportion of 25–30 mm particles was only 12.5%, while particles smaller than 1.7 mm accounted for 29.9% of the total mass. This redistribution of particle sizes increased the initial tapped density from 1.370 to 1.769 g/cm 3 . Morphologically, abrasion continuously reshaped the particles, rendering them smoother and more equiaxial. Flatness generally decreased with increasing revolutions, with the 15–20 mm range exhibiting the largest drop (0.23). Meanwhile, sphericity increased from a range of 0.796–0.813 to 0.843–0.871. Compaction performance also improved markedly: the secant modulus for the main loading stage (2–16 MPa) increased from 80.77 to 156.40 MPa, with a pronounced surge occurring between 500 and 750 r. The final axial strain decreased from 0.206 to 0.106 - a reduction of 48.5%. The abrasion process can be divided into three stages: mild modification (0–250 r), rapid improvement (250–750 r), and stabilization (750–1,000 r). The strong correlation between abrasion loss and final axial strain further suggests that sieve-based abrasion measurements may provide a rapid proxy for evaluating the compaction state of gangue backfill, offering a quick assessment tool for field applications.

papers.title: Enhanced Bread Shelf Life Using Carboxymethyl Cellulose Composite Films with Combined Antibacterial Activity of Zinc Oxide and Cinnamon Essential Oil
papers.abstract: Cellulose is the most abundant natural polymer and is widely used in the packaging industry. One of the primary functions of food packaging is to protect food products from spoilage and extend their shelf life. Although cellulose lacks inherent antimicrobial activity, this limitation can be addressed through appropriate chemical or physical modifications to impart antimicrobial properties to cellulose-based materials. Nevertheless, cellulose represents a suitable matrix for the incorporation of various antimicrobial agents, enabling the development of active packaging materials. Moreover, the combination of multiple antimicrobial agents may result in combined effects, potentially providing broader and enhanced antimicrobial activity while reducing the overall amount of antimicrobial agents required. Herein, we report the preparation of a highly potent antimicrobial composite based on carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles (NPs) loaded with cinnamon essential oil (CEO). The composites were characterized using FTIR, UV–Vis, and fluorescence spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermal analysis. Their mechanical and antibacterial properties, as well as potential biodegradability, were evaluated. The resulting films exhibited good barrier properties and enhanced mechanical performance. Although the composite films are composed of a food additive, spice extract, and ZnO NPs, all of which are generally recognized as safe (GRAS), the resulting innovative packaging exhibited strong antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, with inhibition zones reaching up to 38 mm. Moreover, no viable colonies of planktonic bacterial cells were detected after 4 h of incubation. In preliminary tests, no visible mold growth was observed on bread slices packaged in these films after 28 days of storage, whereas the control samples showed visible spoilage as early as day 7.

papers.title: Advances in artificial intelligence for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis of neurological diseases: a systematic literature review
papers.abstract: Background Brain imaging is central to the structural, functional, metabolic, and neurophysiological characterization of neurological disease, yet interpretation remains constrained by heterogeneity in acquisition, annotation, expertise, and clinical context. Objective This systematic literature review evaluates recent artificial intelligence approaches for brain imaging and computer-aided diagnosis, with emphasis on methods, modalities, neurological diseases, diagnostic tasks, datasets, validation practices, and translational limitations. Methods The review followed PRISMA 2020 and covered peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2020 through June 2026. Eight information sources were searched using database-specific terms for artificial intelligence, neuroimaging, neurological disease, and diagnostic analysis. The search identified 1,078 records; 236 duplicates were removed, 842 unique records were screened, 258 full texts were assessed, and 123 studies were included after a record-level eligibility re-audit. Heterogeneous evidence was synthesized narratively and by descriptive mapping rather than meta-analysis. Results MRI was frequently represented in the included studies and auxiliary mapping data; CT was commonly used in acute stroke and intracranial hemorrhage; PET supported selected molecular and differential-diagnosis studies; fMRI and diffusion imaging were used for network and white-matter analysis; and EEG extended the scope to neurophysiological diagnosis. CNN and three-dimensional networks were commonly reported, while attention, Transformer, graph, self-supervised, generative, multimodal, and foundation-model approaches appeared in selected recent studies. Stroke, dementia, and brain tumors were frequently represented, but heterogeneous populations, outcomes, and incomplete validation extraction precluded ranking diseases, modalities, architectures, or validation strategies. Conclusion The evidence suggests movement from task-specific pattern recognition toward multimodal and context-rich decision support in selected settings, but it does not establish uniform methodological superiority or clinical maturity. Dependable translation requires patient-level data governance, transparent reporting, uncertainty estimation, independent multicenter testing, prospective workflow evaluation, and clinically meaningful endpoints.

papers.title: Thermochemical conversion of water hyacinth biomass into biochar and value-added products: mechanical design and experimental validation
papers.abstract: Abstract The uncontrolled proliferation of water hyacinth in freshwater ecosystems represents a persistent environmental and energy-related challenge. While numerous biomass utilization strategies have been reported, the development of validated thermochemical conversion systems capable of transforming this invasive resource into stable value-added products remains limited. This study introduces mechanical design, numerical validation, and experimental assessment of a thermochemical conversion system for transforming water hyacinth into biochar and bioactive liquid fractions. An additional lab-scale pyrolysis experiment was performed to evaluate the functionality of value-added products (biochar and pyroligneous acid) generated through the thermochemical conversion process. The proposed system consists of a compact horizontal pyrolysis reactor equipped with an internal auger mechanism, external heating system, thermal insulation, and vapor condensation unit. Critical structural and thermal components were numerically validated using finite element analysis (FEA) to ensure mechanical integrity and safe operation under elevated temperature conditions. Results of FEA confirmed the adequate structural integrity, thermal stability, and operational safety under pyrolysis conditions. FEA analysis further confirmed the remaining of bending and thermal stress below the yield strength of stainless steel 304. The proposed thermal insulation exhibited high efficiency toward minimizing heat losses, maintaining safe external temperatures, and keeping thermal stress within material capacity. Engineered biochar produced at 400, 500, and 600°C was comprehensively characterized using spectroscopic (SEM, AFM, EDS, XRD, DSC, and FTIR), physical (specific surface area, pore volume, pore radius, and zeta potential), and chemical (ICP, pH, and EC) analyses. Characterization results confirmed the high functionality of biochar, including porous structure, high surface area, and abundance of active functional groups. Results also showed that increasing pyrolysis temperature was associated with enhancement of porosity, aromatization, and crystallinity. GC–MS and ICP analysis of pyroligneous acid showed also abundance of several compounds previously associated with antimicrobial, antioxidant, and plant-defense-related activities, alongside with considerable macro and micronutrients. Findings from this study, therefore, provide a validated engineering and experimental framework for invasive biomass valorization, contributing to circular bioenergy strategies and sustainable agriculture management.

Results of FEA confirmed the adequate structural integrity, thermal stability, and operational safety under pyrolysis conditions. Results also showed that increasing pyrolysis temperature was associated with enhancement of porosity, aromatization, and crystallinity.

papers.title: Renal injury phenotypes with ICI–VEGFR-TKI combinations in renal cell carcinoma: active-comparator analyses in FAERS and JADER
papers.abstract: Background Renal adverse-event reports during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)–VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy may combine immune-interstitial, proteinuric, and nonspecific acute kidney injury (AKI) features. We compared their reporting patterns with those of nivolumab plus ipilimumab in renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Methods We analyzed FAERS/AERS (2004Q1–2026Q2) and the JADER 202607 release (through 2026Q1), applying latest-version handling, strict indication–drug linkage, author-defined Tier-A reporting labels, regimen-specific common support, and year-stratified Mantel–Haenszel reporting odds ratios (MH-RORs). JADER supplied cross-database directional corroboration. Secondary classification of the rule-derived labels used non-anchor features, with and without regimen indicators, and included temporal evaluation in 2024–2025. Additional analyses assessed sparse cells, terminal periods, standard renal queries, and model ablations. Results Among 84,369 strict-RCC FAERS reports, 2,307 met Tier-A definitions: 219 immune-interstitial, 1,076 VEGF-axis, 932 nonspecific AKI, and 80 mixed. For pembrolizumab plus axitinib, pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib, and nivolumab plus cabozantinib, VEGF-axis MH-RORs were 5.31 (95% CI 2.43–11.59), 19.48 (9.03–42.01), and 4.59 (2.07–10.19). Proteinuria dominated this signal. Exclusive Tier-A AKI estimates were 1.05, 0.93, and 0.78, with intervals crossing one; this finding was definition-dependent, as a separate narrow acute-renal-failure query yielded 1.56 (1.20–2.02) for pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib. Excluding 2026 retained the primary VEGF-axis direction. JADER estimates were 6.28, 19.27, and 6.16. In a secondary consistency analysis, adding regimen increased temporal macro-AUPRC from 0.606 to 0.638, but immune-interstitial class average precision remained 0.253. Conclusions The reproducible finding is a proteinuria-dominant VEGF-axis reporting pattern, not a validated renal mechanism or comparative incidence estimate. Differential surveillance, sparse comparator events, phenotype misclassification, and shared reporting ecology constrain interpretation. The classifier describes internal label consistency and has no established diagnostic use.

papers.title: Product Development from Waste Polymer Packages Through Pyrolysis
papers.journal: International Journal of Chemical Engineering Research
papers.abstract: Pyrolysis of waste plastics is a novel method for effective waste management. Waste polyethylene, polypropylene, and their mixture were pyrolyzed in a tubular batch reactor at about 300-350 °C in the presence and absence of a catalyst. Polyethylene and polypropylene were chosen because they are the most abundant waste polymers. The polymers decomposed into a gas, a liquid, and a solid. The liquid product was further distilled to obtain fractions with properties and compositions similar to those of gasoline and diesel. Innumerable reactions occur during the pyrolysis of plastics, with distinct kinetic parameters. Various tests, including density, aniline point, flash and fire points, and GC-MS analysis, were performed to characterize them.

papers.title: Digital marketing and social network effects in new energy vehicle diffusion: evolutionary dynamics in a dual-layer heterogeneous network
papers.abstract: In the context of the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality strategy and the booming digital economy, the diffusion of new energy vehicles (NEVs) has become an important pathway for industrial green transformation. This study develops a dual-layer heterogeneous network evolutionary game model that integrates supply-side firms and demand-side consumers. Based on this model, we examine the effects of multiple government policies, digital marketing mechanisms, social network effects, underlying physical constraints, and network structure, as well as selected interactions among these mechanisms, on NEV diffusion. The findings reveal several critical insights. First, NEV diffusion exhibits a pronounced bimodal steady-state pattern and strong dependence on initial adoption conditions. It shows an S-shaped relationship with the initial consumer adoption base. Second, government policy transmission is asymmetric across the dual-layer network. Under standardized proportional policy changes, consumer purchase subsidies have a stronger effect on diffusion than technology transition subsidies and carbon prices. Third, digital marketing and social network effects are conditional on the prevailing market structure. When internal combustion engine vehicles initially hold an advantage, stronger marketing utility conversion, local bandwagon effects, and hub node influence can reinforce the incumbent position, whereas information overload weakens this exposure advantage. Fourth, charging anxiety and perceived technological risk constrain sustained NEV diffusion, while purchase subsidies can only partly compensate for severe charging constraints. Selected joint analyses and network robustness tests further show that diffusion outcomes depend on interactions among policy, behavioral, and physical mechanisms, while consumer-network connectivity and topology affect quantitative diffusion outcomes without overturning the main directional relationships. These findings highlight the importance of initial market conditions, cross-layer feedback, and network structure in shaping NEV diffusion and provide implications for policy design and firm strategy.

papers.title: Transition‐Specific Associations of Cardiometabolic Biomarker Burden With Cardio‐Renal‐Metabolic Multimorbidity Progression: A Multistate Cohort Study
papers.abstract: AIMS: To identify representative cardiometabolic biomarkers and examine how individual biomarkers and combined biomarker burden are associated with transition-specific progression of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM). METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 262 464 UK Biobank participants free of cardiovascular disease (CVD), type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) at baseline. Forty-nine candidate biomarkers across five domains, including inflammation, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, adiposity and blood pressure, were evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve and concordance index to select representative markers. Multistate models estimated associations of individual biomarkers, elevated-marker count and a weighted 5-Item Cardiometabolic Risk Score (5-CMRS) with sequential transitions from baseline to first cardio-renal-metabolic disease (FCRMD), FCRMD to Double CRMD and Double to Triple CRMD. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.62 years, 44 339 participants developed FCRMD, 7218 progressed to Double CRMD and 721 progressed to Triple CRMD. Five representative biomarkers were selected: C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio, metabolic score for insulin resistance (METS-IR), triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio, waist-to-height ratio and systolic blood pressure. Higher elevated-marker count showed graded associations across all transitions. Compared with the lowest 5-CMRS category, the highest category was associated with hazard ratios of 2.80, 1.84 and 1.71 for the three sequential transitions. Disease-specific analyses showed the strongest associations with incident T2D. METS-IR showed the largest relative contributions across all transitions, whereas additive interactions were mainly observed during early CRMM progression. CONCLUSION: Combined cardiometabolic biomarker burden was associated with graded, transition-specific risks across CRMM progression, supporting integrated cardiometabolic risk assessment across inflammatory, metabolic, adiposity, lipid and blood-pressure domains.

papers.title: Polymer-modified MXene thin-film nanocomposite membranes for forward osmosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Water scarcity demands novel solutions to address the challenges posed by increasing societal needs. This study presents a novel strategy for fabricating MXene-based thin-film nanocomposite forward osmosis (TFN-FO) membranes with enhanced permeability and selectivity, offering a promising advancement in water treatment technologies. The approach involves synthesizing MXene-functionalized polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-g-MXene) additives through a facile chemical grafting method, where hydroxyl groups serve as linkers to covalently bond PVP onto the surface of 2D MXene nanosheets. Subsequently, PVP-g-MXene is incorporated into a polyamide (PA) thin film via interfacial polymerization (IP) to produce the innovative TFN-FO membranes. Characterization of MXene and PVP-g-MXene was performed using FT-IR, XRD, TGA, and FE-SEM. The fabricated membranes were analyzed for surface morphology, roughness, and hydrophilicity using FESEM, AFM, and water contact angle (WCA) measurements. The results indicate that incorporating PVP-g-MXene significantly alters the physicochemical properties of the membranes, including morphology, roughness, hydrophilicity, and overall performance during the IP process. All modified membranes demonstrated improved water flux compared to the pristine TFC membrane, with TFN-PgM1 and TFN-PgM2 exhibiting superior selectivity. Notably the representative TFN-PgM2 membrane exhibited a water flux of 18.5 LMH, which is approximately 72% higher than that of the TFC membrane, and demonstrated a Js/Jw ratio of 0.167, indicating an 18.1% improvement in selectivity performance. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of polymer-modified MXene for the development of high-performance FO membranes.

papers.title: Three-dimensional evaluation and optimization of breast cancer rehabilitation science popularization videos on mainstream video platforms: a cross-sectional study in Mainland China
papers.abstract: Background With the growing number of breast cancer survivors, rehabilitation has become a critical component of comprehensive cancer care. Mainstream video platforms have emerged as a primary channel for patients to access rehabilitation information, yet the quality of such content remains unevaluated. This study aimed to systematically assess the quality and dissemination characteristics of breast cancer rehabilitation-related videos on TikTok, MicroBlog, and Today’s Headline. Method A cross-sectional design was employed. From June to July 2026, videos related to breast cancer rehabilitation were retrieved on three platforms using an account-free search mode. 450 valid samples (150 per platform) were selected and a three-dimensional evaluation system was established: content scientificity (modified DISCERN scale), dissemination presentation (Global Quality Scale), and source credibility (JAMA scale). Overall quality was the arithmetic mean of the three dimensions. Six evaluators conducted scoring; inter-rater reliability was tested by ICC(2,k). Post hoc power analysis confirmed sufficient power (>0.99) for detecting medium-effect differences. Result The overall quality score was 2.74 ± 0.85, with a pass rate (≥3.5) of only 19.8%; a sensitivity analysis using alternative cutoffs (≥3.0 and ≥4.0) yielded pass rates of 42.4% and 6.7%, respectively, confirming the robustness of the low-quality conclusion. TikTok's overall quality, content scientificity, and source credibility scores were significantly higher than MicroBlog and Today's Headlines (all P < 0.05, η 2 = 0.11–0.16), a difference partly attributable to TikTok's higher proportion of certified physicians. One-way ANOVA revealed significant overall differences among four creator types (F = 128.6, P < 0.001, η 2 = 0.46), with Tukey post hoc tests confirming certified physicians > rehabilitation nurses > health institutions > ordinary users. Subgroup analysis showed that sexual/reproductive rehabilitation videos had the lowest quality (2.45 ± 0.91). A weak negative association was observed between the engagement composite and quality (r = −0.18, 95% CI: −0.27 to −0.09, P < 0.001). Conclusion The overall quality of breast cancer rehabilitation popular science videos on Chinese mainstream platforms was low. Patients should prioritize content from certified physicians and health institutions that cite guidelines and present balanced information. Platform-specific regulation and greater participation by certified oncologists and rehabilitation specialists are urgently needed. Level of evidence Level II; Cross-Sectional Study

papers.title: Engineering-oriented formulation design and synergistic viscosity-enhancing mechanism of a composite modifier for high-viscosity asphalt binder
papers.abstract: High-viscosity modified asphalt (HVMA) binder is commonly used in porous asphalt pavements and ultra-thin overlays to resist rutting, raveling, and moisture-induced interface failure. However, the design of high-viscosity modifier (HVM) is still largely empirical, and the synergistic effects of composite modifier system have not been fully clarified. In this study, a prefabricated composite modifier was developed using star-shaped/linear SBS, C9 petroleum resin, and furfural extract oil (FEO). The formulation was selected based on viscosity, rutting factor, elastic recovery, ductility, and BBS pull-off strength. FTIR, DSC, and GPC were used to reveal the viscosity-enhancing mechanism. The results showed that the preferred modifier contained at least 75% star-shaped SBS, with an SBS/C9 petroleum resin mass ratio of 2:1 and a FEO content of 20 wt%. The recommended asphalt binder showed improved high-temperature rheological performance, its rutting factor was about 1.9 times that of conventional SBS-modified asphalt binder. After 72 h of water immersion, all HVA-modified asphalt binders retained relatively high BBS strength, indicating improved resistance to moisture-induced damage. The physicochemical property results indicated that the enhanced performance was not a simple result of increasing modifier content. Instead, it originated from a balanced polymer-resin-oil synergy: star-shaped SBS formed the elastic skeleton, C9 petroleum resin strengthened tackifying and interfacial interactions, and FEO promoted SBS swelling and dispersion. The recommended system achieved higher molecular weight with a narrower molecular-weight distribution, suggesting a more coordinated multicomponent structure. These structural features contributed to the improved viscoelastic response, high-temperature stability, and interfacial durability of the HVMA binder. The prepared composite modifier provides a mechanism-guided approach for improving HVMA performance and helps to promote its broader application in porous asphalt pavements and ultra-thin overlays.
papers.summary: The recommended asphalt binder showed improved high-temperature rheological performance, its rutting factor was about 1.9 times that of conventional SBS-modified asphalt binder. The physicochemical property results indicated that the enhanced performance was not a simple result of increasing modifier content. The prepared composite modifier provides a mechanism-guided approach for improving HVMA performance and helps to promote its broader application in porous asphalt pavements and ultra-thin overlays.

papers.title: Long-term quality of life, rehospitalization risks, and economic viability of remote cardiac rehabilitation: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Background Although remote cardiac rehabilitation (RCR) is a promising alternative to traditional center-based care, evidence regarding its exact impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL), cardiovascular safety, and economic viability remains fragmented, necessitating a comprehensive synthesis to guide clinical implementation. Objectives This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to evaluate the HRQoL, cardiovascular safety, and economic viability of RCR versus standard center-based care in cardiovascular disease, with subgroup analyses based on follow-up duration and high-risk patient cohorts. Methods Literature searches were conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, supplemented by manual screening of relevant references to identify clinical studies on RCR up to July 2026. Two independent review teams performed data extraction and risk of bias assessment using the RevMan software. Meta-analyses were conducted employing random-effects models to calculate pooled effect sizes with corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I 2 statistic, and potential publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. To evaluate the robustness of the pooled results and explore potential heterogeneity, subgroup and fixed-effects sensitivity analyses were conducted, supplemented by trial sequential analysis (TSA). Results A total of 45 randomized controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis. RCR significantly improved HRQoL across multiple scales (MacNew: MD = 0.17; MLHFQ: MD = −5.38; P < 0.05), while maintaining SF-36 and HADS outcomes comparable to standard care. Exploratory analyses indicated statistically significant improvements in mental health at 6 months (MD = 1.73, P = 0.03) and physical functioning at 12 months (MD = 1.48, P = 0.0002). Regarding cardiovascular safety, RCR was not associated with a statistically significant increase in the risk of MACEs, all-cause mortality, or adverse events ( P > 0.05) compared to conventional care. RCR significantly reduced the risk of cardiac rehospitalization (RR = 0.70, P = 0.01), with exploratory stratified analyses indicating that this favorable association was evident in the hardware-integrated interventions subgroup (RR = 0.59, P = 0.02) and 6-month observation subgroup (RR = 0.38, P < 0.00001), alongside a non-significant numerical protective trend among high-risk patients (RR: 0.59 vs. 0.74, P = 0.15). The economic viability of RCR remains uncertain, critically depending on initial setup outlays, patient scaling, and subsequent healthcare utilization. Conclusions RCR may serve as an effective and safe alternative to conventional care that improves physical and psychological well-being, was associated with a lower risk of cardiac rehospitalization, and may provide economic value in certain healthcare systems. Systematic Review Registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261374977 , PROSPERO CRD420261374977.

Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochrane Q test and I 2 statistic, and potential publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. To evaluate the robustness of the pooled results and explore potential heterogeneity, subgroup and fixed-effects sensitivity analyses were conducted, supplemented by trial sequential analysis (TSA).

papers.title: Electrospun Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 nanofibers as ion-conducting fillers for polyethylene oxide/poly(vinylidene fluoride) composite solid electrolytes
papers.abstract: Polyethylene oxide (PEO)-based composite solid electrolytes containing electrospun lithium aluminum titanium phosphate (LATP) and poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) nanofibers were fabricated to investigate the influence of LATP filler morphology on ionic conduction. LATP precursor nanofibers with the nominal composition Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 were prepared by electrospinning followed by calcination, whereas PVDF nanofibers were incorporated as a fibrous structural component without heat treatment. TGA/DTG analysis showed multistep removal of residual solvents and precursor-derived organic species, and XRD confirmed crystallization of NASICON-type LATP. A weak AlPO 4 secondary-phase peak was already detectable at 800 °C and became more evident at 900 and 1000 °C; therefore, 700 °C was selected as the calcination temperature. DSC analysis showed a composition-dependent effect of filler morphology on PEO crystallinity; notably, at 25 wt% LATP the nanofiber-containing membrane exhibited a lower PEO crystallinity (17.4%) than the corresponding particle-containing membrane (43.7%). Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy showed that the ionic conductivity varied strongly with LATP filler morphology and composition, reaching 1.19 × 10 −4 S cm −1 at room temperature for the 25 wt% sample, whereas the corresponding particle-filled membrane exhibited 5.15 × 10 −6 S cm −1 . Because LATP and PVDF fractions were varied simultaneously, the conductivity trend is interpreted as a combined compositional, morphological, and interfacial effect rather than as an isolated LATP-content effect.

papers.title: Corporate sustainable development effects of the artificial intelligence pilot zone policy: evidence from China based on double machine learning
papers.abstract: Introduction As digital transformation becomes increasingly intertwined with green development, whether the artificial intelligence pilot zone (AIPZ) policy improves corporate sustainable development performance warrants empirical examination. Methods Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we treat the establishment of AIPZs as a quasi-natural experiment and apply double machine learning to estimate the policy effect. Results The AIPZ policy significantly improves corporate sustainable development performance, and the result is robust across alternative specifications and tests. Decomposition analysis shows improvements in environmental performance, the joint development level, and the balance between economic and environmental performance, despite a decline in return on assets. Mechanism tests point to green innovation, lower agency costs, and human capital upgrading as potential channels. The effect is stronger among non-state-owned enterprises, firms outside heavily polluting industries, and high-tech firms. Discussion These findings suggest that governance arrangements, environmental constraints, and technological capabilities shape firms’ responses to the policy. They provide firm-level evidence on how place-based artificial intelligence policy may support green corporate transformation.

papers.title: Fabrication of High‐Performance Sustainable Packaging Composites via Blending of Recycled Polypropylene With Surface‐Functionalized Rice Husk‐Derived Nanosilica and Phthalate‐Modified Starch
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Polypropylene is extensively used as a packaging material, creating a huge amount of waste after use. This work highlights the use of recycled polypropylene (rPP), starch phthalate, and modified nanosilica to produce sustainable packaging material. Both starch and nanosilica are functionalized to improve overall compatibility by increasing dispersion within the rPP matrix. Among the formulations, the optimal composition was 8:0.6:32 (starch/starch phthalate:nanosilica:rPP:PMS3). Characterization through FTIR, SEM, XRD, and TGA confirmed structural and morphological improvements. SEM analysis reveals a more uniform and refined surface upon replacing starch with starch phthalate, reducing mechanical vulnerability and phase separation due to enhanced interfacial adhesion. XRD results indicated crystallinity in the modified blend. The starch phthalate‐based composite shows superior degradability and improved tensile (38.12 MPa) and tear strength (88.24 N/mm) compared to the starch‐based system, showing a higher Young's modulus (1707 N/mm 2 ). Loss in mechanical properties under soil burial conditions for a period of 12 months reveals a decrease in tensile strength, tear strength, and Young's modulus to 25.9216 MPa, 59.1208 N/mm, and 829.6 N/mm 2 , respectively. PMS3 exhibited statistically significant, reproducible, and highly predictable degradation behavior in tensile strength, Young's modulus, and tear strength over 12 months ( R 2 ≥ 0.977, p < 0.05). Kinetic analysis showed that starch modification increased the apparent degradation rate by approximately 86.5%. Thus, the synergistic blend presents a promising sustainable alternative for packaging applications.
