papers.title: NANOVESICULAR TOPICAL DELIVERY SYSTEMS FOR PSORIASIS MANAGEMENT: FROM LIPOSOMES TO INVASOMES—MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS, TRANSLATIONAL ADVANCES, AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES.
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, relapsing, immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis characterized by epidermal hyperproliferation, aberrant keratinocyte differentiation, angiogenesis, and sustained activation of the IL-23/Th17 inflammatory axis.Despite remarkable advances in systemic biologics and targeted immunotherapies, topical treatment remains the cornerstone for managing mild-to-moderate psoriasis and an essential adjunct in severe disease.However, conventional topical formulations often demonstrate limited therapeutic efficacy owing to inadequate penetration across the stratum corneum, poor drug retention, instability of active pharmaceutical ingredients, and dose-related adverse effects.Recent advances in nanotechnology have revolutionized topical drug delivery through the development of nanovesicular systems capable of enhancing drug permeation, increasing epidermal retention, improving pharmacokinetic performance, and reducing systemic exposure.Liposomes, niosomes, transfersomes, ethosomes, transethosomes, glycerosomes, hyalurosomes, and invasomes represent successive generations of vesicular carriers specifically engineered to overcome the skin barrier.Among these systems, invasomes have emerged as highly promising ultradeformable vesicles owing to the synergistic action of phospholipids, ethanol, and terpenes, which collectively facilitate deeper skin penetration and improved therapeutic outcomes.This review critically evaluates the evolution of nanovesicular technologies for psoriasis management, emphasizing mechanistic aspects of skin penetration, formulation design, physicochemical characterization, preclinical and clinical evidence, translational challenges, regulatory considerations, and future perspectives.Particular emphasis is placed on recent advances reported between 2020 and 2026 and their potential to bridge the gap between laboratory innovation and clinical application.

papers.title: Development of Erlotinib Nanoliposome-Loaded Dry Powder Inhaler for Enhanced Pulmonary Delivery
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Objectives: To develop erlotinib nanoliposome-loaded dry powder inhaler formulations for targeted pulmonary delivery in non-small cell lung cancer, addressing the limitations of poor aqueous solubility, systemic toxicity, and suboptimal tumor localization associated with conventional erlotinib therapy.Methods: Six DPI formulations (IF1-IF6) were prepared by co-spray drying of pre-optimized erlotinib nanoliposomes with varying concentrations of lactose monohydrate, mannitol, and L-leucine as carrier excipients.Formulations were systematically evaluated for physicochemical properties, powder flow, aerodynamic performance using Andersen Cascade Impactor, in vitro drug release in simulated lung fluid, solid-state characterization, and accelerated stability under ICH Q1A(R2) conditions.The optimized batch was selected based on superior aerodynamic performance and overall physicochemical attributes.Results: Particle size D50 ranged from 4.82±0.18μm (IF1) to 2.98±0.22μm (IF6), with entrapment efficiency of 84.6-88.1% post spray drying.Formulation IF5 was identified as optimal, demonstrating MMAD of 3.18±0.21μm, FPF of 56.4±1.9%,emitted dose of 88.2±1.4%, and cumulative drug release of 93.4±2.7% over 12 hours in simulated lung fluid.Drug release followed Hixson-Crowell kinetics (R²=0.9986)with anomalous non-Fickian diffusion confirmed by Korsmeyer-Peppas exponent n=0.7153.Accelerated stability studies confirmed no statistically significant changes in critical quality attributes over six months (p>0.05).Conclusion: The developed nanoliposomal DPI system offers a clinically significant advancement in site-specific pulmonary erlotinib delivery, with potential to improve therapeutic outcomes and reduce systemic adverse effects in NSCLC patients, warranting further in vivo pharmacokinetic and efficacy validation.

papers.title: Hippo signalling-linked circulating microRNA networks associate with cardiovascular disease in Type 2 Diabetes
papers.abstract: Abstract Context Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) markedly increases the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers for patient stratification and may provide mechanistic insight into dysregulated pathways in T2D-associated CVD. Objective To identify circulating miRNA signatures in T2D patients with CVD (T2D-CVD) versus T2D patients without CVD using a novel network-based medicine approach. Methods Patients (n = 110) were stratified into T2D and T2D-CVD groups based on the absence or presence of macrovascular complications. Circulating miRNAs, pro-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors were profiled in a discovery cohort (n = 80) and confirmed in a validation cohort (n = 30). Differential expression, network-based approaches and pathway enrichment analyses identified miRNA signatures, co-expression communities, hub miRNAs, and associated signalling pathways. Results T2D-CVD patients showed a set of elevated inflammatory cytokines and circulating miRNAs. Particularly, nineteen miRNAs were differentially expressed between T2D-CVD and T2D patients. Pathway enrichment of these miRNAs highlighted Hippo signalling together with TGF-β, mTOR, Wnt, and PI3K–Akt pathways. Network analysis identified a co-expression community of 34 miRNAs, including hub miRNAs let-7a-5p, miR-132-3p, and miR-1306-3p, all linked to Hippo signalling. Key miRNA interactions were validated, and both differentially expressed and hub miRNAs correlated with inflammatory mediators such as PAR-1, CXCL1 and NEMO, which are linked to Hippo pathway regulation. Conclusions This study identified a network of circulating miRNAs associated with inflammatory cytokines and Hippo signalling pathway in T2D-CVD. These findings reveal novel molecular aspects of the systemic inflammation characterizing T2D-CVD and support the potential of Hippo-related circulating miRNAs as mechanistic biomarkers for cardiovascular risk in T2D.

papers.title: Formulation, Optimization, and Characterization of Oral Floating InSitu Gel of Lovastatin Using 2³ Factorial Design
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Lovastatin, a lipid-lowering agent, exhibits poor oral bioavailability (<5%) due to low aqueous solubility and extensive first-pass metabolism.Improving its delivery through enhanced gastric retention and sustained release systems is essential for therapeutic efficacy.This study focuses on developing a floating oral in-situ gel formulation of Lovastatin to address these limitations.Objective: The aim was to formulate, optimize, and characterize a floating oral in-situ gel of Lovastatin using a 2³ factorial design, ensuring prolonged gastric retention and controlled drug release.Methodology: Nine formulations were prepared with varying amounts of Sodium Alginate, Pectin, and Xanthan Gum.The influence of these variables on viscosity and dissolution rate was assessed using a 2³ factorial design.Evaluation parameters included pH, drug content, gelation time, floating lag time, duration of floating, and viscosity.In-vitro drug release studies were performed over 12 hours in 0.1N HCl (pH 1.2), and the release kinetics were analyzed using various models.Optimization was achieved through overlay plot analysis to determine the ideal formulation.Results: Formulation F1 exhibited rapid gelation (<10 seconds), immediate floating ability (<1 minute), and sustained buoyancy (>12 hours).Viscosity analysis confirmed efficient gel formation, while in-vitro release studies demonstrated 98.6% cumulative drug release within 11 hours.The kinetic analysis revealed a Zero Order release pattern (R² = 0.9843), indicating consistent and controlled drug release.The optimized formulation contained Sodium Alginate (0.42 g), Pectin (0.51 g), and Xanthan Gum (0.197 g), achieving a desirability score of 1.000. Conclusion:The optimized floating oral in-situ gel formulation (F1) effectively enhances the gastric retention and sustained release of Lovastatin, improving its bioavailability and therapeutic performance.This novel approach offers a promising strategy for the effective management of hyperlipidemia.

papers.title: In-Depth Characterisation and Microwave-Assisted Conversion of Opuntia ficus-indica into High-Value-Added Platform Compounds
papers.abstract: Nowadays, humanity is facing a paradigm change in the productive model, switching from fossil-based carbon sources and a linear economy, to more sustainable and circular alternatives. In this regard, lignocellulosic biomass is considered as a perfect substitute for fossil-based carbon sources. Opuntia ficus-indica (OFI) is a crassulacean acid metabolism species, capable of growing in arid places that are not suitable for food production. In this work, a systematic fractionation process combined with analytical techniques (nuclear magnetic resonance, thermogravimetric analysis, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy) unveiled the extraordinarily high carbohydrate content of OFI fruit. Therefore, OFI fruit is a perfect feedstock for the obtention of high-value-added chemicals, namely levulinic acid (LA) and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF). By microwave-assisted thermochemical treatment of the most suitable fraction, LA was obtained in a 22.1 wt. % yield in an aqueous monophasic system, and 5-HMF in an 11.5 wt. % yield in a biphasic system. Reuse of the catalyst and co-catalyst in a monophasic system led to 5-HMF in a 14.3 wt. % yield after five cycles, avoiding the need for an organic co-solvent. This work demonstrates the potential of this feedstock to obtain high-value-added chemicals, employing marginal land in environments where other crops are unable to grow.

papers.title: Surface engineering strategies for PET-Based ligament scaffolds in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: a systematic review of mechanical and biological performances
papers.abstract: Background/Objective ACL reconstruction is among the most common orthopedic procedures, yet autografts and allografts carry significant limitations including donor site morbidity and immunological risk. PET-based synthetic grafts such as LARS were introduced to address these shortcomings, but their biologically inert surface raises concerns regarding cellular adhesion and host tissue integration. A new generation of functionalized PET scaffolds has emerged over the past decade, yet no systematic review has summarized this evidence since 2011. The present review aims to evaluate the biological and mechanical effects of novel functionalized PET scaffolds for ACL reconstruction. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched up to 20 August 2026 for original studies investigating chemically or biologically modified polyethylene terephthalate grafts for Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction and reporting in vitro outcomes, in vivo animal model data, and mechanical properties. Two independent reviewers performed screening, full-text assessment, and data extraction. Results Seventeen studies met the inclusion criteria. Functionalization strategies included physical deposition, chemical surface modification, biomimetic mineral coatings, and hybrid composite fabrication. Across all studies, functionalized PET scaffolds generally demonstrated improved performance compared with unmodified PET controls. In vitro , enhanced cellular proliferation, upregulation of osteogenic markers, and increased angiogenic activity were observed. In vivo , improved graft–bone integration was demonstrated by higher bone volume fraction, reduced tunnel area, and decreased interface width. Post-implantation ultimate load to failure and stiffness generally favored functionalized PET scaffolds, though both parameters remained inferior to the native ACL in direct comparisons. Conclusion Surface biofunctionalization appears to enhance the biological and mechanical performance of PET-based scaffolds for ACL reconstruction, suggesting that surface bioengineering may play an important role in promoting biological integration and functional performance. These findings indicate that functionalized PET scaffolds could represent potential donor-independent alternatives for ACL reconstruction and may warrant further investigation as synthetic ligament substitutes. However, a persistent mechanical gap versus native ligament tissue remains. These findings should be interpreted with caution due to methodological heterogeneity, predominant use of small animal models, and inconsistent outcome reporting across the included studies.
papers.summary: The present review aims to evaluate the biological and mechanical effects of novel functionalized PET scaffolds for ACL reconstruction. Across all studies, functionalized PET scaffolds generally demonstrated improved performance compared with unmodified PET controls. Conclusion Surface biofunctionalization appears to enhance the biological and mechanical performance of PET-based scaffolds for ACL reconstruction, suggesting that surface bioengineering may play an important role in promoting biological integration and functional performance.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic and computational analysis associates Ms4a6c+ macrophages with fibrosis in radiation proctitis and computationally nominates MOTS-c as a candidate modulator
papers.abstract: Background Chronic radiation proctitis (CRP) represents a significant clinical challenge characterized by irreversible fibrosis and a lack of specific pharmacological interventions. This study aimed to elucidate the cellular mechanisms underlying impaired tissue repair to identify novel therapeutic targets. Methods We employed an integrative framework combining machine learning with bulk and high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic profiling in a murine CRP model. Computational mechanistic analyses included regulon inference, cell-cell communication analysis, and single-cell virtual knockout simulation. The pro-fibrotic association of the identified macrophage subset was further examined using independent single-cell datasets from liver cirrhosis and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Furthermore, structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to identify potential pharmacological modulators. Results We identified Ms4a6c as a key candidate gene exclusively expressed in a distinct, hybrid-activation macrophage subpopulation associated with pro-fibrotic transcriptional programs. These macrophages showed predicted associations with fibrosis via Thbs1-Cd47 paracrine signaling interactions with fibroblasts, and SCENIC regulon analysis identified Cebpb as a candidate upstream transcriptional regulator. Cross-disease analysis in liver cirrhosis and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis single-cell datasets indicated that Ms4a6c-high macrophage subsets are consistently associated with elevated epithelial-mesenchymal transition and TGF-β signaling activity, supporting a potentially conserved pro-fibrotic role across organ systems. Furthermore, single-cell virtual knockout simulation predicted that the computational depletion of Ms4a6c may reverse pro-fibrotic transcriptomic signatures. Additionally, molecular docking and dynamics simulations identified the mitochondrial-derived peptide MOTS-c as a top-ranking candidate predicted to target Ms4a6c. Conclusions This study highlights the potential pathogenic involvement of Ms4a6c+ macrophages and identifies the Cebpb-Ms4a6c-Thbs1-Cd47 axis as a candidate pro-fibrotic signaling cascade that may be conserved across multiple organ fibrosis models. We propose MOTS-c as a potential pharmacological agent for mitigating radiation-induced intestinal fibrosis, pending experimental validation.

papers.abstract: Over the years, there have been significant advances in rocket propulsion system. These advances have been encouraged by the urge to improve reliability, efficiency and versatility in space exploration. This study provides comprehensive overview of those advances. It would be focusing on major breakthroughs for rocket propulsion systems and their effect on space missions. In rocket propulsion systems, recent advances cover different factors like engine systems, propulsion systems, control and materials. Some of the examples of electric propulsion systems are Hall and Ion effect thrusters which have transformed long-term missions by providing better fuel efficiency and impulse than conventional chemical counterparts. These systems have been widely used in deep space missions, orbit transfer, and keeping satellite station. In addition, developing engines, combustion technology and smart propellants have advanced traditional chemical propulsion. 3D printing and other technological breakthroughs have enabled production of complex engine parts with better effectiveness and accuracy. It has reduced expenses and improved performance. In addition, researchers have advanced reusable techniques to improve availability of space and reduce launch expenses. As observed by launch of reusable vehicles by several aerospace organizations, major achievements have been observed in reusability of engines, landing, and thermal protection. In addition, ambitious missions have been achieved with advances in rocket propulsion systems, including lunar exploration programs, manned Mars expeditions, and asteroid mining operations. Rocket propulsion systems are needed for covering long distances with spacecrafts and achieving objectives of mission. In rocket propulsion systems, recent advances have exceeded the boundaries of space exploration, offering unmatched potential for corporate ventures and international cooperation.

papers.title: Segmentation of ovarian cancer tumors from CT images based on a two-stage neural network fusion system
papers.abstract: The detection of ovarian cancer using computed tomography images is making rapid progress, combining the strengths of different neural networks within a complex ensemble, a more effective model can be created to support medical decision-making in ovarian cancer cases. Various neural networks and ensemble models were tested on the TCGA OV database. Tumor regions were segmented using computer-assisted annotation masks, while molecular subtype labels were assigned at the patient level based on TCGA genomic classifications and mapped to tumors. As the main novelty, the proposed method involves a two-stage fusion system. The first stage combines several neural networks into four ensembles to capture diverse features, and the second stage integrates these results into a global system to enhance segmentation accuracy. The selected models demonstrated strong segmentation performance within the investigated experimental setting and were subsequently integrated into the proposed two-stage fusion framework. The neural networks for the first stage are Attention U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and ViT. The results show that the proposed two-stage fusion system achieved higher observed segmentation performance than the evaluated individual neural networks and first-stage ensemble configurations within the present TCGA-OV experimental setting. Across the five evaluated classes, the Global System achieved an average F1 score of 93.53%, recall of 93.38%, and precision of 93.68%, supporting the technical feasibility of the proposed two-stage fusion approach for ovarian tumor segmentation within the investigated dataset.

papers.title: A Universal Spin‐Polarization‐Engineered Antibonding‐Orbital Modulation Paradigm for Accelerating Reaction Kinetics in Ultrahigh‐Rate Sodium‐Ion Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Conversion‐type anode materials hold great promise for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass‐transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal–chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long‐standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin‐polarization‐engineered (SPE) antibonding‐orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh‐rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin‐state transition from low‐spin to high‐spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal e g orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin‐engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn‐FeS 2 /CoS 2 anode delivers an ultrahigh‐rate capability of 300 mA h g −1 at 120 A g −1 , together with exceptional long‐term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g −1 ), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial‐level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.

papers.title: Oral Fast Dissolving Films of Meclizine: A Novel Approach for Rapid Relief from Motion Sickness
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Motion sickness is a common physiological disorder that occurs due to sensory mismatch between visual, vestibular, and proprioceptive inputs.It is characterized by symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, dizziness, sweating, and general discomfort, which significantly affect individuals during travel by road, sea, or air.Conventional therapeutic approaches for motion sickness mainly involve the use of antihistamines and anticholinergic drugs such as Meclizine and Scopolamine.However, these conventional oral dosage forms are associated with certain limitations, including delayed onset of action, difficulty in swallowing during nausea, and poor patient compliance, particularly in pediatric and geriatric populations.To overcome these limitations, oral fast dissolving films (OFDFs) have emerged as a novel and promising drug delivery system.These thin polymeric films rapidly disintegrate upon contact with saliva, leading to quick dissolution and absorption of the drug through the oral mucosa, thereby providing a faster onset of therapeutic action without the need for water.Meclizine hydrochloride, a first-generation H1 antihistamine, is widely used in the management of motion sickness due to its antiemetic and antivertigo properties.Its suitability as a low-dose drug with the need for rapid action makes it an ideal candidate for formulation into oral fast dissolving films.The development of Meclizine-loaded OFDFs offers several advantages, including rapid drug release, improved bioavailability, enhanced patient compliance, and ease of administration.This review highlights the potential of OFDF technology as an effective alternative to conventional dosage forms and emphasizes its future scope in improving the management of motion sickness, especially in situations requiring immediate therapeutic relief.

papers.title: Preparation and characterization of corn starch-based food packaging films: effects of thymol essential oil and ZnO nanoparticles on physicochemical, mechanical, barrier, thermal, and antimicrobial properties
papers.journal: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Conventional petroleum-based food packaging materials pose significant environmental challenges due to their non-biodegradable nature, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives with enhanced functional properties. Therefore, this study aimed to develop biodegradable corn starch-based composite films incorporated with varying concentrations of thymol essential oil (0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 wt% of corn starch) and ZnO nanoparticles (5, 16, 28, and 33 wt% of corn starch) and to evaluate their physicochemical, structural, thermal, and antimicrobial properties. The films were characterized using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and other physicochemical analyses, while their antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus was also investigated. The results demonstrated that ZnO nanoparticles significantly enhanced the thermal stability and crystallinity of the corn starch films, whereas thymol essential oil markedly improved their antimicrobial activity. Among all formulations, the film containing 0.3 wt% thymol and 28 wt% ZnO nanoparticles exhibited the well-balanced performance, showing improved mechanical strength, reduced water vapor permeability, enhanced structural integrity, and effective antimicrobial activity. The incorporation of thymol and ZnO nanoparticles also influenced the films’ thickness and optical properties, indicating successful modification of the starch matrix. These findings demonstrate that thymol- and ZnO nanoparticle-reinforced corn starch films are promising biodegradable materials for active food packaging applications by combining improved barrier, mechanical, thermal, and antimicrobial properties.

The results demonstrated that ZnO nanoparticles significantly enhanced the thermal stability and crystallinity of the corn starch films, whereas thymol essential oil markedly improved their antimicrobial activity. papers.title: Recycling of polycarbonate from optical lens manufacturing waste via solvent-targeted recovery and precipitation: A process feasibility and sustainability assessment
papers.abstract: Polycarbonate (PC) is widely used in optical lenses, and lens manufacturing generates a heterogeneous waste stream known as swarf that contains PC, polyurethanes, thermoset resins, coatings, and process debris and is currently unrecyclable. This preliminary feasibility study evaluates swarf as a potential feedstock for PC recycling via solvent-targeted recovery and precipitation (STRAP™). Solvent selection was guided by COSMO-RS modeling to identify solvents that dissolve PC under mild conditions (65–120 °C, ambient pressure) while minimizing urethane-resin dissolution. Among the solvents tested, tetrahydrofuran (THF) gave the highest PC yield (89 wt%), outperforming toluene (74 wt%) and xylenes (63 wt%). Spectroscopic (FTIR), thermal (TGA, DSC), and chromatographic (GPC) analyses confirm the THF-recovered fraction is PC, with no detected contamination from other polymers. A reduction in glass transition temperature (135.4 °C versus 145.6 °C for virgin PC) and a 20 °C decrease in degradation onset measured by TGA suggest the possible formation of a minor low-molecular-weight in the recovered PC. Further development is needed to optimize the process and validate end-use performance at scale. A technoeconomic analysis of small-scale STRAP operations (2000–10,000 t yr⁻ 1 ) indicates that, under favorable assumptions for feedstock logistics, solvent-based PC recovery from swarf can be economically viable. Specifically, a 5000 t yr⁻ 1 plant selling recycled PC at $2.50 kg⁻ 1 achieves a 15 % IRR. Life cycle assessment shows an 79 % reduction in greenhouse gas emissions (kg CO 2 eq.) versus virgin PC production. Further development is needed to address polymer performance at scale.

Further development is needed to optimize the process and validate end-use performance at scale. Further development is needed to address polymer performance at scale.

papers.title: Cyclophilin D deficiency exacerbates diet-induced obesity and selectively enhances skeletal muscle mitochondrial respiration in male mice
papers.journal: Pflügers Archiv - European Journal of Physiology
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of obesity-associated metabolic disease, with the mitochondrial permeability transition pore serving as a key regulator of cellular energy homeostasis. Cyclophilin D, encoded by Ppif, is the principal regulatory component of this pore and has been implicated in insulin secretion, adipocyte survival, and whole-body energy balance. However, whether Ppif loss produces a consistent metabolic phenotype when challenged with high fat diet (HFD) exposure, and whether systemic metabolic alterations reflect tissue-specific changes in mitochondrial oxidative capacity, remains unresolved. Here, we characterized male, 21-weeks-old mice with germline Ppif deletion longitudinally over 34 weeks under standard (SD) and HFD using body composition analysis, indirect calorimetry, glucose and insulin tolerance testing and tissue-resolved, Seahorse-based mitochondrial respirometry. Under SD, knockout mice displayed elevated fat mass without differences in food intake or energy expenditure. High-fat feeding progressively amplified this adiposity, with knockout mice developing significantly greater body weight and fat mass than wild-type littermates by weeks 28 and 36. Glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity remained comparable between genotypes under either diet. ANCOVA revealed significant effects of lean mass (p < 0.001) and genotype (p = 0.017) on energy expenditure, as well as a significant lean mass × genotype interaction (p = 0.025). Consistent with a distinct contribution of lean mass to EE in KO vs. WT mice, we found increased ADP-stimulated mitochondrial respiration in quadriceps of knockout mice under both diets, without corresponding differences in brown adipose tissue or liver, or changes in mitochondrial content across tissues. These findings establish cyclophilin D as a diet- and tissue-specific regulator of energy homeostasis, informing therapeutic strategies targeting the permeability transition pore or cyclophilin D interactome in metabolic disease.

papers.title: Silyl Chloroalkenyl and Alkynyl Sulfur Pentafluorides as Versatile Reagents to Access Fundamental SF5 Building Blocks
papers.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a second-generation SF5-alkenyl platform reagent granting facile benchtop access to a variety of known and unknown SF5-containing building blocks under mild conditions without any necessity to use pentafluorosulfanylation reagents, such as SF5Cl, on-site. This work overcomes the previous synthetic bottleneck that had prevented a broader use of the triisopropylsilylalkynyl (TASP) reagent. This versatile platform reagent is thermally stable, easy to handle, shows high shelf stability, and can be accessed on a multigram scale. This class of reagents undergoes protodesilylation/nucleophilic substitution reactions with O-, S-, and N-nucleophiles allowing access to (E)-configured α-SF5-enamines (up to >99%), (E)-configured α-SF5-vinyl ethers (up to 90%), another synthetically useful access to (E)-configured β-vinyl sulfides (up to 99%), O,O-acetals (up to 95%), and S,S-acetals (up to 97%) in a single reaction step. Further processing allowed access to S,S-ketene acetals (up to 97%), the corresponding α-SF5-acetic acid esters (up to 88%), as well as α-SF5-acetic acid (92%). Based on these findings, we shed light on the operating reaction mechanism by DFT studies, revealing that the amount of charge accumulated on the α-SF5 carbon controls the efficacy of the reaction with different nucleophiles. In a second part, we reconnected to previous inaccessible alkynyl sulfur pentafluorides by developing a novel in situ elimination strategy and identified the TBDMS derivative as an accessible, stable, and reactive reagent to prepare the complementary (Z)-configured β-vinyl sulfides (up to 85%) in a single reaction step, whereas the pure TMS and TES alkynyl derivatives were found to be inaccessible or unstable under ambient conditions. This report offers a versatile and robust protocol to access important SF5-containing organic motifs employing a commercially available prefunctionalized SF5 reagent.

This versatile platform reagent is thermally stable, easy to handle, shows high shelf stability, and can be accessed on a multigram scale. papers.title: Multicarrier electrical and thermal magnetotransport in altermagnetic CrSb
papers.abstract: Chromium antimonide has emerged as a key material platform for studying altermagnetism because of its simple binary composition, high Néel temperature, and semimetallic electronic structure. Here, we investigate electrical and thermal magnetotransport in single-crystalline CrSb using steady- and pulsed-magnetic fields up to 65 T, and complement these measurements with neutron diffraction and magnetization data. We confirm the compensated magnetic structure and observe a large nonsaturating magnetoresistance together with a pronounced nonlinear Hall response at low temperatures. Multicarrier modeling, supported by mobility-spectrum analysis, reveals coexisting electron- and holelike charge carriers with mobilities up to ∼ 3000 cm 2 / Vs and shows that the number of transport channels that can be resolved strongly depends on the accessible magnetic-field range. Thermal-transport measurements further reveal a nonlinear thermal Hall response and a thermal conductivity substantially exceeding a simple Wiedemann-Franz law. The broadly similar field and temperature evolution of electrical and thermal transport point to a dominant electronic contribution, while the remaining deviations indicate additional heat-carrying channels.

papers.title: Modular cryogenic link for microwave quantum communication over distances of tens of meters
papers.abstract: Quantum technologies promise a radically new way to solve classically intractable computing problems. Superconducting circuits as a platform are at the forefront of this field. The cryogenic operation temperatures of superconducting circuits however impose challenges for the further scaling to many connected quantum information processing units into a local area or global network. In this work, we present a hardware solution for connecting quantum devices operating at microwave frequencies into local area networks, which enable the exchange of quantum information between spatially separated parties. Specifically, we demonstrate a modular system spanning distances of 5, 10 and 30 meters operated at cryogenic temperatures and connecting two superconducting circuit systems, located in individual dilution refrigerators, through a quantum communication channel. We develop a thermal model to evaluate the heat transfer processes in the setup, optimize the design and select appropriate materials for its construction. The assembled 30-meter-long system achieves operating temperatures of below 50 mK after a cooldown time of about six and a half days. This link enables the execution of distributed quantum computing and communication algorithms. It also adds the resource of non-locality, certified by a loophole-free Bell test, to the field of quantum science and technology with superconducting circuits.

papers.title: Biochar addition enhances soil aggregate stability by modulating soil internal forces: the critical role of readily oxidized organic carbon and particulate organic carbon
papers.abstract: Abstract. Degradation of soil structure and function is a significant obstacle to sustainable agriculture, yet using biochar is known to be an effective way of increasing soil organic carbon and boosting structure. Aggregate stability is greatly influenced by soil internal forces (SIFs), such as van der Waals, hydration, and electrostatic forces. However, it is still not clear which specific organic carbon components play a significant role in the stability of aggregates and the action of soil internal forces. In this study, a field simulation experiment was conducted using maize straw and wheat straw biochars to investigate how biochar addtion affect soil aggregate stability. The findings showed that as the rate of biochar application increased from 0 % to 10 % over 180 day and 365 days, the contents of soil light fraction organic carbon (LFOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), readily oxidized organic carbon (ROC), as well as soil specific surface area and surface charge number, increased. The content of different carbon fractions decreased with prolonged incubation time, while soil electrochemical parameters continued to increase throughout the incubation period. Pearson correlation and redundancy analyses showed that soil active organic carbon fractions were strongly correlated with soil surface electrochemical properties, with ROC and POC being the primary factors. Soil aggregate stability increased with higher biochar application rates, and the beneficial effect of biochar on aggregate stability became increasingly pronounced over time. Based on the quantitative estimates of SIFs, the addition of biochar facilitated soil aggregates stability by increasing van der Waals attractive pressure and decreasing electrostatic repulsive pressure, and finally lowering net repulsive pressure between soil particles. The soil aggregate breaking strength increased quickly at initially and then leveled out as the electrolyte content decreased; 10−2 mol L−1 marked the tipping point. The study identified the active organic carbon (ROC and POC) fractions which could mediate the soil surface electrochemical properties and soil internal forces, finally enhance soil aggregate stability. Our research provides a theoretical basis for the targeted use and modifying of biochar to efficiently improve soil structure.

The findings showed that as the rate of biochar application increased from 0 % to 10 % over 180 day and 365 days, the contents of soil light fraction organic carbon (LFOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), readily oxidized organic carbon (ROC), as well as soil specific surface area and surface charge number, increased. Soil aggregate stability increased with higher biochar application rates, and the beneficial effect of biochar on aggregate stability became increasingly pronounced over time.

papers.title: Influence of irradiance and mixing layer height on the vertical trace matter distribution in the lower planetary boundary layer – drone-based investigation
papers.abstract: Abstract. Drone-based atmospheric measurements allow time-resolved investigation of stratification in the lower atmosphere of many atmospherically relevant variables. Measuring a variety of variables can be used, e.g., for mixing layer (height, MLH) identification and examination of the representativity of ground-based measurements in the lowermost boundary layer. We present drone-based vertical profiling during two 2.5‑week summer field campaigns in rural Germany to investigate the vertical distribution of trace matter and meteorological variables in the lowermost troposphere. Night-time vertical profiling of temperature, humidity, wind speed, and trace substances (CO2, O3, particle mass and number concentrations) in the lowest 120 m revealed a multiple-layer fine-scale stratification. Trace substances surpassed several traditional meteorological variables in sensitivity for MLH detection. Among all variables, O3 and potential temperature were the most reliable MLH markers, highlighting combining trace matter and meteorological measurements to understand stratification processes. Using a gradient-based approach for diurnal vertical profiles up to 500 m above ground, we evaluate under which conditions and to which degree ground-based measurements, used world-wide in networks or during individual field campaigns, can be taken as representative for the lowermost mixing layer, and how strong radiative-driven mixing reduces vertical gradients. Location-specific sources and sinks affect the trace matter distribution in the ML much stronger than irradiance. However, homogeneity of aerosol particle concentrations was strongly promoted under high-radiative conditions, even at low MLHs. This suggests distinguishing between high- and low-irradiation conditions in the planetary boundary layer could improve parameterization for vertical mixing and should be considered when evaluating ground-based data.

papers.title: Integrative analysis reveals gut microbiota-associated host regulatory networks in liver fibrosis
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
papers.abstract: Background Gut microbiota-derived metabolites may contribute to liver fibrosis by affecting host inflammatory, metabolic, and epigenetic pathways. We aimed to identify microbiota-associated host genes shared across liver fibrosis of different etiologies. Methods Microbiota- and metabolite-associated host genes were obtained from gutMGene v2.0 and integrated with differentially expressed genes from two human liver transcriptomic datasets: GSE84044 for HBV-related fibrosis and GSE49541 for NAFLD-related fibrosis. Shared genes were analyzed using protein–protein interaction and functional enrichment analyses. Selected metabolite–protein interactions were assessed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Two-sample Mendelian randomization was used to examine potential associations between candidate gene expression and liver fibrosis risk. Results Fourteen microbiota-associated genes were differentially expressed in both fibrosis cohorts, including CCL2, CCL20, CXCL6, PTGS2, HDAC2, HDAC3, ADRA2A, SOD1, PEMT, and GNMT. These genes were mainly associated with chemokine activity, histone deacetylation, and IL-17 and TNF signaling. Molecular docking suggested structural compatibility between phenylacetylglutamine and ADRA2A, while butyrate showed weaker predicted interactions with HDAC2 and HDAC3.Molecular dynamics analysis supported the stability of the ADRA2A–phenylacetylglutamine complex under the simulated conditions. Mendelian randomization identified nominal associations of HDAC3, CCL2, PTGS2, and VCL expression with liver fibrosis risk. Conclusions This study identified shared microbiota-associated host regulatory candidates in HBV- and NAFLD-related liver fibrosis.HDAC3 and ADRA2A may represent potential links between microbial metabolic signals and fibrotic responses, although further experimental validation is required.

papers.title: Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitors: Structural Evolution, Binding Mechanisms, and Theranostic Applications in Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography Imaging
papers.abstract: α-Fibroblast activation protein (α-FAP) is overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts within the tumor microenvironment of most epithelial cancers, making it an attractive target for cancer-specific imaging and therapy. This article summarizes the structural features, binding mechanisms, radiolabelling strategies, and clinical potential of FAP inhibitors (FAPIs). FAPI molecules generally consist of three functional modules: a quinoline-based core for target recognition, a linker, and a DOTA/NOTA chelator for radionuclide labelling. The interaction between FAPIs and α-FAP is primarily mediated by several amino acid residues, each engaging a specific structural module of the inhibitor, but residues involved are not fixed and may shift with structural variation among FAPI derivatives. The evolution from early boronic acid compounds to UAMC-1110 marks a transition from non-selective dipeptidyl peptidase inhibitors toward FAP-selective warheads, while later modifications (e.g., cyano to α-ketoamide) addressed the need for prolonged target residence. PET/CT is the combination of functional and structural scanning, increasing diagnostic accuracy. The same targeting principle also enables therapeutic applications when labelled with β-emitting radionuclides. The clear specificity of FAPI also helps overcome many limitations of 18 F-FDG.

papers.title: Molecular Conformation as a Determinant of Self-Assembly in Sequence-Isomeric Tripeptides
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
papers.abstract: Abstract In this work, we evaluate whether computed conformational ensembles of seven tripeptides─the six C-terminal amidated D/Y/F sequence isomers and the closely related sequence FFD─are informative of their self-assembly propensity. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (AA-MD) simulations and intramolecular side-chain dihedral angles as a collective variable, we calculate conformational free-energy landscapes (FELs) for these sequences. We then introduce a novel method to numerically characterize the computed FELs and find a correlation between thermal conformational accessibility and a sequence’s tendency to self-assemble or remain in solution. In addition, we evaluate and rationalize the impact of water model selection on conformational ensembles in terms of peptide-water interaction strengths, and also investigate the influence of ionization state on conformation. The presented methodology implicitly accounts for amino acid sequence context, which is a major determinant of divergent properties for sequence isomers. It also has a low associated computational cost, making use of single-molecule simulations to predict supramolecular assembly outcomes. These features are an important advancement toward a general scheme for the theory-informed design of peptide materials.

papers.title: From Soldering to Sintering: Novel Interconnection Technology for SiC Power Device Package
papers.abstract: As new energy vehicles and wide-bandgap semiconductor power devices have been used more widely, higher requirements have been put forward for packaging interconnections, above all under repeated thermomechanical loading, at high operating temperature, and at high current density. Conventional solder joints do not perform well in such a situation, since intermetallic compounds grow, voids form, and fatigue damage develops during long service, and the long-term reliability is thus weakened; therefore, three typical interconnection technologies of next-generation power devices are reviewed in this paper, that is, transient liquid-phase sintering/bonding, silver sintering, and copper sintering. Their bonding mechanisms, processing characteristics, mechanical properties, electrical and thermal performance, and major challenges are compared. TLPS can achieve low-temperature bonding and high-temperature service, but its reliability is restricted by brittle intermetallic compounds and void evolution. Ag sintering provides excellent thermal conductivity, electrical conductivity, bonding strength, and high-temperature stability, but high cost, electrochemical migration, and large-area bonding remain important concerns. Cu sintering offers low cost, good conductivity, and better resistance to electrochemical migration, while oxidation sensitivity and pressure-dependent densification limit its practical application. Finally, this review suggests that future interconnection design should balance performance, cost, process compatibility, and long-term reliability for high-power semiconductor packaging.
papers.summary: As new energy vehicles and wide-bandgap semiconductor power devices have been used more widely, higher requirements have been put forward for packaging interconnections, above all under repeated thermomechanical loading, at high operating temperature, and at high current density. Cu sintering offers low cost, good conductivity, and better resistance to electrochemical migration, while oxidation sensitivity and pressure-dependent densification limit its practical application. Finally, this review suggests that future interconnection design should balance performance, cost, process compatibility, and long-term reliability for high-power semiconductor packaging.

papers.title: Stearic acid-modified sodium methyl silicate for enhanced mechanical strength and hydrophobicity of 3D-printed mortar
papers.abstract: The durability of cement-based materials is limited by inherent hydrophilicity and porosity, exacerbated in 3D-printed mortar by weak interlayer interfaces and interconnected pores, accelerating water ingress and performance degradation. This study developed a green aqueous modification method using stearic acid (SG) and sodium methyl silicate (SM) to synthesize a hydrophobic composite (MG). The coating and modification mechanism of SG on SM were characterized by scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) and dynamic light scattering (DLS), and scanning electron microscopy–energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) elemental mapping. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) revealed that MG8, modified with 8% SG, exhibited optimal hydrophobicity through ion exchange between -COOH and Na + and condensation with Si-OH, resulting in the formation of stable Si-O-C(O)-R covalent structures. When incorporated into 3D-printed mortar, the effects of MG8 dosage were evaluated using SEM-EDS elemental mapping, XRD, FTIR, thermogravimetric–derivative thermogravimetric analysis (TG-DTG), and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP). Results showed that increasing MG8 dosage progressively reduced printability, accompanied by a decrease in dynamic yield stress and an increase in plastic viscosity, while the mechanical and hydrophobic properties initially improved and then declined. This work presents a green and efficient hydrophobic modification strategy for 3D-printed cement-based materials.

papers.title: Competitive Coordination to Ether Oxygens Enables High‐Ionic‐Conductivity Solid Polymer Electrolytes at Room Temperature
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical application of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) electrolytes in solid‐state lithium metal batteries is severely constrained by low ionic conductivity at ambient temperature. To address this intrinsic limitation, we introduce FeF 3 as a multifunctional additive into the PEO/poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‑HFP) matrix, yielding the FeF 3 ‑PEOPVLi electrolyte. Fe 3+ ions with strong Lewis acidity competitively coordinate with the ether oxygen atoms via Fe 3+ –O–C interactions, thereby weakening the native Li + –O–C coordination and substantially reducing the energy barrier for Li + hopping. Concurrently, the strong electron withdrawing nature of Fe 3+ promotes lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) dissociation by weakening the Li–N bond, increasing the concentration of free Li + ions available for ionic transport. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the FeF 3 ‑PEOPVLi electrolyte achieves high ionic conductivity of 0.13 mS cm − 1 at 25°C. Solid‐state Li||LiFePO 4 batteries deliver discharge capacity of 120.6 mAh g − 1 at 0.5 C at 25°C and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. This work demonstrates that rational modulation of the coordination environment within PEO provides a viable and effective pathway toward high‑performance room‑temperature solid‑state lithium metal batteries.

papers.title: Some Synthetic Approaches for Copper-Containing Terpyridine-Functionalized Polysiloxane Complexes
papers.abstract: Terpyridine-containing polysiloxanes (tpy-PMHS and tpy-PDMS) were synthesized via hydrosilylation and used as macromolecular ligands for coordination with copper(I) and copper(II) precursors. Cu-tpy-PDMS-1 exhibited catalytic activity in mechanochemical azide–alkyne cycloaddition, affording the target product in 80% yield.

papers.title: Low-glycemic index functional flour modulates gut microbiota in association with anti-obesity effects in mice
papers.abstract: Background Obesity has become a prevalent global chronic disease, and dietary intervention is a safe and effective strategy for obesity prevention and management. Laminaria japonica and Lentinula edodes are widely consumed edible resources in China, while the lipid-lowering efficacy of functional noodles supplemented with their dietary fibers remains unclear. Moreover, the potential synergistic effects of combining these fibers with other functional plant ingredients have not been systematically explored. Methods This study developed three low-glycemic index (low-GI) functional flour formulations (R1: basic formula; R2: basic formula supplemented with L. japonica and L. edodes dietary fibers; R3: R2 fortified with additional functional starches) based on nutritional balance principles. The in vitro nutritional properties, digestibility, cholesterol and bile salt binding capacities, as well as α-glucosidase and pancreatic lipase inhibitory activities were evaluated. Furthermore, a high-fat diet-induced obese ICR mouse model was established to evaluate the in vivo regulatory effects of the three formulations via a 6-week dietary intervention. Results All three formulations exhibited GI values below 55 and showed significantly lower starch hydrolysis rates compared with wheat flour (WF), along with enhanced cholesterol adsorption capacity and bile salt-binding capacities, as well as stronger α-glucosidase and pancreatic lipase inhibitory activities. In the animal experiments, all three formulations significantly reduced mouse body weight, alleviated liver damage and hepatocellular pathology, reduced epididymal adipocyte size, and attenuated cecal tissue inflammation, with R3 showing the most pronounced effects. Notably, Formula 3 (R3) treatment also significantly modulated gut microbiota composition, as evidenced by increased beneficial bacteria, a reduced Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes (F/B) ratio, decreased potentially pathogenic taxa, and elevated fecal short-chain fatty acids (acetic, propionic, butyric, and isobutyric acids) compared with the model group. Correlation analyses revealed significant associations between specific microbial genera and metabolic parameters. Conclusion These findings suggest that the low-GI functional flours, particularly R3, improve metabolic health in obese mice, accompanied by modulation of gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) production. However, given the correlational nature of the current data, causal relationships need to be confirmed through further mechanistic studies, such as fecal microbiota transplantation. Overall, R3 represents a promising dietary intervention for obesity management.

papers.title: Recent Advances in the Molecular Mechanisms of Nutritional Biochemistry in Human Health and Disease
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Nutritional biochemistry has evolved from descriptive assessments of nutrient intake to a mechanistic discipline that interrogates how dietary components regulate cellular signaling, gene expression, and metabolic homeostasis.This review synthesizes recent advances in the molecular actions of macronutrients, micronutrients, and bioactive food constituents on key nutrient-sensing networks, including AMPK-mTOR, SIRT1-PGC-1α, PPARs, FXR/TGR5, and Nrf2.Particular emphasis is placed on how these pathways coordinate energy metabolism, redox balance, and immune function, and how their dysregulation contributes to metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer.We also examine emerging data from metabolomics and microbiome research showing that diet-derived metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, and tryptophan indole derivatives act as signaling intermediates at the interface of the gut, liver, immune system, and brain.In parallel, nutrigenomic and epigenetic studies illustrate how vitamins, methyl donors, amino acids, and phytochemicals remodel chromatin and transcriptional programs that shape individual disease risk.Finally, we discuss how integrated multi-omics and systems-biology approaches are beginning to define molecular phenotypes of dietary response, providing a framework for precision nutrition.Remaining challenges, including inter-individual variability, environmental modifiers, and limited large-scale clinical validation, are highlighted as priorities for future research aimed at translating mechanistic insight into targeted, personalized dietary strategies for chronic disease prevention.

papers.title: Type-, dose-, and subgroup-specific associations of dairy intake with depressive and anxiety symptoms among middle school students
papers.abstract: Background Depression and anxiety are major public health concerns among adolescents. Dairy products are important components of adolescent diets, but evidence on the associations of different dairy intake patterns with mental health symptoms remains limited. This study examined the associations of six dairy intake variables with depressive and anxiety symptoms among middle school students. Methods This cross-sectional study included 135,138 middle school students in China. Dairy intake was assessed using six variables: frequencies of milk, yogurt, milk powder, and cheese/cheese cube intake; daily amount of milk, yogurt, and milk powder; and daily amount of cheese/cheese cubes. Depressive and anxiety symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression scale and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale, respectively. Multivariable linear regression models, restricted cubic spline analyses, and interaction analyses by gender and urban-suburban context were conducted. The secondary analysis was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the Shandong Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Approval No. SDJK(K)2025-057-01). Results Daily milk intake was reported by 27.5% of students, whereas daily yogurt, milk powder, and cheese/cheese cube intake were less common. Higher frequencies of milk and yogurt intake were associated with lower depressive and anxiety symptom scores. Compared with students who never consumed milk, daily milk consumers had lower depressive symptoms (β = −2.30, 95% CI:−2.50 to −2.10) and anxiety symptoms (β = −0.90, 95% CI:−0.99 to −0.81). The associations for milk powder, cheese/cheese cubes, and total dairy amount were more complex. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested nonlinear associations, and interaction analyses indicated that several associations differed by gender and urban–suburban context. Conclusions Dairy intake was differentially associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms among middle school students. More frequent milk and yogurt intake showed relatively consistent inverse associations with symptom scores, whereas associations for milk powder, cheese/cheese cubes, and amount-based dairy measures were less consistent and, for some measures, sensitive to model specification. These findings should be interpreted as observational associations and warrant further investigation in longitudinal studies with more detailed dietary assessment.
papers.summary: Background Depression and anxiety are major public health concerns among adolescents. More frequent milk and yogurt intake showed relatively consistent inverse associations with symptom scores, whereas associations for milk powder, cheese/cheese cubes, and amount-based dairy measures were less consistent and, for some measures, sensitive to model specification.

papers.title: Nitrogen‐Doped Mesoporous Carbon Loaded With Zn Single Atoms as a Catalyst for the Synthesis of 2,4(5)‐Diarylimidazoles
papers.abstract: Single‐atom catalysts have emerged as highly effective alternatives to conventional metal catalysts due to their uniform active sites and superior catalytic performance. Stabilizing single zinc atoms on nitrogen‐doped mesoporous carbon (NMC) enhances their stability, selectivity, electrical conductivity, and compatibility with green chemistry principles. In this study, a Zn@NMC catalyst was synthesized via solvent evaporation‐induced self‐assembly, followed by thermal polymerization and pyrolysis, and characterized by 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller, thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and energy‐dispersive X‐ray mapping analyses. The catalyst was successfully applied in the one‐pot Radziszewski synthesis of 12 2,4(5)‐diarylimidazole derivatives from phenylglyoxal, various substituted benzaldehydes, and ammonium acetate. 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy were used to characterize the products. Optimal results were obtained in methanol at room temperature (25 °C) for 12 h, affording the desired products in yields of up to 97%. The incorporation of isolated zinc atoms into the nitrogen‐rich carbon matrix significantly improved selectivity toward the target diarylimidazoles by suppressing side reactions and preventing catalyst deactivation.

papers.title: Strengthening the Occupational Safety and Health Workforce: A Mixed Methods Evaluation of a NIOSH-Funded Education and Research Center
papers.journal: Journal of Public Health Management and Practice
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Workplace injuries and fatalities remain persistent public health and occupational concerns in the United States. At the same time, emerging hazards, including automation, psychosocial stressors, climate-related exposures, and an aging workforce, are reshaping occupational risk profiles. These challenges underscore the need for a well-prepared occupational safety and health (OSH) workforce. National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)-funded Education and Research Centers (ERCs) play a central role in workforce development through graduate education, research training, continuing education, and outreach. METHODS: This Practice Report describes the Deep South Center for Occupational Safety and Health (DSC), a NIOSH-funded ERC serving parts of the southeastern United States. Between October 2025 and January 2026, a cross-sectional stakeholder survey was administered to DSC program alumni, employers, continuing education (CE) participants, and industry leaders. Data were collected anonymously using Qualtrics XM and included quantitative and open-ended items. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative responses were examined using deductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: A total of 297 stakeholders responded. Respondents represented diverse OSH sectors, with the largest representation from manufacturing, health care, and the private sector. Most DSC alumni reported maintaining employment or securing positions within 12 months of graduation and reported high levels of workforce preparedness. Employers similarly rated graduates as well prepared and reported positive contributions to organizational safety practices. CE participants rated courses highly for quality, relevance, and practical applicability. Respondents consistently emphasized the importance of applied learning, experiential training opportunities, and alignment between academic preparation and workforce needs. CONCLUSION: Findings highlight the DSC's role in strengthening the regional OSH workforce through integrated graduate education and CE programming. Stakeholders emphasized continued emphasis on experiential learning, flexible delivery modalities, and enhanced research-to-practice translation. Ongoing refinement of programming in response to workforce feedback may further improve preparedness, accessibility, and occupational safety outcomes.

Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative responses were examined using deductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: A total of 297 stakeholders responded.

papers.title: Imbalance and transition: a textual analysis of 125 ecological restoration policy documents in the Yangtze River Basin
papers.abstract: The Yangtze River Basin is central to China’s socio-economic development. Its ecological restoration is key to regional ecological security, sustainable economic and social progress, and national strategic implementation. By establishing a three-dimensional framework encompassing policy tools, themes, and development stages, this study conducts a quantitative text analysis of 125 central and provincial policy documents (comprising 349 policy clauses) to systematically examine the patterns and evolutionary characteristics of the Yangtze River Basin’s ecological restoration framework. The findings show an uneven distribution in the use of policy tools and themes: environmental-oriented tools dominated (65.62%), while Planning for Ecological Conservation and Restoration was the most frequent theme (57.60%), and public participation and industrial integration remained marginal. Across development stages (slow: 2001–2015; rapid: 2016–2020; flourishing: 2021–2024), the policy mix shifted. From the rapid development stage (2016–2020) to the flourishing development stage (2021–2024), the combined share of supply- and demand-oriented tools increased from 33.33% to 34.59%. As a text-based analysis, this study focuses on policy design features and stage transitions, offering insights for sustainable policy formulation and methodological guidance for future research in related fields.

papers.title: Surface Fluorination of LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 by Fluoropolymer Thermal Decomposition: From Reactive Gas Speciation to Electrochemical Stabilization
papers.abstract: Abstract Surface fluorination is an effective strategy to stabilize high-voltage LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO) cathodes against interfacial degradation, yet the role of the fluorinating agent and its decomposition pathway in governing surface speciation remains poorly understood. Here, PTFE and CYTOP are investigated as solid fluoropolymer-derived fluorinating agents for LNMO surface modification via thermal decomposition under inert atmosphere, yielding comparable surface fluorine contents of approximately 0.08 mmol g–1 for both treatments. X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy confirm that both treatments preserve the cubic spinel framework, indicating that fluorination is confined to the particle surface. XPS reveals the formation of LiF-like species, M–F bonds and manganese oxyfluoride-like environments, while EPR reveals modifications of the manganese electronic environment after treatment. Galvanostatic cycling over 100 cycles at C/10 demonstrates improved capacity retention for both fluorinated samples: all three electrodes deliver an initial discharge capacity close to 143 mAh g–1. After 100 cycles, LNMO–PTFE retains 95% of its initial discharge capacity (136 mAh g–1), compared to 91% for LNMO–CYTOP and 90% for pristine LNMO (∼128 mAh g–1). TGA-MS and in situ gas-phase FTIR identify the reactive species generated during decomposition: PTFE mainly releases :CF2, •CF, •C2F3 and •CF3 fragments, whereas CYTOP produces a broader distribution of fluorinated species over a wider temperature range. These differences in decomposition chemistry directly control the nature of the fluorinated interphase and the resulting electrochemical stabilization of LNMO. This work establishes mechanistic guidelines for designing scalable fluoropolymer-based surface treatments for high-voltage cathode materials, as an alternative to reactive fluorine sources such as F2 or XeF2.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT OF THERMOSTABLE EDIBLE PACKAGING MATERIALS BASED ON STARCH–PROTEIN COMPOSITES FOR HOT FOOD APPLICATIONS: A CRITICAL REVIEW
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: This narrative review critically examines starch–protein edible composites as potential packaging materials for hot meals, with particular emphasis on thermal transitions, wet-state mechanical integrity, water resistance, processing routes and food-contact safety. The analysis integrates peer-reviewed literature on starch-based films, starch–protein compatibility, plasticizer selection and recent modification strategies. A central distinction is made between thermal stability measured by differential scanning calorimetry or thermogravimetry and practical serviceability during contact with hot, aqueous and fatty foods. Protein blending can improve cohesion and modify film barriers, but the outcome depends on protein chemistry, pH, blend ratio, plasticizer content and processing history. Available evidence supports formulation optimization and application-specific testing rather than a general claim that edible starch–protein packaging is already suitable for all hot meals. A validation framework combining thermal, mechanical, moisture, migration, sensory and microbiological measurements is proposed.

papers.title: Two-Timescale Modelling of a Single-Inductor Dual-Input DC-DC Converter: Power Sharing, Output Ripple and Stability of the Averaged Plant
papers.journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.abstract: A single-inductor dual-input single-output (DISO) DC-DC converter shares one inductor between two sources by timedivision scheduling. When the sources lie on opposite sides of the regulated output, the converter alternates between step-down and step-up operation within every scheduling frame. This paper develops a two-timescale model in which the switching-periodaveraged models of the two modes are combined over the frame. The model gives closed-form relations for the delivery ratio that sets the required inductor current, the power share produced by a given time allocation, the quantisation of that allocation by the digital control period, and the output ripple on the frame and switching timescales. For fixed duties and positive parameters, the continuous-conduction frame-averaged model is globally exponentially stable about its unique equilibrium. For a 14.3 V / 5.0 V to 6.7 V converter with a 250 µs frame, a 70 % time allocation gives a 76.35 % power share. In 75 controller-free simulations spanning allocation, load and scheduling period, the relations predicted the mean inductor current within 0.0113 % and the power share within 0.0555 %, and the frame-rate ripple within 4.7 %, in every case slightly overestimating it. A switched model confirms the frame-rate ripple of the switching-period-averaged output and shows that the instantaneous terminal voltage carries an additional switching-frequency step of about ܴ௘௦௥·݅௅ during step-up intervals, which raises its peak-to-peak ripple by a factor of 2.5–2.8

papers.title: Comprehensive Study on Spontaneous Combustion Risk of Pyrite and Pyrrhotite Based on Thermal Analysis Kinetics and Phase Evolution
papers.abstract: The oxidation characteristics and spontaneous combustion propensity of pyrite and pyrrhotite are investigated using TG–DSC, FWO/KAS/Friedman kinetic analysis, XRD, and FactSage simulation. Both minerals exhibit intense exothermic events between 400°C and 650°C. Their peak temperatures shift to higher values and their exothermic enthalpies increase significantly with heating rate. The average apparent activation energies of pyrite, at 134.3 kJ/mol by FWO, 129.4 kJ/mol by KAS, and 136.7 kJ/mol by Friedman, are consistently lower than those of pyrrhotite, at 140.9 kJ/mol, 135.6 kJ/mol, and 142.2 kJ/mol, respectively, indicating a higher oxidation propensity for pyrite. Semi-quantitative XRD analysis using the RIR method reveals that Fe2O3 forms at 350°C for pyrite, with a content of 1.73 wt%. For pyrrhotite, the Fe2O3 content is 4.57 wt% at 350°C and 5.93 wt% at 400°C. A quantitative comparison between XRD-RIR measurements and FactSage simulations shows that the lower oxide‑formation temperature of pyrite is consistent with its lower activation energy. This suggests that oxide-formation temperature can serve as a supplementary indicator for evaluating spontaneous combustion susceptibility. These findings have practical implications for enhancing mine safety, predicting spontaneous combustion, improving ore storage management, and supporting industrial risk assessment.

papers.abstract: Quercetin dihydrate, a naturally occurring flavonoid, has attracted considerable attention due to its extensive pharmacological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities.It is plentifully present in dietary sources such as onions, apples, berries, and grapes.It exhibits stronger antioxidant activity in comparison to vitamin C and E, due to its potent free radical scavenging ability.It neutralizes reactive oxygen species and protects the cells from oxidative stress-induced damage.Furthermore, quercetin has demonstrated promising anticancer activity through the inhibition of cancer cell proliferation, induction of apoptosis, and modulation of multiple cellular signaling pathways, including NF-kB, MAPK, and PI3K/AKT pathways.This review highlights recent advances in analytical approaches for the identification, characterization, and quantification of quercetin dihydrate, with particular emphasis on validated HPLC and reverse-phase HPLC methods coupled with diode array and UV detection systems.Critically validated parameters such as linearity, precision, accuracy, robustness, ruggedness, selectivity, sensitivity, and stability have been comprehensively evaluated.

papers.title: Development of an FTIR-DSC-based quantification method for component ratio determination in ABS/PC polymer blends
papers.journal: International Journal of Polymer Analysis and Characterization
papers.abstract: Due to the distinct properties of both components constituting Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene/Polycarbonate (ABS/PC) polymer blends, the ratio of the polymers in the blend significantly impacts the characteristics of the final product. Furthermore, the taxation of ABS/PC polymer blends in commercial circulation is determined based on these blend ratios. In this study, a preliminary quantitative analytical method was developed to determine polymer ratios in ABS/PC blends, intended for industrial quality control and customs taxation. The developed method was established based on Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) analytical data. Within the scope of the study, granular ABS and PC polymers were mixed at various ratios using a twin-screw extruder to prepare a total of six polymer blends. FTIR and DSC analyses were performed on the produced samples. In the FTIR analysis, the height and area values of specific polymer peaks were examined, while in the DSC analysis, the glass transition temperatures and changes in heat capacity were evaluated. The statistical results highlighted a significant relationship between the polymer blend ratios and the combined data from FTIR and DSC parameters. Although both linear and non-linear regression models were initially developed, the non-linear equations were found to provide a better fit. Given their higher determination coefficients (R2 > 0.99) and capacity to handle the complex structure of the data compared to linear approximations, these equations were adopted as the primary calculation method.

papers.title: Resination-Assembled Soft Multiaxial Molecular Ferroelectrics Enable Exceptional Low-Electric Field Polarization Switching
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Resination of soft polymer ferroelectrics has recently emerged as a promising avenue to assemble high- performance electroactive materials, due to the coupling of ferroelectricity with enhanced mechanical and processable merits. However, it remains a huge challenge to stabilize ferroelectricity and dipolar activity at the resin–ferroelectric interface. For the first time, we adopt here the resination assembling strategy into the soft molecule-based ferroelectric (BZA)2(DMA)BiI6 (1, BZA = benzylammonium; DMA = dimethylammonium), which enables the unusual ferroelectric behavior of low-electric field switching of polarization. Compound 1 is a high-temperature multiaxial ferroelectric with six possible equivalent polarization directions and a low coercive electric field, arising from its stepwise phase transitions around 350 K (Tc). Strikingly, the precise resination of 1 with the epoxy-matrix composite yields a highly loaded composite with a microscopic cross-linked structure, whose polarization can be switched under a quite low coercive electric field (Ec ∼ 3.8 kV/cm). These shape-customized ferroelectric resin wafers of 1 have superior antielectric fatigue attributes after ∼104 cycles. Moreover, these wafers exhibit enhanced resistance to localized deformation, evidenced by a 30.9% decrease in maximum penetration depth relative to the bulk single crystals. As the first study on the resination of molecular ferroelectrics, our findings bridge the gap between molecular ferroelectrics and material engineering, which highlights the application potential of resinated molecular ferroelectrics.

papers.title: Tuning the Screening Effect on Optical Properties of Flexible PVA Films via the Synergistic Incorporation of Nano-La2CuO4, Electrolytic LiClO4, and Varied Plasticizer PC Content
papers.abstract: Abstract The development of flexible, leakage-free solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) represents a critical milestone for the societal transition toward sustainable, high-safety portable electronics and smart optical displays. This work addresses this need through the novel fabrication of flexible nanocomposite membranes via a streamlined solution-casting approach, uniquely achieving precision tuning of the electronic screening effect within a host poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) matrix. The PVA matrix incorporates 2 wt % La2CuO4 nanoparticles (verified at 80–120 nm via TEM), 10 wt % LiClO4 electrolytic salt, and varying fractions (2 to 8 wt %) of propylene carbonate (PC) plasticizer. FTIR spectroscopy confirmed robust complexation, showing systematic red shifts (downshifts) in the host matrix O–H (∼21 cm–1) and C═O (∼10 cm–1) stretching bands, driven by extensive ion-dipole coordination networks. SEM and XRD analyses indicated a highly amorphous microstructure within the plasticized matrices. DSC thermograms verified superior film flexibility, with the glass transition temperature (Tg) systematically dropping from ∼98 °C to ∼66 °C. Optical metrics revealed that the direct optical bandgap (Eg) was nonlinearly tuned, initially decreasing from 5.22 eV (pure PVA) to 3.29 eV at 2 wt % PC, and subsequently expanding to 3.79 eV up to 8 wt % PC due to a prominent screening/capping effect. Concurrently, the refractive index at 250 nm systematically shifted from 1.78 to 3.00, while the optimal 2 wt % PC loading yielded a peak optical conductivity of 8.11 × 1011 s–1. These data-driven findings confirm that this tunable composite matrix bridges the gap between film flexibility and precise optoelectronic modulation.
