papers.title: Dynamic performance enhancement of a three-phase interleaved resonant boost MMC using adaptive disturbance compensation
papers.abstract: Offshore wind energy is emerging as a critical renewable energy source. For the three-phase interleaved resonant boost MMC considered in this study, load variations, input-voltage fluctuations, and modeling uncertainties may degrade output-voltage regulation performance. To improve the transient response and disturbance-rejection capability of the converter, a backstepping dynamic surface control strategy assisted by a Zernike neural-network-based adaptive compensator is proposed. First, a state-space model of the three-phase interleaved parallel MMC boost converter is established. Then, the Zernike neural network is employed to adaptively approximate the unknown load-dependent term in the output-voltage dynamics and generate an online compensation signal. with a compact basis-function structure compared with the conventional RBF neural network used for comparison. Meanwhile, DSC is incorporated into the backstepping framework to avoid the derivative explosion problem and reduce implementation complexity. Lyapunov analysis proves that all closed-loop signals are bounded and the tracking error is semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. The inherent low-ripple and self-balancing characteristics of the topology are validated before the dynamic control performance is investigated. The proposed method achieves smaller overshoot and requires less execution time than the RBF-NN-assisted ABDSC under the adopted implementation settings. Therefore, the proposed strategy provides a preliminary methodological reference for improving the dynamic performance of MMC-based converters, with potential relevance to future offshore wind power HVDC applications.

papers.title: Untargeted metabolomics and antioxidant responses reveal tissue- and species-specific metabolic profiles in three Epimedium species
papers.abstract: Objectives This study systematically analyzed the antioxidant responses, untargeted metabolomic profiles, and secondary metabolic pathways of three representative Epimedium species. Methods Meteorological data (atmospheric pressure, temperature, relative humidity, and precipitation) were recorded from July 2022 to July 2025 to provide environmental background context. Antioxidant indexes including H 2 O 2 and O 2 - levels, as well as CAT, POD and SOD activities in different plant tissues were determined. Untargeted metabolomics was performed to explore metabolic differences. PCA, differential metabolite analysis, KEGG and MSEA enrichment were conducted to screen key metabolic pathways, and correlation analysis was employed to explore exploratory associations between antioxidant enzyme activities and secondary metabolite abundances. Results The levels of H 2 O 2 and O 2 - were generally higher in roots than in stems and leaves. CAT activity showed no significant differences among tissues or species, whereas POD and SOD activities presented distinct tissue-specific and species-specific patterns. A total of 2730 MS features were detected. PCA and differential metabolite analysis revealed remarkable metabolic separation and diverse metabolite changes among the three Epimedium species. KEGG and MSEA enrichment indicated that differential metabolites were mainly involved in phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, flavonoid biosynthesis, galactose metabolism and so on. 46 MS features were putatively annotated at the compound level (MSI Level 2 or 3) via MS/MS fragment interpretation and literature evidence. Correlation analysis was performed to explore the associations between antioxidant enzymes and key secondary metabolites. Conclusions The three Epimedium species exhibit distinct antioxidant characteristics and metabolic profiles under the local meteorological environment. Tissue-specific and species-specific differences are mainly concentrated in phenylpropanoid and flavonoid metabolism, with potential associations observed between these metabolites and the antioxidant system. These results provide descriptive insights into the physiological characteristics and quality formation of Epimedium species.

These results provide descriptive insights into the physiological characteristics and quality formation of Epimedium species.

papers.title: Binding of Zinc(II) to Apo‐Metallo‐β‐Lactamases: Characterization by Isothermal Titration Calorimetry
papers.abstract: Antibiotic resistance caused by metallo‐β‐lactamases (MβLs) is a global public health threat. In this work, we first directly investigated the binding of Zn 2+ to apo‐MβLs through isothermal titration calorimetry. It was found that carbapenem and cephamycin resistance metallo‐β‐lactamase (CcrA), New Delhi metallo‐β‐lactamase‐1 (NDM‐1) and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Metallo‐β‐lactamase‐1(L1) bind Zn 2+ in a sequential mode, while imipenemase‐1 (IMP‐1) and Verona Integron‐encoded metallo‐β‐lactamase‐2 (VIM‐2) bind Zn 2+ in a mode of varying levels of cooperativity, in which the mononuclear species was not detectable, and also, the mode was verified through the titration of Co 2+ into apo‐VIM‐2 monitored by UV–vis. The thermodynamic and kinetic parameters revealed the binding of Zn 2+ to the active sites was independent of stoichiometry. Analysis of the parameters determined suggested that the binding of B1 and B3 MβLs to Zn 2+ depends on the binding affinity and/or Gibbs free energy change of Zn 1 and Zn 2 sites of the enzymes, and two metal sites have almost equal contributions for full activity of the MβLs. The information gained in this work is helpful for the further mechanism studies and the development of the broad‐spectrum MβL inhibitors.

papers.title: Effects of Two Different Synthetic Wollastonite Microfibers Produced with Natural and Waste Raw Materials on Engineered Geopolymer Composites
papers.journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract This study covers the effects of two different synthetic wollastonite microfibers (SWMs) on the properties of engineered geopolymer composites (EGCs) developed with fly ash (FA) and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS). Firstly, SWMs with two different maximum aspect ratios ( 44 ∶ 1 and 12 ∶ 1 ) were produced by using different SiO 2 sources [silica powder and silica fume (SF)] with the specific production process in the laboratory. SWM with a maximum aspect ratio of 44 ∶ 1 had a high proportion of the needle-shaped particles while SWM with a maximum aspect ratio of 12 ∶ 1 had the rare acicular particles. These microfibers were then used at 3, 6, and 9 wt% in place of FA in FA + GGBFS - based EGC. As a results of characteristics tests, it can be concluded that both SWMs increased the bearing strength and deformation capacity of the EGC by up to 6% of replacement level. The incorporation of 6% SWM with a higher aspect ratio increased the 28 day compressive strength, flexural strength, and midspan beam deflection of the EGCs by 11.2%, 6.5%, and 42.6%, respectively, whereas for the SWM with a lower aspect ratio, these improvements were 4.4%, 3.6%, and 8.2%, respectively. Moreover, the presence of wollastonite in the system was confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, while thermogravimetric analysis/differential thermal analysis (TGA/DTA) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) analyses validated the mechanisms responsible for the observed enhancement in mechanical performance. Accordingly, the improvement in mechanical performance of SWM-incorporated EGCs is governed by physical and micromechanical mechanisms, notably crack-bridging efficiency, interfacial bonding, and aspect-ratio-dependent stress transfer rather than by chemical contributions to geopolymerization. Consequently, SWMs with higher aspect ratios and denser acicular particle structures enhanced remarkably the mechanical performance of the EGCs.

papers.title: Micronization-assisted pulsed electric field treatment on functional and structural modification of red pepper seed protein isolates
papers.abstract: Background Red pepper seeds are an underutilized source of plant proteins with functional potential, but their poor solubility and limited functionality restrict food applications. This study investigated the effects of micronization-assisted pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment on the structural, physicochemical, and functional properties of red pepper seed protein isolates (RPSPIs). Methods RPSPIs were subjected to micronization pretreatment followed by PEF treatment under different electric field strengths and processing conditions. The effects of combined treatment on surface hydrophobicity, turbidity, Free Sulfhydryl (SH) Content, particle size distribution, surface morphology, secondary conformation, thermal stability, solubility, emulsifying properties, and foaming characteristics were systematically evaluated. Structural modifications were characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), fluorescence spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Results The combined treatment significantly impacted the functional properties, including zeta potential and particle size of RPSPI-treated samples, enhancing stability compared to control samples. The structural data revealed important molecular modifications, including enhanced SH − content and reduced fluorescence intensity, suggesting that the structure partially unfolded. In addition, FTIR analysis combined with Amide I deconvolution demonstrated that MR and PEF treatments significantly altered the secondary structure composition of RPSPI, with changes in α-helix, β-sheet, β-turn, and random coil components. The combined MR-PEF treatment promoted greater protein conformational rearrangement, which was associated with improved dispersion behavior, and enhanced functional properties. SEM micrographs revealed significant changes and fragmentation, further supporting our findings. The XRD analysis revealed changes in crystalline structure and crystallinity, while DSC results demonstrated increased denaturation temperatures after treatment, indicating enhanced thermal stability of RPSPI. The combined treatments also had significant impacts on these structural changes, enhancing foaming capacity, solubility, and emulsifying properties and decreasing turbidity. Conclusion This study's findings add value to red pepper seed by-product and provide insight into novel processing methods for high-value plant protein components.

papers.title: The Carnivore Diet and Cardiovascular Disease Risk: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: The carnivore diet consists of meat, fish, eggs, and animal fats, and excludes all plant-based foods. Controlled prospective studies have not evaluated the implications of the carnivore diet for cardiovascular safety, and the existing evidence base remains limited in quality and scope. This narrative review evaluated the scientific literature on the carnivore diet to assess nutrient adequacy, metabolic effects, and alignment with established dietary guidelines for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention. We searched PubMed and Google Scholar through April 2026. Eligible studies included modeling research, surveys, case reports, and reviews of carnivore diets; findings from ketogenic and low-carbohydrate diets were drawn upon extensively, given the absence of carnivore-specific trial data. Carnivore diets provide high intakes of saturated fat, cholesterol, sodium, heme iron, and protein and lack fiber and essential nutrients such as folate, vitamin C, magnesium, and potassium. Reported short-term benefits (e.g., improved glycemic control, weight loss, and elevated HDL-cholesterol) are derived primarily from self-reported survey data and case reports, and are therefore highly susceptible to selection, recall, and reporting biases, alongside the absence of objective clinical verification. Significant elevations in total and LDL-cholesterol were also documented. The carnivore diet is inconsistent with public health guidelines recommending plant-based dietary patterns for CVD risk reduction, and current evidence does not support its long-term safety. Based on currently available evidence, the carnivore diet cannot be considered a heart-healthy eating pattern; however, well-designed prospective trials are needed to definitively characterize its long-term cardiovascular effects.

papers.title: Acoustic emission multi-parameter characterization of seismic damage evolution for different double skin composite shear walls
papers.abstract: Double skin composite (DSC) shear walls have recently gained increasing attention as an emerging structural system for high-rise buildings; however, their seismic damage evolution and performance degradation mechanisms under earthquake excitations remain insufficiently understood. This study comparatively investigates conventional and enhanced DSC shear walls through acoustic emission (AE) monitoring and proposes a multi-parameter framework for damage characterization and damage-state assessment. Results show that geometric asymmetry induces pronounced asymmetric hysteretic responses. Failure evolves from buckling of steel-concrete columns to core concrete crushing and final tensile fracture of steel plates, indicating a progressive ductile-to-brittle transition. AE features reveal a clear transition from dispersed minor damage to localized severe damage in different DSC shear walls. Strong correlations among energy-related parameters indicate consistent AE intensity responses during damage development. Peak frequency, historical index (HI), and severity value (S r ) and normalized AE activity indicate that the web wall makes a greater contribution to global damage accumulation, with failure concentrated near its base. RA-AF analysis indicates a dominant tensile-cracking tendency, with tensile AE events accounting for approximately 80%; increased web-end CFST steel tube thickness may enhance confinement and help mitigate brittle tensile failure. These findings provide new insights into the multi-scale damage evolution and failure mechanisms of DSC shear walls, with implications for seismic performance evaluation and future AE-based damage-state assessment of steel-concrete composite structures.

papers.title: Semi-analytical investigation of fin configuration effects on PCM solidification in cylindrical thermal energy storage systems
papers.abstract: Thermal energy storage systems (TES) employing phase change materials (PCMs) are often constrained by the inherently low thermal conductivity of PCMs, resulting in slow heat transfer and prolonged charging and discharging processes. This study investigates the influence of fin configuration and fin number on the solidification behavior of PCMs in TES systems using a semi-analytical model based on Green’s function and the Megerlin method. The proposed framework predicts the evolution of the solidification front under different thermal boundary conditions while providing a computationally efficient alternative to conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. The thermal performances of radial and longitudinal fin configurations are systematically compared to identify the most effective design for accelerating solidification. The results demonstrate that fin geometry has a greater influence on heat transfer enhancement than simply increasing the fin surface area. Among the investigated configurations, the two-radial-fin arrangement reduces the total solidification time by 21.38% compared with the unfinned tank and achieves an additional 12.37% reduction relative to the longitudinal-fin configuration. Moreover, the predicted solidification contours show that radial fins promote more effective heat extraction and suppress the formation of large unsolidified liquid regions. The proposed semi-analytical framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient tool for analyzing PCM solidification and offers practical design guidelines for optimizing fin configurations in high-performance LHTES systems.

The results demonstrate that fin geometry has a greater influence on heat transfer enhancement than simply increasing the fin surface area.

papers.title: Multiscale Physicochemical Response of Lignocellulosic Carludovica palmata Fibers to Controlled Drying and Alkaline Hydrogen Peroxide Treatment
papers.abstract: Processing can alter the optical, structural, spectroscopic, morphological, and thermal characteristics of lignocellulosic fibers in different ways. Five measured states of Carludovica palmata were compared: an artisan-processed reference (PJ-0), water-conditioned fibers dried for 1 h at 84 and 104 ∘C (SPJ-84 and SPJ-104), and SPJ-104 fibers treated with two nominal alkaline hydrogen peroxide formulations (BPJ-3% and BPJ-6%). Relative image-based color analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) coupled with fractal, multifractal, orientation, and spatial-texture analyses, and TGA/DTG were integrated within the same processing series. The BPJ-3% and BPJ-6% images showed similar measured appearance in the relative image-based color analysis, with a pairwise ΔE00=1.7, whereas their selected SEM fields differed in directional and boundary organization. The selected BPJ-3% field showed higher axial anisotropy (A=0.2835) than BPJ-6% (A=0.1183), while the selected BPJ-6% field showed DB=1.5570 and a singularity-spectrum width of Δα=1.3444. In the individual XRD profiles, BPJ-3% showed higher apparent Scherrer and Segal descriptors than BPJ-6%, whereas the individual BPJ-6% TGA/DTG profile showed the highest principal degradation-rate temperature of the series (Tmax=322.6∘C). Because the principal physicochemical series contained one independent specimen per condition and one SEM, XRD, and TGA/DTG measurement set per condition, these numerical differences are interpreted as specimen-level observations rather than reproducible treatment-level effects. The study therefore provides an integrated multiscale description of the measured fiber states while explicitly delimiting the level of inference supported by the experimental design.

The selected BPJ-3% field showed higher axial anisotropy (A=0.2835) than BPJ-6% (A=0.1183), while the selected BPJ-6% field showed DB=1.5570 and a singularity-spectrum width of Δα=1.3444. In the individual XRD profiles, BPJ-3% showed higher apparent Scherrer and Segal descriptors than BPJ-6%, whereas the individual BPJ-6% TGA/DTG profile showed the highest principal degradation-rate temperature of the series (Tmax=322.6∘C).

papers.title: Deep Multimodal Fusion of Thermal and Visible Images for Emotion Interpretation
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Emotion recognition plays a crucial role in affective computing and human-computer interaction, enabling intelligent systems to understand and respond to human emotional states.Conventional emotion recognition approaches primarily rely on visible-light facial images; however, their performance is significantly affected by variations in illumination, occlusion, and low-light conditions.Thermal imaging offers a complementary modality by capturing physiological changes such as blood flow and temperature variations associated with emotional responses, and it remains robust under challenging environmental conditions.This study explores emotion interpretation using fused thermal and visible facial images through deep learning techniques.A multimodal framework employing dual-stream convolutional neural networks is discussed, where modality-specific features are extracted independently and fused at the feature level to enhance discriminative capability.Various fusion strategies, including early, mid-level, and late fusion, are analyzed to highlight their effectiveness in improving recognition accuracy.The integration of thermal and visible modalities demonstrates improved robustness, particularly for subtle and negative emotions.The findings emphasize that multimodal deep learning-based fusion provides a reliable and scalable solution for emotion interpretation, with promising applications in healthcare, automotive safety, surveillance, and human-robot interaction.

papers.title: Thermo-Oxidative Ageing Mechanisms in Polypropylene–Xylite Composites: A Multiscale Analysis of Surface, Structural, and Mechanical Degradation
papers.abstract: This study investigates the accelerated ageing behaviour of isotactic polypropylene (iPP) composites containing 10 and 25 wt.% xylite using a multiscale approach combining water sorption, contact angle and surface free energy measurements, DSC, WAXS, FTIR, SEM, and mechanical testing. Xylite incorporation significantly modified the surface and structural response of iPP during ageing. Although the composites initially exhibited increased hydrophobicity and a lower polar contribution to the surface free energy, exposure for up to 1000 h progressively altered their wetting behaviour. Xylite-containing composites also showed higher long-term water uptake than neat iPP, particularly at 25 wt.% filler content, indicating increased contributions from filler accessibility, interfacial pathways, and ageing-induced microstructural changes. DSC and WAXS revealed a complex evolution of the semicrystalline iPP matrix, indicating that oxidative degradation occurs concurrently with crystalline reorganization. These structural changes were reflected in the mechanical response, with xylite-containing composites showing greater retention of mechanical stability during prolonged ageing than neat iPP. SEM observations further confirmed progressive surface and interfacial deterioration. Overall, the results demonstrate that xylite modifies the ageing pathway of iPP through coupled surface, structural, moisture-related, and interfacial processes. The multiscale analysis highlights filler content as a key factor controlling the balance between structural reorganization and ageing-induced damage in iPP–xylite composites.

These structural changes were reflected in the mechanical response, with xylite-containing composites showing greater retention of mechanical stability during prolonged ageing than neat iPP. papers.title: First-principles study on the interfacial activation of peracetic acid over bimetallic 3d-TM@N-CNTs for triclosan degradation
papers.abstract: Advanced oxidation technologies based on peracetic acid (PAA) have attracted widespread attention in the field of water pollution treatment. However, the development of highly efficient and stable PAA activation catalysts remains a challenge. This study employed first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations to systematically investigate the adsorption and activation properties of PAA by ten types of 3d transition metal-doped nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (3d-TM@N-CNTs). Five candidate metals (V, Cr, Mn, Fe, and Co) with moderate adsorption strengths were screened from single-atom catalysts (SACs). Structural optimization revealed that PAA undergoes molecular adsorption on Ni/Cu/Zn@CNTs, but dissociative adsorption on all other SACs and DSCs. Twenty dual-site catalysts (DSCs) were constructed to evaluate the effects of two nitrogen coordination configurations (a: M 1 M 2 –N 6 shared-coordination cage, b: MN 4 /M′N 4 adjacent independent coordination) on PAA adsorption. Bimetallic synergistic effects significantly enhanced PAA adsorption compared to SACs. To examine the product desorption behavior, the ·OH desorption energies were calculated, ranging from −0.56 to 4.60 eV. CrFe(a) (Δ E ads = −4.34 eV, Δ E des = 0.99 eV), MnCo(b) (−4.14 eV, 1.28 eV), and VCo(b) (−4.24 eV, 1.38 eV) were identified as the promising candidates, achieving a balance between PAA activation and product release. Bader charge analysis and difference charge density revealed that the mechanism of bimetallic sites was categorized into concerted activation and main-auxiliary synergy. Co-adsorption calculations confirmed that PAA and TCS can stably coexist on the dual-metal site, with PAA preferentially occupying the active site for activation. This work establishes a catalyst–PAA–ROS–TCS mechanistic link and provides theoretical guidance for the rational design of PAA activation catalysts in water treatment applications.
papers.summary: Advanced oxidation technologies based on peracetic acid (PAA) have attracted widespread attention in the field of water pollution treatment. Bader charge analysis and difference charge density revealed that the mechanism of bimetallic sites was categorized into concerted activation and main-auxiliary synergy. This work establishes a catalyst–PAA–ROS–TCS mechanistic link and provides theoretical guidance for the rational design of PAA activation catalysts in water treatment applications.

papers.title: Pullout Behavior and Interfacial Properties of Cementitious Composites with Graphene Oxide-Treated Polymer Fibers
papers.abstract: Poor fiber–matrix interfacial adhesion limits the mechanical performance of synthetic fiber-reinforced cementitious composites. To overcome this limitation, this study investigates the impact of surface-treating polypropylene (PP) macrofibers with graphene oxide (GO) on single-fiber pullout behavior. The thermal and structural response of the treated fibers was characterized using Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), and mechanical performance within the cementitious matrix was quantified. DSC analyses revealed changes in the thermal response of the polymer surface caused by the coating. In pullout tests, surface modification with GO resulted in higher resistance values at specific displacement levels, fR0.5 and fR3.5, showing increases of 20% and 18%, respectively. It is concluded that the GO coating effectively acts as an interfacial anchoring agent, optimizing interfacial shear transfer and enhancing the composite’s energy dissipation capacity in cementitious structures.

papers.title: Organic Electrodes With Excellent Rate Capability and Cycling Stability Enabled by Assembling Active Materials onto Conductive Agents
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic redox compounds represent a class of alternative electrode materials for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) that are free of transition metals and completely biodegradable, with high molecular tunability, environmental benignity, and economic affordability. However, to realize this promise in practical devices, organic electrode materials (OEMs) must overcome low rate capability and poor cycling stability stemming from their intrinsically low electronic conductivity and pronounced solubility in organic solvents. Herein, we demonstrate an integrated strategy of embedding OEMs within conductive networks to simultaneously resolve these challenges. Using lithium terephthalate (LTP) as a model system, we assembled it on the conductive agent Super P (SP), the resulting composite delivers an impressive capacity of 104 mAh g −1 at a demanding 5C rate and retains 130 mAh g −1 after 1000 cycles at 1C, significantly outperforming its physically mixed counterpart, which delivers merely 25 mAh g −1 at 5C and rapidly fades to 56 mAh g −1 under identical cycling conditions. These exceptional electrochemical properties originate from the intimate interaction between the active LTP and the conductive SP network, which not only creates robust electronic pathways to access the potential capacities but also effectively prevents LTP dissolution in electrolytes during prolonged cycling.

papers.title: Hybrid photovoltaic–thermoelectric generator renewable energy systems-a comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
papers.abstract: Advancing renewable energy sources is crucial to meeting the growing energy demand. Solar energy conversion systems, such as photovoltaic (PV) cells and thermoelectric generators (TEG), play a significant role in addressing this need. PV systems primarily convert visible and ultraviolet (UV) light from sunlight, while TEGs utilize the infrared (IR) spectrum to generate electrical energy. Combining PV systems with TEGs allows for more comprehensive utilization of the solar spectrum, resulting in improved energy production. Recent research has focused on PV/TEGs hybrid generation systems (HGSs) to boost conversion efficiency. By harnessing the heat released from the PV system, TEGs can enhance the hybrid system’s overall power output and efficiency, potentially leading to superior performance. However, integrating these systems presents challenges due to their differing characteristics. This review aims to explain the fundamental principles of PV and thermoelectric generators, analyze recent research findings in enhancing this hybrid system’s performance, and explore various approaches to optimizing the performance of these hybrid systems. In sum, a review of previous works shows compelling evidence for integration between PV and TEG. For instance, previous works have demonstrated overall efficiency gains of 7.33%–32.09%. Furthermore, reported results confirm that TEG integration can reduce PV operating temperature while generating additional power from waste heat. An assessment of a PV-TEG system using real-world data reveals a 6% improvement in energy output compared to standalone PV systems. In addition, the phase change material can mitigate fluctuating solar irradiation, resulting in an enhancement of daily overall efficiency 25.55%–26.57%.
papers.summary: Advancing renewable energy sources is crucial to meeting the growing energy demand. This review aims to explain the fundamental principles of PV and thermoelectric generators, analyze recent research findings in enhancing this hybrid system’s performance, and explore various approaches to optimizing the performance of these hybrid systems. An assessment of a PV-TEG system using real-world data reveals a 6% improvement in energy output compared to standalone PV systems.

papers.title: Mechanical Properties and Volatile Pollutants Absorbing Capacity of Mortar Composites with Addition of Coconut Shell Activated Carbon and Gamal Wood Chips Aggregates
papers.abstract: The use of biomass has the potential to improve the mechanical characteristics of cement-based composites. Activated carbon is considered competitive in absorbing hazardous pollutants in the air, is able to reduce cracking and increase the mechanical strength of cement-based composites. The addition of gamal wood chips also has the potential to increase flexibility in mortar composites. The purpose of this study was to analyze the characteristics of the mechanical properties and pollutant absorption capacity of mortar composites with the addition of activated carbon and gamal wood chips. In this study, activated carbon is used as a fine aggregate (filler) with an addition of 1-5% to the weight of cement. Gamal wood chips are used as much as 1.5% of the total weight. Composite brick testing includes density, compressive strength, modulus of elasticity (MOE), modulus of rupture (MOR), adsorption capacity for ammonia, benzene, chloroform, and formaldehyde and thermal analysis of Field Emission Electron Microscopes (FE-SEM) and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The density of composite mortar with the addition of activated carbon and gamal wood chips ranges from 1950.36±19.54-2137.24±45.09 kg/m3, compressive strength 8.48±0.76-9.71±1.68 MPa, MOE 421.74±69.59 -645.58±57.51 MPa, MOR 2.14±0.27-2.75±0.20 MPa. The composite mortar exhibited a total pollutant absorption rate of less than 3% for all tested parameters. The addition of activated carbon up to 4% can increase the mechanical strength and pollutant absorption capacity and can produce more CaCO3 in composite bricks. Morphological observations as analyzed by FE-SEM, were found to correlate with FTIR analysis, namely the formation of CaCO3. The following method produces an environmentally friendly mortar composite that performs exceptionally well and has a lot of potential for use in sustainable building.
papers.summary: The use of biomass has the potential to improve the mechanical characteristics of cement-based composites. Morphological observations as analyzed by FE-SEM, were found to correlate with FTIR analysis, namely the formation of CaCO3. The following method produces an environmentally friendly mortar composite that performs exceptionally well and has a lot of potential for use in sustainable building.

papers.title: Photopolymerization Kinetics and Improved Performances of Polyacrylate-Type Semi-interpenetrating Solid Polymer Electrolytes
papers.abstract: Abstract Crosslinking solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are expected to expedite the extensive application of lithium metal batteries (LMBs) by enabling appropriate ionic conductivity and good compatibility with the cathode. However, researchers tend to focus more on the performance of SPEs themselves, rather than delving deeply into the mechanisms by which the kinetic characteristics of random polymerization reactions influence SPE properties. In this work, semi-interpenetrating (semi-IPN) SPEs are fabricated by crosslinking poly(ethylene glycol) methacrylate (PEGMA) and poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) blended with lithium perchlorate under UV irradiation in the presence of 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropiophenone as the photoinitiator. By varying the number average molecular weights (Mn) of PEGMA (Mn = 300, 475, or 950 g mol–1) and PEGDA (Mn = 200, 400, 600, or 1000 g mol–1), respectively, a series of networks composed of acrylates with different glycol chain lengths are facilely obtained. Photopolymerization kinetics and gelation times of the semi-IPN systems are characterized by photo-differential scanning calorimetry and photo-rheology technology, respectively. The results show that the glycol chain length of the linear PEGMA segment shuttling in the polymer backbone plays a pivotal role in influencing the chemical dynamic features of the synthetic process, which are also confirmed by mechanical and electrochemical property measurements additionally. Furthermore, the cells assembled by the optimal semi-IPN SPEs achieve enhanced specific capacity and cyclability in solid-state LMBs, highlighting the practical significance of research on polymerization kinetics in guiding the design of state-of-the-art SPEs.

papers.title: Upcycling Greenhouse Refrigerants into Sustainable Chemical Feedstocks
papers.abstract: Abstract Rising global temperatures are driving demand for air conditioning, while leakage of high-GWP refrigerants further accelerates warming. In addition, the transition to low-GWP alternatives generates large volumes of waste refrigerants, which are currently treated by energy-intensive thermal destruction processes that often lead to the loss or downgrading of fluorine resources. Although dehydrofluorination offers a promising route to convert hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) refrigerants into low-GWP alternatives, conventional approaches are often limited by catalyst deactivation and degradation of target products caused by hydrogen fluoride (HF) as a by-product. Here, we show a practical continuous-flow process that overcomes these barriers by using alkali metal fluoride catalysts and silica as a sacrificial reagent to capture HF irreversibly as gaseous silicon tetrafluoride. This system enables the direct upcycling of legacy refrigerants into sustainable chemical feedstocks, including low-GWP hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs) and key monomers for fluoropolymers. Furthermore, selective conversion of the HFC-125 component within the near-azeotropic refrigerant blend R410A alters the boiling-point distribution, providing a potential route to HFC-32 recovery. Waste glass from end-of-life solar panels can also serve as the silica source under the reaction conditions.

Waste glass from end-of-life solar panels can also serve as the silica source under the reaction conditions.

papers.title: Toward a Local Manipulation of DNA by Quantum Fields
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen bonds are the fundamental backbone for deoxyribo-nucleic acid (DNA) stability. In this Letter we investigate a new strategy based on plasmonic cavities to perform manipulation of hydrogen bonds in DNA. The analysis is performed using state-of-the-art Quantum Electrodynamics Coupled Cluster (QED-CC) calculations. We investigate whether in the strong coupling regime modifications of the nucleotide bases’ interactions can be induced in a totally nonintrusive manner. Our strategy proposes an alternative approach to methodologies based on a collective coupling to perform optical DNA manipulation.

Our strategy proposes an alternative approach to methodologies based on a collective coupling to perform optical DNA manipulation.

papers.title: Rational design of biochar for carbon dioxide capture and catalytic conversion
papers.abstract: The continuous increase in carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions has intensified the need for efficient carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technologies. Biochar has emerged as a promising, cost-effective, and sustainable platform for CCU. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the rational design of biochar for CO2 capture and subsequent catalytic conversion. We first discuss various synthesis methods and activation strategies for tailoring the physicochemical properties of biochar. We then elucidate the mechanisms of CO2 capture, highlighting the roles of pore modification and heteroatom functionalities in enhancing both physisorption and chemisorption. Furthermore, the roles of biochar in thermocatalytic, electrocatalytic, and photocatalytic CO2 conversion are critically examined, with particular emphasis on its function as a multifunctional support for metal nanoparticles, molecular catalysts, single atoms, and nanoclusters. Finally, we outline key challenges and future directions for the rational development of next-generation biochar toward practical carbon-neutral technologies. Accordingly, this review establishes a rational design framework based on application demand, key performance parameters, and targeted synthesis strategies, thereby linking practical CCU requirements with the controlled engineering of biochar porosity, surface chemistry, conductivity, and catalytic functionality.

papers.title: Immunotechnology-based toolbox for care of chronic wounds
papers.abstract: Wound healing is a complex natural process with overlapping sequences of inflammatory, proliferation, and remodeling stages. All stages involve immune cells and their secreted molecules, including macrophages, neutrophils, and cytokines. This process becomes dysregulated in chronic wounds, such as diabetic ulcers and malignant (fungating) wounds, where healing halts before it can be completed. Both generic immunomodulation and targeted immunoengineering approaches constitute a powerful toolbox to reset healing processes. This brief review first provides background on the involvement of immune system components contribute to wound healing and their dysregulation during impaired wound healing. It then discusses the current state of knowledge on immunomodulation and immunoengineering as applied to chronic wound care. The immunomodulation approach uses stem cells or extracellular vesicles to regulate inflammation and prevent cellular senescence so that tissue regeneration takes place. Immunoengineering approaches cover the use of DNA nanoparticles to aid tissue regeneration, and aptamer-antibody conjugates to control inflammation. Finally, theranostic devices which provide real-time sensing and delivery of necessary proteins and drugs to reset wound healing have been discussed.
papers.summary: Wound healing is a complex natural process with overlapping sequences of inflammatory, proliferation, and remodeling stages. Immunoengineering approaches cover the use of DNA nanoparticles to aid tissue regeneration, and aptamer-antibody conjugates to control inflammation. Finally, theranostic devices which provide real-time sensing and delivery of necessary proteins and drugs to reset wound healing have been discussed.

papers.title: Sr-anchoring-directed gradient shell architecture in Sr 2 Fe 1.5 Mo 0.5 O 6- δ cathodes for reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Strontium segregation remains a critical challenge for Sr-containing double perovskite cathodes, wherein outward-migrating Sr species accumulate at the surface and severely deteriorate interfacial electrochemical kinetics in reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs). Herein, we develop a Sr-anchoring–driven interfacial catalytic architecture on Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6−δ (SFM) via vanadium-assisted near-surface phase engineering. The incorporation of V introduces Lewis-acidic centers that effectively immobilize migrating Sr species and simultaneously induce the in situ reconstruction of a nanoscale SrMoO4/SrVO3 heterointerface. More importantly, this reconstructed interface functions as a catalytically active region with enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized oxygen-defect chemistry, which collectively promote oxygen adsorption, dissociation, and charge-transfer kinetics. The gradient shell architecture not only suppresses detrimental Sr segregation but also establishes fast and continuous pathways for coupled ion–electron transport across the interface. Electrochemical impedance and distribution of relaxation time (DRT) analyses reveal substantially reduced polarization resistance and decreased activation energy, indicating accelerated oxygen electrocatalysis. Consequently, the SFM-V cathode exhibits markedly enhanced reversible electrochemical performance compared to pristine SFM, delivering a peak power density of 1.23 W cm-2 at 650 °C together with high electrolysis activity and robust cycling stability, ranking among state-of-the-art SFM-based air electrodes for R-PCECs. This work demonstrates that Sr-anchoring interfacial engineering is an effective strategy to stabilize perovskite cathodes while maintaining fast interfacial kinetics.

This work demonstrates that Sr-anchoring interfacial engineering is an effective strategy to stabilize perovskite cathodes while maintaining fast interfacial kinetics.

papers.title: Effect of injectable platelet rich fibrin augmented with vitamin c compared to injectable platelet rich fibrin alone on healing of necrotic mature single rooted teeth with chronic periapical periodontitis following regenerative endodontic therapy (a randomized controlled trial)
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the healing potential, postoperative pain and clinical normalcy associated with injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C in regenerative endodontic procedure using cone-beam computed tomography and two-dimensional radiograph. METHODS: Twenty-eight healthy patients with mature permanent single-rooted teeth diagnosed with pulp necrosis and chronic apical periodontitis were randomly allocated into two groups (n = 14). Regenerative endodontic treatment was performed using injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C (intervention group) and injectable platelet-rich fibrin alone (control group). Periapical healing was assessed using CBCT and periapical radiographs over 12 months. Postoperative pain and clinical normalcy were also evaluated. RESULTS: Both groups showed significant lesion reduction at 12 months (P = 0.001), with no significant between-group differences in postoperative lesion size (P = 0.981) or reduction magnitude (P = 0.497). CBCT-PAI scores improved in both groups without significant intergroup differences at baseline or follow-up. Two-dimensional radiographs showed a baseline difference (P = 0.007) but no postoperative differences; both groups demonstrated significant longitudinal reduction (P < 0.001). Postoperative pain scores were comparable between groups at all time points (P > 0.05), with a significant temporal decrease observed only in the intervention group (P = 0.001). All teeth remained asymptomatic during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Both i-PRF combined with vitamin C and i-PRF alone appear to be effective regenerative scaffolds, demonstrating comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes in regenerative endodontic procedures. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT05585359), registered on 14 October 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05585359 .

papers.title: Integrative population genetics and multi-omics reveal IL15RA as a shared pathogenic hub in rheumatoid arthritis-related heart failure
papers.abstract: Purpose Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients face a significantly elevated risk of heart failure (HF), but population-level evidence and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We aimed to assess the RA-HF association using national data and identify dietary compounds targeting shared inflammatory pathways. Methods We analyzed NHANES data (n=2,931) and performed two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Integrated machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, clinical samples, and in vitro experiments identified therapeutic targets and evaluated the effectiveness of dioscin (a yam-derived saponin). Results The rate of HF in RA patients is high, and RA patients with HF have a worse prognosis. MR analysis also revealed that RA was a significant HF risk factor. IL15RA emerged as a shared causal target, whose silencing suppressed TNF-α-induced ICAM-1 in endothelial cells and reduced M1 (CD86 + ) macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, MIF signaling were strongly implicated in the crosstalk between endothelial cells and macrophages. Dioscin bound IL15RA and reduced its expression in both cell types, phenocopying IL15RA silencing. Conclusion This study identifies IL15RA as a key therapeutic target linking RA and HF, and dioscin as a dietary phytochemical with anti-inflammatory potential. Our findings provide a population-based framework and a readily translatable nutritional strategy for mitigating cardiac comorbidity in RA patients.
papers.summary: Purpose Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients face a significantly elevated risk of heart failure (HF), but population-level evidence and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We aimed to assess the RA-HF association using national data and identify dietary compounds targeting shared inflammatory pathways. MR analysis also revealed that RA was a significant HF risk factor.

papers.title: Isolation and Structural Elucidation of Flavonoid Compounds from the Bark of Arcangelisia flava (Yellow Wood) from Kalimantan and Their Cytotoxicity Test Against MCF-7 Breast Cancer Cells
papers.journal: Fundamental and Applied Research in Medicine and Allied Sciences Indonesia
papers.abstract: Arcangelisia flava (L.) Merr., locally known as “akar kuning,” is a traditional medicinal plant from Kalimantan with limited evidence regarding its anticancer compounds. This study aimed to isolate bioactive compounds from A. flava bark and evaluate their cytotoxicity against MCF-7 breast cancer cells. Dried bark was macerated in 95% ethanol, fractionated with n-hexane, ethyl acetate, and n-butanol, and the ethyl acetate fraction was further purified by chromatography. Isolated compounds were identified using spectroscopic methods, while cytotoxicity was evaluated using the MTT assay with doxorubicin as a positive control. Three compounds were identified: berberine (85 mg), palmatine (62 mg), and quercetin (41 mg). All showed concentration-dependent cytotoxicity, with IC₅₀ values of 8.74 ± 0.38, 14.23 ± 0.61, and 18.56 ± 0.72 µg/mL, respectively. Berberine showed the highest potency and selectivity (SI = 11.27), followed by palmatine (6.14) and quercetin (6.07), while the ethyl acetate fraction had an IC₅₀ of 22.17 ± 0.94 µg/mL. These findings indicate that A. flava bark contains promising cytotoxic compounds, particularly berberine, supporting further investigation as a potential anticancer lead

papers.title: A multifunctional Tb3+–salicylic acid hydrazide phosphor for anti-counterfeiting, forensic fingerprint visualization, and biological applications
papers.abstract: Abstract A novel terbium(III) complex, Tb(SAH) , derived from salicylic acid hydrazide ( SAH ), was successfully synthesized and fully characterized. Stoichiometric analysis confirmed a 1:2 metal-to-ligand ratio. X-ray diffraction and microscopic studies revealed a polycrystalline structure with micro- and nanodomain features. Photoluminescence investigations demonstrated intense monochromatic emissions: blue for SAH and green for Tb(SAH) , with relatively long excited-state lifetimes in dimethylformamide (DMF), solid state, and polymeric matrices (PVA (polyvinyl alcohol), PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate), and silica xerogel). An efficient ligand-to-metal energy transfer mechanism under ultraviolet (UV) excitation was confirmed, indicating a strong antenna effect responsible for enhanced luminescence. Both SAH and Tb(SAH) were successfully applied in latent fingerprint visualization, clearly resolving level I–III ridge details on diverse porous, non-porous, and multicolored substrates. Additionally, transparent luminescent security inks prepared from the compounds exhibited excellent storage stability and humidity resistance, highlighting their suitability for anti-counterfeiting applications. Biological evaluation revealed that Tb(SAH) exhibits significantly greater in vitro cytotoxicity against the hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG-2) cell line than the free ligand. Significant antioxidant activity was observed for SAH and Tb(SAH) (IC 50 = 0.38 and 0.78 μM, respectively), surpassing ascorbic acid. The Tb(SAH) complex also exhibited improved antidiabetic activity (IC 50 = 14 μg/mL) compared with SAH (IC 50 = 44 μg/mL), with potency comparable to that of acarbose (IC 50 = 35 μg/mL). Antimicrobial studies indicated marked enhancement upon Tb 3 ⁺ coordination, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus . Molecular docking against DNA gyrase B (PDB ID: 6TCK) supported strong binding interactions, corroborating the experimental antimicrobial findings.

Additionally, transparent luminescent security inks prepared from the compounds exhibited excellent storage stability and humidity resistance, highlighting their suitability for anti-counterfeiting applications. Antimicrobial studies indicated marked enhancement upon Tb 3 ⁺ coordination, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus .

papers.title: Phase-separation-enabled hollow silicon carbide composite nanofibers with multiscale interfaces for electromagnetic wave absorption over a wide temperature range
papers.abstract: Abstract Silicon carbide (SiC) nanofibers are attractive for electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption in harsh environments, but the controllable construction of hollow architectures and the enhancement of dielectric loss remain challenging. Herein, phase-separation-enabled hollow SiC composite nanofibers with multiscale interfacial structures were developed to address these issues. By combining phase-field simulations with experiments, liquid-liquid phase separation was identified as the key factor governing radial compositional segregation and hollow-fiber formation, enabling controllable regulation of the phase constitution, defect density, and interfacial structure through the precursor ratio. The hollow architecture, together with the resulting multiscale interfaces and abundant defects, synergistically enhanced dielectric loss and improved impedance matching. At a PVP/PSN mass ratio of 2:1, the sample obtains a minimum reflection loss of -56.11 dB at 1.53 mm, while the 1:1 hollow fiber delivered the broadest effective absorption bandwidth of 4.96 GHz at 1.39 mm. After incorporation into an AlPO4 matrix, the optimized fibers enabled stable EMW absorption from 298 to 873 K, with a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.08 GHz in the X-band. This work demonstrates a controllable route for constructing hollow silicon carbide-based fibrous absorbers and provides insight into multiscale interfacial design for EMW absorption over a wide temperature range.

papers.title: Specific Standardization and Determination of Curcuminoid Levels in Turmeric (Curcuma longa) Rhizomes from Three Cultivation Centers in Java Using the HPLC Method
papers.journal: Fundamental and Applied Research in Medicine and Allied Sciences Indonesia
papers.abstract: Curcuma longa is one of Indonesia's most important medicinal plants, with curcuminoids (curcumin, demethoxycurcumin, and bisdemethoxycurcumin) responsible for its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, hepatoprotective, and anticancer activities. This study aimed to standardize turmeric rhizomes from Temanggung, Blitar, and Wonogiri and determine curcuminoid levels using a validated HPLC method. Specific standardization parameters were evaluated according to the Indonesian Herbal Pharmacopoeia (FHI) Edition II, while HPLC analysis employed a C18 reversed phase column with UV detection at 425 nm. All samples met FHI physicochemical standards, and the HPLC method showed excellent linearity (r² ≥ 0.9996), precision (%RSD ≤ 0.95%), and accuracy (98.7–99.8%). Curcuminoid content differed significantly among cultivation sites (p < 0.001), with the highest level in Blitar (4.48 ± 0.09%), followed by Temanggung (3.96 ± 0.07%) and Wonogiri (3.39 ± 0.06%). Curcumin levels ranged from 2.46–3.19% w/w, exceeding the FHI minimum standard (≥1.0%). These findings demonstrate that cultivation site significantly influences curcuminoid profiles, emphasizing the importance of region specific quality specifications for herbal raw material procurement.

papers.title: Exercise programmes incorporating proximal kinetic-chain components in flexible flatfoot: a systematic review and meta-analysis of foot posture, neuromuscular, and dynamic outcomes
papers.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the effects of exercise programmes incorporating proximal kinetic-chain components versus local or basic foot–ankle exercise in individuals with study-defined flexible flatfoot or low-arch/pronated-foot phenotypes. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and SPORTDiscus were searched from inception through 19 July 2026. Randomised controlled trials comparing exercise programmes incorporating proximal kinetic-chain components with local or basic foot–ankle exercise programmes were included. Random-effects meta-analyses used restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Results Fourteen randomised trials reported in 15 publications were included; 13 trials (14 reports) contributed to at least one meta-analysis. Programmes containing proximal or kinetic-chain components were associated with lower navicular-drop values (11 trials, 410 participants; mean difference −2.34 mm, 95% CI −3.30 to −1.37; I²=84.6%; low-certainty evidence). The Foot Posture Index estimate was uncertain (4 trials, 157 participants; mean difference −1.67 points, 95% CI −3.36 to 0.01; I²=89.1%; very-low-certainty evidence). The exploratory Plantar Arch Index and all three exploratory Y-Balance estimates had confidence intervals including the null and very-low-certainty evidence. Evidence for muscle, plantar-pressure, gait, kinematic, patient-reported, adherence, and adverse-event outcomes was limited and mainly derived from individual trials. Conclusion Programmes incorporating proximal kinetic-chain components may reduce short-term navicular drop compared with local or basic foot–ankle exercise programmes, but substantial heterogeneity limits confidence in the magnitude of this response; effects on FPI-6 remain uncertain. Evidence for dynamic, functional, and patient-reported outcomes remains insufficient. Systematic review registration identifier CRD420261455079.

papers.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli -based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection.

Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection.

papers.title: A systematic review of machine learning approaches for MRI-based brain tumor analysis
papers.abstract: Machine learning is now widely applied to magnetic resonance imaging-based brain tumor analysis, with task-specific performance metrics: the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) quantifies segmentation overlap, while the area under the curve (AUC) and accuracy measure classification performance. A PRISMA 2020 systematic review was conducted, searching Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore, and identified 213 eligible studies published between January 2018 and the final search date of March 16, 2026. Segmentation performance was synthesized by random-effects meta-analysis and classification performance was summarized descriptively. Classification, detection, and grading tasks dominated the literature, followed by segmentation; U-Net variants were the most frequent architectures, with transformer-based models growing fastest. The pooled mean DSC was 0.871 (95% CI: 0.852–0.889) with a 95% prediction interval of 0.7880.953, and heterogeneity was extreme ( I 2 = 99.9%), so the pooled mean should be read as a descriptive summary of the literature rather than a single underlying effect. The descriptive mean AUC across classification studies was 0.960. Methodological gaps were pervasive: only 18.8% of studies incorporated explainability, only 18.8% performed external validation, and none reported robustness metrics. Benchmark accuracy has outpaced clinical evidence: until models are validated on independent cohorts, evaluated for robustness under realistic acquisition shifts, and made interpretable to clinicians, reported performance is unlikely to translate into patient care.

papers.title: Characterization of Bentonite Clay from the Krantau and Beshtyube Deposits and their Physicochemical Investigation
papers.journal: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
papers.abstract: Nowadays, the production and utilization of traditional chemical fertilizers are associated with a series of issues, such as high resource consumption, significant energy expenditure, and severe environmental pollution, which have brought about non-negligible negative impacts on the growth of green plants and the ecological environment. This document presents a comprehensive study on the characterization and physicochemical investigation of bentonite clay from the Krantau and Beshtyube deposits in Karakalpakstan. The research focuses on utilizing bentonite in the production of complex mixed fertilizers. The study outlines the chemical composition, physicomechanical properties, and mineralogical composition of bentonite clays from these deposits. The research employs various analytical techniques to investigate the bentonite samples. Technologies such as Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA), Fourier-Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and Optical Emission Spectrometry utilizing Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP-OES) are among these. The findings show that the Krantau bentonite clay is largely made up of sodium montmorillonite, with illite, kaolinite, hydromica, and feldspar also present. The study shows several unique and interesting insights. To begin, the Krantau deposit in Karakalpakstan has a substantial advantage, with bentonite discovered between glauconite layers and projected reserves of approximately 5 million tons. This co-occurrence of bentonite and glauconite may result in more efficient extraction and usage of both minerals. Second, the study underlines bentonite's potential for increasing the effectiveness of mineral fertilizers due to its large specific surface area and high cation exchange capacity. Finally, the study emphasizes the value of indigenous mineral resources in Uzbekistan and Karakalpakstan for agricultural uses, which might reduce reliance on imported fertilizers while also boosting sustainable farming practices in the area.

papers.title: A hybrid deep Kronecker and BN-eLU-AlexNet framework for early prediction of learner outcomes in e-learning platforms
papers.abstract: Introduction Early prediction of learner outcomes in online learning environments can support timely academic intervention and learner support. Methods This study proposes DKBNE-AlexNet, a hybrid architecture combining a Deep Kronecker Network branch, a feature-token batch-normalized eLU AlexNet-inspired branch, gated residual fusion, and a wide linear residual path. Using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, 24,153 enrolments from 22 module presentations and 22,234 learners were analyzed. Eighty-four predictors were constructed from learner characteristics, course design, and engagement during the first 25% of each presentation. The target was the weighted mean of tutor-marked and computer-marked assessment scores. Models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation grouped by module presentation and repeated three times. Results DKBNE-AlexNet achieved an MAE of 11.424 (95% group-bootstrap CI 10.389-12.560), RMSE of 14.843, and R 2 of 0.117. Random Forest and LightGBM achieved slightly lower MAEs of 10.916 and 10.918, respectively, but the presentation-level difference between DKBNE-AlexNet and Random Forest was not statistically significant (Wilcoxon p = 0.388; Holm-adjusted p = 1.000). Distinct learning materials accessed and active learning days were among the strongest predictive contributors. Discussion DKBNE-AlexNet provides a competitive and stable framework for early learner-outcome prediction, while strong tree-based models remain important baselines. The framework is best interpreted as an early-warning learning-analytics tool rather than a direct measure of teacher effectiveness.

papers.title: Effect of Hydrogen Sulfide on Physiological and Biochemical Parameters in Two Barley Varieties Under Drought Stress
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses reduce barley growth and yield by elevating the free radicals such as reactive oxygen (ROS), nitrogen (RNS), carbonyl (RCS), and sulfur species (RSS) in plant cells. Among these, hydrogen sulfide (H2S), classified as RSS, serves as a signalling molecule and growth regulator in stress responses. However, the optimal sodium hydrosulphide (NaHS; an H2S donor) concentrations for barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) remain unknown. In this study, two barley cultivars (Kalaycı-97 and Yaprak) were treated with exogenous NaHS at different concentrations (0.1, 0.3 and 0.5 mM) and then exposed to drought stress. The results showed that NaHS applications increased chlorophyll content, reduced root length, and altered plant growth responses in a dose- and genotype dependent manner under drought conditions. Furthermore, it increased endogenous H2S levels in both varieties under drought conditions, leading to a decrease in H2O2 levels, an indicator of oxidative stress. In conclusion, it was shown that NaHS, particularly at concentrations of 0.3 mM and 0.5 mM, helped reduce the detrimental effects of oxidative stress in both varieties, and that genotypic differences played a significant role in this regulation. These findings highlight that NaHS regulates drought tolerance in a genotype-specific manner, strengthening enzymatic antioxidant defenses in the susceptible Kalaycı-97 while activating non enzymatic mechanisms in the tolerant Yaprak.

papers.title: Photo-Activatable RNA Switches for Optical Control of Cell-Free Protein Synthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract Programmable RNA switches enable target-dependent regulation of cell-free protein synthesis. Here, we report a photo-activatable RNA switch using photocleavable Lock DNA (pcl-Lock) to enable optical control of in vitro translation. Synthesized by solid-phase methods, pcl-Lock incorporates a coumarin-based photocleavable linker that maintains the RNA switch in an inactive state. Irradiation with 456 nm light cleaves the linker, releasing inhibition and activating translation. Light-triggered activation produced β-galactosidase, yielding approximately 4-fold and 30-fold increases in fluorescence and glucose signals, respectively. Native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis confirms efficient photocleavage of the pcl-Lock strand, while control experiments verify that light-dependent activation does not occur with the Lock strand lacking the photocleavable linker. This strategy enables optical regulation of cell-free protein synthesis and establishes a strategy for integrating photochemical control with programmable gene regulation.

papers.title: From Biological Activity to Flow Assurance: An Evidence-Qualification Framework for Biocatalytic and Bio-Derived Wax Control in Waxy Crude Oils
papers.abstract: Wax accumulation and gel formation remain critical flow assurance obstacles in the extraction and conveyance of waxy crude oils, whereby precipitation, crystal development, aggregation, ageing, rheological behavior, and wall deposition are interrelated yet distinct processes. Traditional mitigation relies on temperature regulation, physical extraction, and chemical supplements. There is an increasing fascination with sustainable oilfield chemistry that has incorporated microorganisms, enzymes, biosurfactants, and renewable formulations as substitutes or enhancements. In many instances of this material, there is a paucity of demonstration about the intermediary causal processes, with signs of hydrocarbon biodegradation, paraffin utilization, or reductions in pour point and viscosity being regarded as proof of wax-deposition control. This comprehensive critique integrates literature from petroleum engineering, wax rheology, and microbiology with a systematic evidence-evaluation methodology, revealing four progressively robust assertions: biological activity, alteration of wax-related characteristics, diminished dynamic deposition, and engineering validation. The assessment delineates five realms of evidence, specifically biological functionality, compatibility with crude oil, change of the wax phase, response to flow assurance, and sustainable implementation. A six-tier qualifying framework is suggested, constraining the validity of a technological assertion to the evidence that has been substantiated. A novel seven-phase experimental approach is introduced, advancing from candidate identification and functional description, through crude oil compatibility, fundamental performance, and mechanistic validation, to dynamic deposition assessment and translation. A five-arm baseline control framework—untreated crude, formulation matrix, inactivated preparation, commercial standard, and active treatment—is suggested to differentiate catalytic, interfacial, carrier, and formulation influences. The synthesis indicates that biological systems present exciting research opportunities; nonetheless, the evidence for direct wax-control mechanisms is far less advanced compared to hydrocarbon degradation or biosurfactant activity. The essential research requirement is not merely further screening but rather reliable, crude-specific, dynamically evaluated data that connects biological activity to wax-phase behavior and pipeline-scale flow assurance.
papers.summary: Wax accumulation and gel formation remain critical flow assurance obstacles in the extraction and conveyance of waxy crude oils, whereby precipitation, crystal development, aggregation, ageing, rheological behavior, and wall deposition are interrelated yet distinct processes. This comprehensive critique integrates literature from petroleum engineering, wax rheology, and microbiology with a systematic evidence-evaluation methodology, revealing four progressively robust assertions: biological activity, alteration of wax-related characteristics, diminished dynamic deposition, and engineering validation. The essential research requirement is not merely further screening but rather reliable, crude-specific, dynamically evaluated data that connects biological activity to wax-phase behavior and pipeline-scale flow assurance.

papers.title: Green Recycling of Waste Tire Rubber Crumb: Characterization and Water Treatment Applications
papers.abstract: Discarded tires are adding to the waste problem that exists worldwide and requires proper recycling methods. Rather than employing chemicals or energy-intensive thermal treatments, which leads to an increase in environmental pollution, in this work, the discarded tires are subjected to mechanical grinding into a fine powder form, resulting in recycled Waste Tire Rubber Crumb (WTRC), then used as an adsorbent for the removal of methylene blue (MB) dye from the polluted water. The use of the adsorbent is eco-friendly and cost-effective, which is beneficial for water treatment. The structural, thermal, and morphological characteristics of WTRC were studied with the use of X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM/EDX), thermal gravimetric analysis (TGA), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and zeta potential analysis. It was found that there was an elastic polymer matrix with inorganic additions of ZnO and CaCO3. Zeta potential measurements provided the value −32.5 mV at pH 7.0, demonstrating electrostatic repulsion of the particles and providing solid colloidal stability in aqueous media. In batch tests, WTRC proved to be a good adsorbent of MB, with up to 92.7% removal efficiency within 30 min. under the basic medium (pH 11.0, 1.2 g/50 mL dosage, and initial MB concentration of 5 mg/L ppm). The Langmuir model gave the best fit, with R2 = 0.982, which is more than Freundlich model, R2 = 0.957. The good fit of the Langmuir model indicates that adsorption predominantly occurred as a monolayer on relatively homogeneous adsorption sites on the surface of WTRC. The theoretical monolayer capacity (qmax) is calculated as 0.95 mg/g. It is proved by the surface changes after the adsorption of MB, shown in FTIR and SEM pictures. In general, the raw WTRC can serve as a simple and economic adsorbent for dyes from industry.

papers.title: Interconnected communication mechanisms in plants and their ecological functions and agricultural implications
papers.abstract: Plants interact through a coordinated communication network that enables them to perceive, process, and respond to environmental stimuli. This communication network consists of complex biological systems, including root systems, volatile organic compounds, RNA-based molecular signals, and fungal networks. Plants use these interconnected pathways to share information that regulates defense activation, resource distribution, and developmental processes. This review discusses the mechanisms of plant communication, the impacts of climate change on interplant signaling, and their ecological and agricultural significance. These insights will advance our understanding of plant survival strategies, community dynamics, and crop productivity within the broader context of ecology and sustainable agriculture.

papers.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Novel STK3/4 Inhibitors with Anti-Obesity Potential
papers.abstract: Background: Obesity is associated with impaired adipocyte metabolism driven in part by mitochondrial dysfunction.Serine/ threonine-protein kinase 3 (STK3) and STK4 promote mitophagy, leading to reduced mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue.Thus, inhibition of STK3/4 represents a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders.Methods: Two novel STK3/STK4 inhibitors, LL-M and LL-P, were identified from a focused small-molecule library using a fluorescence-based titration assay.Their effects on STK3/4 signaling and mitophagy were evaluated in C3H10T1/2 adipocytes.In vivo efficacy was assessed in male C57BL/6J mice fed either a normal chow diet or a high-fat diet (HFD), followed by a 2-week treatment with LL-M or LL-P.Metabolic outcomes, including body weight, glucose tolerance, and energy expenditure, were assessed.Results: In adipocytes, LL-M and LL-P effectively suppressed STK3/4 signaling, reduced BCL2 interacting protein 3 (BNIP3)mediated mitophagy, and increased mitochondrial metabolic activity.In HFD-fed mice, treatment with either compound attenuated body-weight gain, improved glucose tolerance, and enhanced energy expenditure.Conclusion: Pharmacological inhibition of STK3/4 by LL-M and LL-P restores mitochondrial function through suppression of BNIP3-mediated mitophagy, leading to improved adipocyte function and metabolic outcomes.These findings support the therapeutic potential of LL-M and LL-P as small-molecule candidates for the treatment of obesity and related metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Territorial governance for transformative change? Insights from the Chico Mendes Extractive Reserve in the Brazilian Amazon
papers.abstract: Brazilian extractive reserves constitute a model for the territorial governance of protected areas. With a focus on the territorial rights of traditional populations, they can serve as a catalyst for transformative change that reconciles the conservation of nature with the sustainable use of natural resources. However, the sustainability of land use in the Chico Mendes Extractive Reserve (CMER) is increasingly under pressure. Located in the western Amazon, sustainable forest extractivism has traditionally constituted the main livelihood of inhabitants. Yet, over the last 20 years, deforestation rates have increased significantly. This increase has been driven by the expansion of cattle ranching, illegal land sales, and population growth. While the causes of deforestation in the CMER have been widely documented, this study aims to understand how different actors and institutions interact to shape territorial governance and land use in the CMER, and how these governance arrangements can serve as a catalyst for transformative change. The research is based on a qualitative case study design, involving qualitative interviews, participant observation, and a photo-based approach, applied during three fieldwork visits to the research region between March 2024 and April 2025. The findings indicate that governance interactions are not only influenced by state institutions. They are shaped by economic incentives provided by the market and are contingent upon the social organization of civil society. To realize its potential for transformative change, territorial governance should adopt a multilevel governance approach, consider the local context, be based on cooperation between actors, and facilitate social learning.

The findings indicate that governance interactions are not only influenced by state institutions.

papers.title: Enhancing the Properties of Devulcanized Natural Rubber Through Sulfur Revulcanization Followed by Electron Beam Postcuring
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Devulcanized natural rubber (DNR) is a sustainable material with potential for circular resource utilization. This study investigated electron‐beam irradiation as a postcuring treatment for sulfur‐revulcanized DNR over a dose range of 0–500 kGy. Irradiation promoted additional crosslink formation, progressively increasing crosslink density, although the rate of increase reduced above 200 kGy, suggesting increasing competition from possible radiation‐induced chain scission. The resulting network modification enhanced thermomechanical and dynamic mechanical properties, as evidenced by increased TSSR index, storage modulus, and glass transition temperature, together with decreased tan δ. Increased crosslink density also promoted molecular orientation and shifted the onset of strain‐induced crystallization to lower strains, while the possible formation of relatively rigid CC crosslinks may further contribute to this behavior. Although modulus increased progressively with irradiation dose, optimum mechanical performance was achieved at 100 kGy, with a substantial 39% increase in tensile strength without sacrificing extensibility. Electron‐beam postcuring also improved mechanical‐property retention during thermal aging, whereas excessive irradiation, particularly at 500 kGy, caused substantial deterioration after prolonged aging. Overall, 100 kGy provided the most favorable balance between additional crosslinking and irradiation‐induced structural changes, demonstrating the potential of controlled electron‐beam postcuring for enhancing the performance and high‐value utilization of sulfur‐revulcanized DNR.

Overall, 100 kGy provided the most favorable balance between additional crosslinking and irradiation‐induced structural changes, demonstrating the potential of controlled electron‐beam postcuring for enhancing the performance and high‐value utilization of sulfur‐revulcanized DNR.
