papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Hydrophobic Matrix Incorporation and Polymeric Film Coating for Stabilization of Potassium Clavulanate Under Open Exposure Conditions
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Potassium clavulanate is a moisture-and temperature-sensitive β-lactamase inhibitor prone to hydrolytic degradation, discoloration, and packaging instability under humid and thermal conditions.The present study comparatively evaluated two stabilization strategies-hydrophobic matrix incorporation using stearic acid and polymeric film coating using HPMC-ethylcellulose applied to potassium clavulanate diluted with Sylloid (1:1).Stearic acid was incorporated at 10% and 20% w/w levels via physical blending, while film coating was applied to achieve 5% weight gain using a top-spray fluidized bed system.Samples were assessed under open exposure at 25°C/60% RH and under refrigerated conditions (2-8°C).Additional evaluation included solution stability of 1% (w/v) aqueous preparations and thermal stress testing (80°C, 1 h) in Alu-Alu blisters.Stearic acid incorporation delayed initial discoloration but did not fully prevent degradation under prolonged humidity exposure.Film coating provided improved resistance to moisture ingress and reduced blister bulging under thermal stress, although strict temperature control during processing was essential.The findings support a diffusion-controlled degradation mechanism and highlight the relative advantages of internal hydrophobic modification and external barrier coating strategies for stabilizing moisture-sensitive clavulanate systems.

papers.title: Soil Organic Carbon Dynamics and Carbon Management Index under Forest and Agricultural Land-Use Systems in the Western Himalayas
papers.abstract: Himalayan soils are highly susceptible to the impacts of climate change and land-use shifts. Soil organic carbon (SOC) and the carbon management index (CMI) are key measures of soil health in response to land use changes. This study assessed total organic carbon (TOC), carbon fractions, carbon pool index (CPI), CMI, and physicochemical properties in forest and agricultural land-use systems in the temperate western Himalayas. Soil samples were collected across 32 distinct sites representing forest (FS), wheat (WS), rice (RS), and maize (MS) systems (n = 32). FS exhibited the highest average TOC (25.6 g kg-1), followed by MS (19.3 g kg-1), WS (15.2 g kg-1), and RS (14 g kg-1). TOC levels differed significantly between land-use categories (ANOVA; F = 13.4, P< 0.001), with all agricultural systems showing significantly lower TOC levels than forests. The maximum concentration of labile carbon (LC) was identified in FS (4.3%), while the lowest was observed in WS (2.8%). MS had the highest CPI (0.75), whereas RS had the highest average CMI (85.5), indicating distinct carbon management dynamics despite lower baseline TOC. TOC was positively correlated with altitude and electrical conductivity but negatively correlated with soil pH. Multiple linear regression (R2 = 0.70) confirmed land-use type as the primary predictor of TOC variation, showing significant reductions for RS (11.6 g kg-1), WS (10.7 g kg-1), and MS (4.9 g kg-1) compared to the forest baseline (P< 0.05). Principal component analysis successfully differentiated agricultural and forest systems based on topography, soil properties, and carbon pools. The primary cause of SOC depletion is the initial conversion of forests to farmland, underscoring the need for climate smart land management to maintain ecosystem services and replenish regional carbon stocks.

papers.title: Ionic-Liquid-Catalyzed Depolymerization of PET: BHET Recovery and Re-Polymerization
papers.abstract: The accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste presents significant environmental challenges due to its extensive usage and low global recycling rates. Among the available recycling routes, chemical depolymerization by glycolysis offers a promising way to recover high-value monomers. In this study, six ionic liquids (ILs) were tested as homogeneous catalysts for the glycolysis of post-consumer PET bottles in ethylene glycol (EG) at 200 °C for 3 h, alongside an uncatalyzed control. 1-Butyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate ([BMIM][OAc]) and trihexyltetradecylphosphonium decanoate ([P6,6,6,14][Dec]) gave complete PET conversion with isolated bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) yields of 33.6% and 72.4%, respectively. Moreover, trihexyltetradecylphosphonium bis(2,4,4-trimethylpentyl)phosphinate ([P6,6,6,14][TMPP]) reached 56% conversion with no separable product; however, the other three chloride-based ILs and the control reaction demonstrated negligible conversion at the given process parameters. The recovered BHET was characterized by FT-IR, 1H and 13C NMR and GC-MS, and further, was re-polymerized by melt polycondensation at 270 °C. The FT-IR fingerprint, thermogravimetric decomposition profile and solid-state 13C NMR spectrum indicated that the properties of the recycled PET compete with those of the bottlegrade PET. Their melting peak lay 7.7 °C below the reference on first heating (240.6 vs. 248.3 °C) but rose to 248.5 °C on second heating, 3.3 °C above the reference, suggesting that the initial difference arises mainly from crystal perfection and thermal history rather than from an altered chain structure.

papers.title: Hybrid Reinforcement of Carboxymethyl Cellulose Films with Nanocellulose, Bentonite, and Ceramic Industry Waste: Structural, Thermal, and Morphological Characterization
papers.abstract: In this study, biodegradable hybrid polymeric films were developed by reinforcing a carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) matrix with nanocellulose (NC), bentonite, and ground fired ceramic waste recovered from the vitrified ceramic industry. Seven formulations were prepared by the solvent casting method, and their structural, thermal, thermomechanical, and morphological properties were characterized by Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA/DTGA), dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), and scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX). DSC analysis revealed endothermic peaks at 240–248 °C corresponding to the onset of thermal degradation, while DTGA curves showed a two-stage degradation behavior for all formulations. The incorporation of inorganic reinforcements markedly improved thermal stability: the temperature at 10% mass loss (T10%) increased from 150 °C for pure CMC to 207 °C for the ceramic-waste-containing films, and the highest T50% value (397 °C) and char yield (40.2%) were recorded for F7 (80% CMC, 10% NC, 10% ceramic waste), confirming a thermal barrier effect. DMA results showed that F4 (85% CMC, 10% NC, 5% bentonite) exhibited the highest storage and loss modulus values, whereas excessive bentonite loading reduced stiffness through agglomeration. FT-IR spectra indicated that interactions between the components were governed by hydrogen bonding and physical mixing rather than covalent bonding, and SEM-EDX analyses revealed more homogeneous filler dispersion at low loading levels. Accordingly, F4 and F7 were identified as the optimum formulations for dynamic mechanical stiffness and thermal stability, respectively.

papers.title: Structure–Processing–Property Relationships in PVOH/PBAT Blends Plasticized with Dipentaerythritol, ε-Caprolactone, and Water
papers.abstract: Abstract Water-soluble poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVOH) offers high tensile strength and an excellent oxygen barrier, but its dense hydrogen-bond network places its melting point close to its decomposition temperature, making it difficult to melt-process. Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is melt-processable and ductile but has low strength and dimensional stability that restrict its use. To combine their strengths, PBAT/PVOH blends (10–40 wt % PBAT) were melt-compounded with a 20 wt % ternary plasticizer of dipentaerythritol, ε-caprolactone, and water in equal parts, benchmarked against a water-only control at 40 wt % PBAT. Across FTIR, XRD, DSC, steady-shear and oscillatory rheology, DMA, tensile, SEM, AFM, TGA, and gas-barrier measurements, the ternary plasticizer governs the structure–property relationship by redistributing the PVOH hydrogen-bond network rather than breaking it; it broadens and shifts the O–H stretching envelope, suppresses PVOH crystallinity and recrystallization, depresses the glass transition by 17–27 °C, and broadens the relaxation spectrum, with no cross-linking or covalent grafting. Composition sets the phase topology─dispersed PBAT domains at 20–30 wt % and a cocontinuous structure at 40 wt %─while the plasticizer controls interfacial adhesion, converting the weakly bonded, void-laden interfaces of the water-only control into well-adhered ones. Among the series, the 20 wt % blend (PBAT-20) gives the best stiffness–toughness balance (modulus ≈ 0.23 GPa, ultimate tensile strength ≈ 20 MPa) together with an oxygen transmission rate of ≈6.4 cm3 m–2 day–1 for a 400 μm film, equivalent to ≈102 cm3 m–2 day–1 when normalized to a 25 μm thickness. The water-vapor transmission rate of the same film remains high (6.06 g m–2 day–1), so the films reported here are suited to oxygen-sensitive but moisture-tolerant applications rather than to moisture-critical ones. These findings position ternary hydrogen-bond engineering as a reaction-free, melt-processing route to property-tunable PBAT/PVOH films for biodegradable flexible packaging.

papers.title: The CXCL12/CXCR4 axis in breast cancer-associated fibroblasts: a transcriptome analysis and systematic literature review
papers.abstract: Background Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) represent a pivotal component of the breast cancer microenvironment. In a paracrine model, CAFs secreted the chemokine CXCL12 (SDF-1α), which bound to CXCR4 and activated the PI3K/AKT and MAPK signaling pathways, stimulating their migration and invasion. TGF-β1 induces myofibroblast differentiation of CAFs by acting through the TGFBR2/ALK5 receptor complex and phosphorylating SMAD2/3, thereby increasing the expression of ACTA2 and FAP. An autocrine loop has been demonstrated in CAF, whereby TGF-β1, via SMAD3, induces the transcription of CXCR4, and subsequently, CXCR4, by binding to the same cell, maintains the myofibroblast phenotype. However, a systematic comparison of paracrine and autocrine variants has not yet been conducted in the context of CAF subtypes. Methods A secondary analysis of 101 bulk RNA-seq samples was performed, with classification into healthNF, riskNF, cancerNF, and CAF S1-S4 using correlation analysis (Spearman), differential expression (DESeq, FDR <0.05), GSEA (FDR <0.25), and a systematic review of the literature (2005–2026). Results The PCA and the contingency table analysis enabled the description of two patterns of Cancer-associated fibroblasts subtype distribution across clinical and morphological groups: healthNF → cancerNF → CAF and healthNF → riskNF → CAF. Elevated levels of CXCR4 were identified exclusively in CAF (22.7%, FDR = 5.98 × 10 −4 ) and were associated with the CAF-S3 and CAF-S4 fibroblast phenotypes. At CXCR4 High levels, the correlation between CXCL12 and TGFB1 became negative, while the correlation between CXCL12 and ITGAV, FAP, and ITGB1 remained positive. This finding suggests a possible shift from TGF-β-dependent to CXCR4-mediated regulation of CXCL12. GSEA revealed an association of CXCR4 High -CAF with enrichment of gene sets related to the interferon response, inflammation, and apoptosis, as well as with decreased enrichment of proliferation sets, EMT, and TGF-β signaling. A recent systematic review revealed that only 8.6% of publications contain experimental data supporting an autocrine loop, 17.1% describe a paracrine model, and 74.3% do not distinguish between the signaling types. Conclusion It is hypothesised that the CXCR4 High -CAF transcriptome profile is compatible with a biologically plausible theory of transition between paracrine and autocrine regulatory modes and inflammatory cell states. In vitro validation is a prerequisite for establishing a causal relationship.

papers.title: Sustainable Development of Multifunctional Jute Fiber-Reinforced Epoxy Composites Enhanced with Agricultural Bran Fillers for Sustainable Structural and Antimicrobial Applications
papers.abstract: This study investigates multifunctional jute fiber-reinforced epoxy composites incorporating agricultural bran filler (0–4 wt.%) fabricated by hand lay-up. The composite containing 3 wt.% bran exhibited optimum performance, achieving tensile, flexural, and impact strengths of 76.16 MPa, 81.27 MPa, and 17.19 kJ/m2, respectively. Shore D hardness increased from 58 to 69, while thermal conductivity and coefficient of linear thermal expansion decreased from 0.86 to 0.62 W/mK and 1.16 × 10−5 °C−1 to 0.96 × 10−5 °C−1, respectively. Heat deflection temperature increased from 79°C to 104 °C, while thermogravimetric analysis indicated improved thermal stability and char formation. Under cyclic loading initiated at 70% of the respective ultimate tensile strength, the 3 wt.% composite retained a fatigue strength of 42.86 MPa at 20,000 cycles, 15.4% higher than the unfilled composite. papers.title: Pyrolysis Characteristics of Straw Fuel and Its Compound Fuel
papers.abstract: Abstract To address the global energy crisis and valorize industrial and agricultural solid waste, a corn straw-oil sludge composite fuel (CF) with a mass ratio of 1.5:1 was prepared. Pure corn straw fuel (SF) served as the control. The pyrolysis characteristics of both pellet fuels up to 1000 °C were systematically investigated via thermogravimetric (TG) analysis at heating rates of 10, 20, and 30 °C/min. The pyrolysis characteristics were analyzed via characteristic parameters, Gaussian fitting assignments, and the Flynn–Wall–Ozawa (FWO) and Kissinger–Akahira–Sunose (KAS) model-free kinetic methods. Within the tested temperature range (50–1000 °C), CF exhibited higher characteristic parameters than SF, suggesting facile initiation under the conditions tested. A positive deviation between the experimental and calculated TG curves preliminarily indicated a synergistic effect during the core copyrolysis stage (170–650 °C). Gaussian fitting was tentatively assigned to four bond cleavage stages for both fuels, with the cleavage of Cal–heteroatom bonds as the dominant reaction (proportion >50%). The addition of oil sludge introduced more alkyl-substituted aromatic compounds into CF, increasing the proportion of Car–Cal and Car–heteroatom bond cleavage from 6.8% (SF) to 15.8% (CF). The average apparent activation energy of CF was higher than that of SF. Notably, CF exhibited a kinetic characteristic of low initial activation energy and high overall activation energy, which favored facile pyrolysis initiation and inhibition of side reactions.

papers.title: Architecture–Property Relationships in 3D ‐Printed G– PEG – CH Scaffolds: Effects of Pore Spacing and Deposition Strategy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Gelatin‐based hybrid hydrogels have emerged as versatile scaffolds for biomedical applications, yet their functional performance depends heavily on rational architectural design rather than material formulation alone. In this study, a gelatin–PEG–chitosan (G–PEG–CH) hybrid hydrogel was processed via low‐temperature 3D bioplotting to systematically investigate the role of scaffold architecture on structural, mechanical, physicochemical, and biological properties. The work was conducted in two stages: first, four configurations with increasing pore spacing (Void_0–Void_3) were evaluated to identify an optimal balance between mechanical integrity, swelling behavior, and degradation stability; second, the selected pore spacing (~1.0 mm) was tested using two different filament deposition strategies (octagonal and isogonal) to verify architectural robustness. Compression tests revealed a strain‐dependent mechanical behavior, where an intermediate pore spacing (Void_1) provided the most favorable balance between low‐strain stiffness, energy absorption, and deformation tolerance. Physicochemical analyses confirmed high swelling capacity (~577%) and controlled degradation, while in vitro assays demonstrated favorable short‐term cytocompatibility and cell adhesion. Variations in filament deposition strategy did not significantly alter overall cell viability, suggesting that, at the selected pore spacing, deposition orientation had a comparatively limited effect on short‐term cell viability. Overall, this study highlights scaffold architecture as a critical design parameter for G–PEG–CH hydrogels and provides a structured framework for optimizing 3D‐printed constructs for soft‐tissue and wound‐related applications.

papers.title: Surface Modified Cellulose Based Green Selenium Adsorbent Tailored via Radiation Assisted Graft Polymerization Approach
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Selenium in ground water, a micronutrient in trace levels, can be potentially hazardous if exceeding permissible limits. Despite a gamut of remediation strategies available for targeting toxic metal ions, adsorption continues to be the preeminent method notwithstanding limitations in terms of sustainability, reusability, and scalability. This work reports implementation of an eco‐friendly gamma radiation mediated surface modification approach to generate a functionally active green cellulose‐based adsorbent for removing selenite ions from water. 3‐Methacrylamido‐N,N,N‐trimethylpropan‐1‐aminium chloride (MAPTAC) was radiolytically grafted onto cellulose fabric (Cotton‐ g ‐PMAPTAC) to incorporate quaternary ammonium groups under optimized reaction parameters. Cotton‐ g ‐PMAPTAC sequestered SeO 3 2− ions with an uptake efficiency of ~29 mg g −1 in batch adsorption. FTIR, XPS, SEM, and TGA analysis were invoked for physicochemical characterization of the adsorbent, while EDXRF and GFAAS were employed to evaluate uptake performance in the ppm and sub‐ppm levels, respectively. Influence of parameters: pH, temperature, grafting yield, and ionic strength on adsorbent efficiency was investigated, and its potential scalability explored through column flow mode adsorption studies. The maximum uptake efficiency recorded was 41.36 mg g −1 , with reusability demonstrated for 8 batch cycles using 0.5 N NaCl as eluent media. The developed adsorbent presents a sustainable material with multicycle reusability for effective Se(IV) mitigation in the environment.

papers.title: Design and Characterization of Nanostructured Lipid Carrier of Poorly Water Soluble Drug for Improvement of Bioavailability
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Oxaprozin is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) belonging to the Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) Class II, characterized by poor aqueous solubility despite high permeability.Its limited water solubility results in a slow dissolution rate, delayed onset of action, and reduced oral bioavailability, which can compromise its therapeutic efficacy.Therefore, developing an effective drug delivery system to enhance the solubility and bioavailability of oxaprozin remains an important pharmaceutical challenge.The present study aimed to design and characterize a nanostructured lipid carrier (NLC) formulation of oxaprozin to improve its solubility, dissolution behavior, and oral bioavailability.Nanostructured lipid carriers were developed using a blend of solid and liquid lipids stabilized with suitable surfactants through high-shear homogenization followed by ultrasonication.The formulation variables were optimized to obtain nanoparticles with desirable physicochemical properties and high drug encapsulation.The prepared NLCs were comprehensively characterized for particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), zeta potential, drug loading, entrapment efficiency, morphology, thermal behavior, crystallinity, and in vitro drug release.The optimized formulation exhibited nanosized particles with a narrow size distribution, high encapsulation efficiency, and acceptable zeta potential, indicating good physical stability.Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses confirmed the successful incorporation of oxaprozin into the lipid matrix with a reduction in its crystalline nature, contributing to improved drug solubility.In vitro dissolution studies demonstrated a significantly enhanced drug release profile from the optimized NLC formulation compared with pure oxaprozin, owing to the increased surface area and partial amorphization of the drug within the lipid matrix.The sustained release characteristics of the NLCs further suggested their potential to maintain therapeutic drug concentrations over an extended period.Pharmacokinetic evaluation indicated that the optimized NLC formulation improved the oral bioavailability of oxaprozin by enhancing its dissolution rate and intestinal absorption.The lipid-based nanocarrier system also has the potential to facilitate lymphatic transport and reduce first-pass metabolism, thereby improving systemic drug exposure.Overall, the findings of this study demonstrate that nanostructured lipid carriers are a promising and effective approach for enhancing the solubility, dissolution, and oral bioavailability of poorly water-soluble oxaprozin.The developed formulation may improve therapeutic efficacy while reducing dose-related variability, making NLCs a suitable delivery platform for oxaprozin and other poorly water-soluble drugs.

papers.title: Development and Characterization of Gastroretentive Microballoons of Tegoprazan for Antiulcer Activity
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Peptic ulcer disease remains one of the most prevalent gastrointestinal disorders, primarily caused by excessive gastric acid secretion, Helicobacter pylori infection, and prolonged use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.Although Tegoprazan, a novel potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), provides rapid and effective suppression of gastric acid secretion, its therapeutic performance may be improved through a gastroretentive drug delivery system that prolongs its residence in the stomach.The present study focuses on the development and characterization of gastroretentive floating microballoons of Tegoprazan to enhance gastric retention, provide sustained drug release, and improve antiulcer efficacy.The optimized formulation demonstrated excellent floating behavior, remaining buoyant for more than 12 hours, with high entrapment efficiency and satisfactory production yield.In vitro drug release studies indicated sustained release of Tegoprazan over an extended period, following controlled-release kinetics and providing a gradual release profile suitable for gastroretentive delivery.The antiulcer potential of the optimized gastroretentive microballoons was evaluated using suitable experimental ulcer models.The formulation exhibited superior gastroprotective activity compared with the conventional Tegoprazan formulation, as evidenced by a significant reduction in ulcer index, enhanced gastric mucosal protection, and prolonged acid suppression.The improved therapeutic performance was attributed to extended gastric residence time, sustained drug release, and enhanced local availability of Tegoprazan at the site of action.Overall, the developed gastroretentive floating microballoons of Tegoprazan demonstrated desirable physicochemical characteristics, prolonged buoyancy, controlled drug release, and enhanced antiulcer activity.The study suggests that floating microballoons represent a promising oral gastroretentive drug delivery system capable of improving the therapeutic efficacy of Tegoprazan while reducing dosing frequency and enhancing patient compliance.Further pharmacokinetic and clinical investigations are recommended to establish their potential for the effective management of peptic ulcer disease.

papers.title: Kinetic, thermodynamic and TG-FTIR Analysis of industrial wastewater treatment sludge pyrolysis
papers.journal: Ömer Halisdemir Üniversitesi Mühendislik Bilimleri Dergisi
papers.abstract: Industrial Wastewater Treatment Sludge (IWTS) is a potential feedstock for waste to energy conversion by pyrolysis, allowing simultaneous waste reduction and energy recovery. In this study, IWTS obtained from the chemical treatment unit of a wastewater treatment plant located in the Samsun-Central Organized Industrial Zone, Türkiye, was characterized and their pyrolytic behavior was studied using TGA, DSC and TG-FTIR. The feedstock had 63.82% volatile matter, 24.76% ash, 11.42% fixed carbon and higher heating value of 15.42 MJkg-1. The thermal decomposition process occurred in three stages, removal of moisture below 150 °C, a major devolatilization stage between 200 and 450 °C and slow decomposition of char/mineral above 500 °C, resulting approximately 46% residual mass at 800 °C. Kinetic evaluation was conducted by the Coats-Redfern method and the second order chemical reaction model provided the best fit with an activation energy of 53.15 kJmol-1 (R2 = 0.99883), an interpretation further supported by the master plot analysis. The thermodynamic parameters indicated that the activation process required a substantial energy input and involved the formation of a more ordered activated complex. TG-FTIR showed the evolution of H2O, CO2, phenolic compounds and minor aliphatic species during the devolatilization. These findings provided useful preliminary design parameters (decomposition stages, kinetic and thermodynamic parameters, and volatile product profile) for the development of sludge pyrolysis systems.

papers.title: Synthesis, Characterization, and Biodegradability of a Superabsorbent Cellulose-Based Hydrogel Derived from Olive Pomace
papers.abstract: In this study, a cellulose-based hydrogel was derived from olive pomace through a three-stage valorization process. In the first stage, cellulose was extracted from de-oiled olive pomace, yielding 9.16%. In the second stage, the extracted cellulose was converted to sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) via carboxymethylation with monochloroacetic acid (MCA) under alkaline conditions. In the third stage, the synthesized CMC was chemically crosslinked with epichlorohydrin (ECH) in an alkaline medium to produce a biobased hydrogel. The resulting material exhibited an amorphous phase fraction of 80.93% and an exceptional equilibrium swelling ratio of 2616% after approximately 12 days of immersion in distilled water. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed that the hydrogel exhibited good thermal stability, with an onset degradation temperature of 236.05 °C, and retained 27.05% of its mass at 600 °C. Furthermore, time-dependent deswelling measurements demonstrated strong water-retention performance, with a cumulative mass loss of only 20.93% after 6.5 h under ambient evaporation conditions. The biodegradability test was systematically assessed via a 28-day soil burial test using two different carrier systems: perforated polyethylene bags and muslin/cheesecloth bags. Following 28 days of soil burial, the hydrogel exhibited gravimetric mass losses of 41.25% and 53.88% in the perforated polyethylene and muslin/cheesecloth carrier systems, respectively. These results indicate that the hydrogel derived from olive pomace is an olive pomace-derived biodegradable water-retention material with significant potential for agricultural soil conditioning, controlled-release fertilizer systems, and other environmental applications.

papers.title: Body weight–normalized resting metabolic rate and its associations with malnutrition and sarcopenia in hospitalized older adults: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Background Malnutrition and sarcopenia are major contributors to frailty, functional decline, and mortality in older adults. Although the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria provide a standardized framework for diagnosing malnutrition, they do not incorporate physiological measures of metabolic function. We therefore investigated the associations of body weight–normalized resting metabolic rate (RMR/weight) with GLIM-defined malnutrition and sarcopenia in hospitalized older adults. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed baseline data from a prospective cohort of hospitalized older adults who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH) between February 2024 and August 2025. Malnutrition was diagnosed according to the GLIM criteria, and sarcopenia was defined according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2019 criteria. RMR was measured by indirect calorimetry and normalized to body weight (kcal/kg/day). Associations between RMR/weight and study outcomes were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the discriminatory ability of RMR/weight for malnutrition. Results A total of 141 participants (mean age, 74.8 ± 6.6 years; 54.6% women) were included, of whom 74 (52.5%) had GLIM-defined malnutrition. Both RMR and RMR/weight were significantly lower in participants with malnutrition than in those without malnutrition. After adjustment for age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) score, and Katz Activities of Daily Living (ADL) score, each 1-kcal/kg/day increase in RMR/weight was associated with lower odds of GLIM-defined malnutrition [odds ratio (OR), 0.698; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.597–0.816; p < 0.001] and sarcopenia (OR, 0.756; 95% CI, 0.658–0.870; p < 0.001). RMR/weight showed moderate discriminatory ability for malnutrition (area under the curve, 0.759; 95% CI, 0.677–0.838). An exploratory threshold of 20.5 kcal/kg/day yielded a sensitivity of 83.8% and specificity of 40.3%. Low RMR/weight (< 20.5 kcal/kg/day) was associated with higher odds of GLIM-defined malnutrition and sarcopenia, as well as with all three GLIM phenotypic criteria and several sarcopenia components. Conclusions Lower RMR/weight was independently associated with GLIM-defined malnutrition and sarcopenia in hospitalized older adults. RMR/weight may provide complementary metabolic information regarding nutrition- and muscle-related impairment, although its clinical utility requires further validation.

RMR/weight showed moderate discriminatory ability for malnutrition (area under the curve, 0.759; 95% CI, 0.677–0.838).

papers.title: A review of synthesis, characterizations, and biological activity of amphiphilic copolymers containing pendant phosphorylcholine groups
papers.abstract: Pendant 2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC) is a hydrophilic, biocompatible nanodrug, those are required for the preparation of patient-specific nanomedicine to enhance therapeutic efficacy in the human body. MPC combined with hydrophobic n -butyl methacrylate (BMA) or n -dodecyl methacrylate (DMA) with varying molecular weights and compositions obtained block (PMPC n -b-PBMA m and PMPC n -b-PDMA m ; m and n represent degrees of polymerization) and random (P(MPC/BMAx) and P(MPC/DMAx); x represents composition) copolymers with reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) radical polymerization. Their aggregation properties were evaluated by 1 H NMR spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, static light scattering (SLS), dynamic light scattering (DLS), surface tension, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and in vitro anticancer activities. The 1 H NMR data of PMPC n -b-PBMA m confirmed highly restricted motion of the n -butyl moiety through hydrophobic interactions between PMPC and PBMA blocks and established the restricted mobility of DMA and MPC pendant groups of P(MPC/DMA x ), while MPC units were trapped in a hydrophobic micro domain. Hydrophobic probe pyrene was encapsulated in PMPC n -b-PBMA m micelles to exhibit fluorescence activity. Aggregation number increased with increasing ‘x’ due to the enhancement of hydrophobic interactions between n -dodecyl groups. SLS studies can exhibit structural properties of copolymer micelles by comprising a PBMA core with a PMPC shell. DLS studies demonstrated sizes of PMPC n -b-PBMA m micelles were gradually increased with increasing PBMA block lengths. Size, surface morphology, and thickness of bilayers were confirmed by SEM and TEM. Both copolymers are used as emerging candidates in biomedical research fields because the paclitaxel drug is incorporated in micelles; that’s why PMPC forms a biocompatible outer shell to exhibit stimuli-responsive drug efficacy and gene therapy.

papers.title: Solvent-Dipole Deshielding of Hydrated Aluminum Lewis Acids for Enhanced 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Production from Biomass
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) is a key biomass-derived platform chemical for producing furan-based fuels, fine chemicals, and polymers. Its production from glucose in homogeneous catalytic systems, however, is often limited by the solvation of Lewis acid catalytic centers, where coordinating solvent molecules and anions can shield the active sites, restrict substrate access, and diminish HMF yield and selectivity. Here, we demonstrate that polar aprotic cosolvents can function as active components of the catalytic microenvironment rather than passive reaction media. In water-rich AlCl3 solutions, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), N,N-dimethylacetamide (DMA), and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) exert dipole–dipole interactions with Al-coordinated water molecules through hydrogen bonding, distorting the [Al(H2O)6]3+ solvation shell and increasing access to the Lewis acidic Al center without directly coordinating to it. Spectroscopic measurements and electronic-structure calculations reveal that weakening of the Al–O(water) interaction increases in the order of DMF < DMA < DMSO. This solvation-shell deshielding decreases the apparent activation energy for glucose-to-fructose isomerization from 96 to 79 kJ·mol–1 and enables an HMF yield of 90% from glucose at 150 °C. Glucose streams derived from sugarcane bagasse, poplar sawdust, and palm trunk sawdust afford HMF yields exceeding 80%, while the integrated sugarcane-bagasse route achieves a 49 mol % HMF yield based on the cellulose originally present in the biomass. These results establish dipolar cosolvent control of hydrated metal centers as a molecular design principle for homogeneous biomass conversion.

papers.title: Dual‐Encrypted Ultraviolet Optical Communication Driven by Opto‐Piezoelectric Coupling in Two‐Dimensional Flexible Ferroelectric Single‐Crystalline Thin‐Films
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of flexible wearable electronics has triggered an urgent demand for high‐security and miniaturized encrypted optical communication systems. However, conventional optical encryption strategies predominantly rely on dual‐wavelength excitation, tunable light sources, or software‐based algorithms, leading to bulky configurations and vulnerable hardware‐level security. Herein, we report a dual‐encrypted ultraviolet optical communication system based on BA 2 EA 2 Pb 3 Br 10 ( 1 , where BA is n‐butylamine and EA is ethylamine) ferroelectric single‐crystalline thin‐films (SCFs). The 1 ferroelectric SCFs show a photoresponsivity that reaches 230% of the original level under +1.13% tensile strain. Notably, we innovatively define the strain‐ratio key (ε 1 /ε 2 , ε 2 /ε 3 , ε 3 /ε 4 ) induced by distinct bending states as the intrinsic unclonable hardware secret key, and construct a 4‐bit combined coding scheme based on four distinguishable photocurrent levels modulated by these strain ratios to realize secure transmission of the message “FJIRSM.” This strain ratio‐based system avoids complex optical modulation, ensuring ultrahigh security, and expands the application of two‐dimensional ferroelectrics in advanced encrypted optoelectronics.

papers.title: Sustainable development of multifunctional epoxy composites reinforced with jujube seed particles
papers.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the multi-functional performance of epoxy composites reinforced with Indian wild jujube ( Ziziphus mauritiana ) seed particles as a sustainable and low-cost reinforcement. Composites were fabricated by hand layup with particle concentrations of 4, 8, 12, 16, and 20 wt% in an LY-556 epoxy matrix cured with HY-951 at room temperature. Mechanical, tribological, water absorption, and thermal properties were evaluated, and scanning electron microscopy was used to relate performance to morphology and interfacial behaviour. Particle size analysis showed a bimodal distribution with an average hydrodynamic diameter of 1099 nm and a polydispersity index of 0.969. The composite with 12 wt% particles showed the highest tensile strength of 43.5 MPa, which is a 14.5% improvement over pure epoxy at 38.0 MPa. The maximum flexural strength of 148.7 MPa was obtained at 8 wt% with a 7.5% improvement. Water absorption increased with filler content under both conditions, while saltwater absorption remained lower due to ion-retarded diffusion. Erosion resistance improved for all composites, with the lowest erosion rate of 1.59 mg/min at 20 wt% compared to 1.74 mg/min for pure epoxy. The lowest wear rate of 7.560 × 10⁻⁶ mm³/(Nm) was observed at 4 wt%, after which wear increased with filler content. Thermal analysis showed slower degradation and higher char residue above 450 °C with increasing particle content. This study provides one of the first comprehensive evaluations of epoxy composites reinforced solely with jujube seed particles across mechanical, tribological, and thermal domains. The utilisation of agricultural jujube seed waste as reinforcement supports circular economy principles and contributes to SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), and SDG 13 (Climate Action). Furthermore, the valorisation of agricultural waste into engineering reinforcements promotes resource efficiency and supports the development of sustainable composite materials for advanced engineering applications.

papers.title: A comparative investigation on molten salt hot corrosion of GTA and SMA-welded super-heater pipes of 70 MW CFBC boilers
papers.abstract: Abstract The tubular SA 335 P91 joints are generally used as super-heater pipes in CFBC boilers. This research work presents hot corrosion studies on similar SA 335 P91 joints using ErNiCrMo-3 and E9018 B9 fillers via GTAW and SMAW. The HTC studies were conducted at 770 ± 1˚C employing Na 2 SO 4 +60% V 2 O 5 molten salt mixture on parent metal (PM) and GTA and SMA-weldments with 50 cycles. To predict the corrosion kinetics, TGA were generated. The layer of oxide formed on the surface of weldments and PM has been methodically described using SEM/EDS. The phases of oxide layers were examined through XRD analysis. The investigation confirms that the Ni-rich filler fusion zone coupon exhibits superior oxidation resistance due to the formation of spinel oxide (NiFe 2 O 4 ), which acts as a protective barrier against the penetration of corrosive species. The cross-sectional SEM image and XRD results confirmed that the thin scale formed on the oxidized weldments which were well adherent with the substrate. Blistering was experienced at the E9018 B9 weld zone and found to be more vulnerable to degradation. Consequently, ERNiCrMo-3 filler is recommended for joining similar joints of P91 metals employing the GTAW process used in CFBC boilers.

papers.title: A decade of cannabis‐related hospital admissions in Victoria, Australia: A retrospective observational study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Over the past decade, there has been increased lifetime use of illicit and medical cannabis, underscoring the need to examine public health impacts. This includes reports of increased cannabis-related psychosis. In this context, this study aimed to determine all cannabis-related hospital admissions in Victoria, Australia, over a 10-year period to characterise poisonings and mental health harms. DESIGN: This is a retrospective observational study of the Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED) records, which include all hospital admissions in the state of Victoria and are supplied by the Victorian Department of Health. SETTING: Victoria, Australia. CASES: Hospital records for poisoning (diagnosis code T40.7) and mental health and behavioural disorders (diagnosis codes F12.0-F12.9) related to use of cannabis for the period July 2013 to June 2023 were selected for this study. MEASUREMENTS: Crude and age-standardised rates per 100 000 population are reported. Net percentage change over the 10-year study window was estimated using generalised linear models with a log-population offset, contrasting the final year (2022/2023) against the baseline (2013/2014). RESULTS: There were 39 565 cannabis-related admissions in the 10-year period, including 7263 admissions where cannabis-related harm was the principal diagnosis. The age-standardised rate per 100 000 population was 63.6 for all cannabis-related harm admissions and 11.7 for principal diagnosis cases. The peak annual rate for all cannabis-related harm was observed in 2020/2021 (77.3 per 100 000). There was a 49.0% (P < 0.0001) increase in the rate of hospital admissions with a cannabis-related principal diagnosis, when comparing 2022/2023 with baseline (2013/2014). Overall, harmful use (diagnosis code F12.1) was the most common cannabis-related mental and behavioural disorder. Psychotic disorder (F12.5) was the most common principal diagnosis only (40.1%; n = 2909/7263). When considering principal diagnosis only, the rates were highest in males aged 15-24 years (36.9/100 000), followed by females in the same age group (20.5/100 000). While most principal diagnosis cases involved males, a greater percentage change between the first and last years of the study period was observed for females (+75.1%, P < 0.0001) compared with males (+34.6%, P = 0.003). SUMMARY: Hospital admissions with a cannabis-related principal diagnosis were 49% higher in Victoria, Australia, in 2022/2023 than in 2013/2014, with the highest rates among people aged 15-24 years and a larger relative increase among females than males; however, trends were non-linear, with admission rates peaking in 2020/2021.

papers.title: Comparative study of chemical treatments on the mechanical and moisture absorption behavior of coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composites
papers.abstract: Rising demand for eco-conscious-based functional material drives the focus of materials science field scientists towards research on natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites (NFRPCs), which hold significant attention due to their high strength-to-weight ratio and sustainability. For further enhancement, composites are reinforced with surface-treated fibers, which exhibit optimal performance. This work focuses on fabricating epoxy composites reinforced with Coccinia indica fiber. Different surface-treating chemicals were utilised to determine the optimal chemical and its concentration to obtain effective mechanical and water absorption properties of the composite. Results revealed that Coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composite reinforced with 0.5% of KMnO 4 showed superior performance with a tensile strength of 40.13 MPa and a flexural strength of 89.74 MPa. The compression strength and impact strength of this composite were recorded as 50 MPa and 650 J/m, respectively. By comparison, the untreated CIF/epoxy composite exhibited a tensile strength of 34.59 MPa, flexural strength of 66.63 MPa, compressive strength of 34.4 MPa, and impact strength of 386.7 J/m. The failure mechanism of the fractured samples was determined by employing SEM analysis. Hydrophilic characteristics were determined through the water absorption process, revealing the lowest water intake percentage for this composite, indicating the effective function of KMnO 4 in bonding between the matrix and reinforcement. These findings suggest Coccinia indica fiber-reinforced epoxy composite reinforced with 0.5% of KMnO 4 as a viable alternative to conventional materials, offering a balanced combination of performance, cost-effectiveness, and environmental advantage for semi-structural and automobile applications.

papers.title: Applied nutritional investigation determinants of lower quadriceps skeletal muscle measured by ultrasound at ICU admission: a cross-sectional analysis
papers.abstract: Background Low skeletal muscle (SM) is common at ICU admission and is associated with worse prognosis. Early identification of at-risk patients is essential, but determinants of low SM in critically ill patients remains unclear. Objective To identify sociodemographic, nutritional, and clinical characteristics associated with low SM at ICU admission. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included critically ill patients ≥18 years admitted within 24 hours. Sociodemographic and nutritional data were obtained through anamnesis, while clinical data were extracted from records. Quadriceps muscle layer thickness (QMLT) was measured using a B-mode US. Lower QMLT was defined as values below the sex-specific 25th percentile of the sample. Binary logistic regression was performed. Results 399 patients were included (age 61.4 ± 14.9 years; 56.6% male). Older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.0–1.04), previous unintentional weight loss (OR = 1.64; CI 95% 1.03–2.61), reduced food intake before admission (OR = 2.32; CI 95% 1.44–3.74), and pressure injuries (OR = 1.83; CI 95% 1.05–3.20) were associated with low QMLT. However, in multivariate analysis, only older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.00–1.04) and reduced food intake (OR = 2.26; CI 95% 1.22–4.18) remained independent determinants. Conclusion Older age and reduced food intake were independently associated with lower QMLT at ICU admission. These findings highlight the need for early screening and targeted strategies to mitigate muscle loss and improve outcomes in critically ill patients.

papers.title: LSTM-based prediction and parameter optimization analysis of sandstone subgrade compaction quality
papers.abstract: The study proposes an LSTM-based framework for next-pass Compaction Energy Value (CEV) prediction and subsequent energy planning during sandstone subgrade compaction. Field tests were conducted at two sites, each divided into 24 spatial areas. For each completed compaction pass, cumulative vibration input energy, moisture content, and measured CEV were used to characterize the historical compaction state. At Site 1, information from the first two completed passes was used to predict the CEV after the third pass, whereas at Site 2, information from the first three passes was used to predict the CEV after the fourth pass. The LSTM model achieved RMSE, MAE, and MAPE values of 1.008, 0.801, and 4.74%, respectively, for Site 1, and 1.292, 1.218, and 6.92% for Site 2. To evaluate model selection under the limited field dataset, LSTM was further compared with XGBoost and SVR using identical six-fold spatial cross-validation partitions. LSTM achieved the lowest out-of-fold RMSE, MAE, and MAPE, with values of 0.486, 0.356, and 2.17%, respectively. For subsequent energy optimization at Site 2, area-specific relationships between CEV and energy relationships were first used to estimate initial candidate energies, which were then iteratively adjusted through repeated forward prediction using the fixed LSTM model. After iteration, the proportion of areas with predicted CEV values within the prescribed control interval increased from 75 to 100%, while the predicted CEV range and standard deviation decreased by 75.9% and 82.3%, respectively. The resulting remaining energy demands were further converted into rolling plans, with one weak-vibration pass assigned to 7 areas and one strong-vibration pass to the remaining 17 areas. The proposed framework provides a quantitative link between next-pass CEV prediction, area-specific energy demand, and subsequent rolling planning for sandstone subgrade compaction.
papers.summary: The study proposes an LSTM-based framework for next-pass Compaction Energy Value (CEV) prediction and subsequent energy planning during sandstone subgrade compaction. To evaluate model selection under the limited field dataset, LSTM was further compared with XGBoost and SVR using identical six-fold spatial cross-validation partitions. The resulting remaining energy demands were further converted into rolling plans, with one weak-vibration pass assigned to 7 areas and one strong-vibration pass to the remaining 17 areas.

papers.title: Watermelon vine as dual-functional additive in ecological porous concrete
papers.abstract: Ecological porous concrete (EPC) is constrained by a persistent trade-off: the dense cementitious matrix required for strength reduces porosity and generates a highly alkaline pore environment (pH > 11) inimical to plant growth. To address this, the present study investigates watermelon vine (WV), an abundant agricultural waste, as a dual-functional additive that simultaneously provides physical reinforcement and chemical alkalinity regulation. An integrated orthogonal array–response surface methodology–entropy-weighted TOPSIS framework was established for multi-objective mix optimisation. WV content was identified as the dominant factor governing pore pH, reducing it to 7.6 at an optimal dosage of 3 wt% within 14 days. The optimised mix—comprising 16–20 mm coarse aggregate, 20 wt% fly ash, a water-to-binder ratio of 0.26, and 3 wt% WV—achieved a compressive strength of 10.4 MPa and an effective porosity of 27.7%, with compressive strength remaining stable at 60 d. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a dense interfacial transition zone containing crystalline products morphologically consistent with calcium oxalate, and plant germination tests confirmed vegetation establishment exceeding 80% coverage within 60 days. These converging lines of evidence support an in-situ acid–base neutralisation mechanism, positioning WV as a viable, low-cost functional resource for sustainable construction.

An integrated orthogonal array–response surface methodology–entropy-weighted TOPSIS framework was established for multi-objective mix optimisation. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a dense interfacial transition zone containing crystalline products morphologically consistent with calcium oxalate, and plant germination tests confirmed vegetation establishment exceeding 80% coverage within 60 days.

papers.title: Necroptosis as a key player in cervical cancer progression and management: a systematic review and transcriptomic cross-study consensus analysis
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has improved outcomes for a subset of patients with locally advanced cervical cancer. However, many tumors remain immunologically "cold" and fail to respond. Strategies that enhance tumor immunogenicity are therefore of increasing interest. Necroptosis, a regulated form of inflammatory cell death, has emerged as a potential mechanism capable of promoting the anti-tumor immune responses through the release of damage-associated molecular patterns and enhanced antigen presentation. In this study, we performed a systematic review and transcriptomic cross-study consensus analysis of all studies carried out describing the role and mechanisms of necroptosis occurrence in cervical cancers. We analyzed all published necroptosis-related prognostic gene signatures and integrated these findings into an exploratory transcriptomic analyses to identify mechanistic insights into interlinked biological pathways, and potential therapeutic targets. Following PRISMA guidelines, we analyzed seven published prognostic models, from studies using RNA sequencing and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-based feature selection to generate a prognostic risk score for patients. We then conducted a comparative analyses of eight overlapping genes and their reported risk score coefficients. Across studies, seven necroptosis-related genes were identified, many of which are functionally linked to mitochondrial transport and permeability regulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and inflammatory signaling. Overall, our findings support a key role for necroptosis in cervical cancer, where activation thereof is generally associated with enhanced immune infiltration and activation; thereby improved prognosis. These findings position necroptosis as a promising target for combination therapy strategies aimed at converting immunologically "cold" tumors into more responsive phenotypes. By integrating published signatures with exploratory analyses, we identify potential avenues to modulate necroptotic signaling in ways that may enhance synergy with immunotherapies, and have synthesized a hypothetical cell signaling and interaction diagram. Collectively, this work provides a foundation for future experimental validation and therapeutic development.
papers.summary: Immunotherapy has improved outcomes for a subset of patients with locally advanced cervical cancer. These findings position necroptosis as a promising target for combination therapy strategies aimed at converting immunologically "cold" tumors into more responsive phenotypes. Collectively, this work provides a foundation for future experimental validation and therapeutic development.

papers.title: Taurine is a functional regulator of transthyretin; implication in transthyretin-induced hypothyroidism and amyloidosis
papers.abstract: Transthyretin (TTR) is a homo-tetrameric, 55 kDa, transport protein synthesized mainly in the liver, retinal epithelium, choroid plexus, placental villi and uterus. The main function of TTR is transport of thyroxine (T 4 ) and retinol-binding protein, while it also plays a crucial role in neuroprotection. The binding of thyroxine assists in maintaining the stability of the native tetramer, which is crucial for its functionality. Eventually, dissociation of the tetramer to its monomer results in the formation of toxic oligomeric TTR species and their deposition causes diseases such as cardiomyopathy, polyneuropathy, dementia and preeclampsia. While current kinetic stabilizers occupy the hydrophobic thyroxine-binding pocket, identifying endogenous modulators that maintain TTR homeostasis without impairing hormone transport remains a key objective. In this study, we investigated taurine—a vital neuronal osmolyte and endogenous chemical chaperone—as a functional regulator of TTR dynamics. In the present study, we have systematically evaluated the effect of taurine on the structure-function paradigm of TTR using various biochemical, biophysical tools and cellular model. We discovered that taurine exhibits preferential binding to TTR leading to functional enhancement of T 4 -binding affinity and exhibits anti-aggregation potential towards TTR amyloidosis. Further examination of the mechanism revealed that taurine exhibits preferential binding to TTR microstates and restricts local conformational fluctuations, without altering the global native structure or thermodynamic folding. Together, these findings identify taurine as a trans-acting allosteric chemical chaperone of TTR. This discovery of functional regulation of TTR by taurine offers a promising, non-toxic therapeutic strategy in repurposing of taurine (an FDA-approved supplement) for TTR amyloidosis and TTR-induced hypothyroidism, especially in neuronal and gestational impairments.

papers.title: Stress-induced eIF2α phosphorylation promotes tumor metastasis in oral squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract: Abstract Stress granules (SGs) are non-membranous protein–RNA aggregates that form in the cytoplasm of mammalian cells under various stress conditions. In normal cells, SGs mitigate stress-induced damage by arresting translation. SGs have also been implicated in cancer cell tumor progression and metastasis through their interaction with key signaling pathways. However, their role in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains poorly understood, despite growing interest. In this study, we investigated SG formation and its regulatory effects on tumor progression and metastasis in OSCC. SG markers, including G3BP1, eIF2α, TIAR, and PABP, were significantly overexpressed in OSCC tissues compared with those in adjacent normal tissues. In mouse models established using OSCC cells subjected to hypoxia preconditioning or ISRIB treatment after sodium arsenite-induced stress, suppression of eIF2α phosphorylation was associated with reduced SG formation, tumor growth, and metastatic burden. Moreover, SG formation was elevated during hypoxia-induced stress, highlighting a stress-responsive regulatory mechanism. These findings indicate that SGs promote OSCC progression via eIF2α phosphorylation and might serve as a novel therapeutic target.

papers.title: Nano-eggshell/B(III)as a highly efficient heterogeneous catalyst for the synthesis of 1,3-oxazines in aqueous media, along with DFT simulations
papers.abstract: In the present study, a convenient and greener synthesis of a series of naphtho[1,2- e ][1,3]oxazines was accomplished via three-component one-pot cyclocondensation between β -naphthol, formaldehyde, and various amines using nano-eggshell/B(III) as a natural catalyst in aqueous medium. The Lewis acid nano-eggshell/B(III) catalyst was investigated by techniques such as Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetry analysis (TGA), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), mapping, field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). This approach is totally non-polluting and several advantages, such as shorter reaction time, mild reaction conditions, simple workup, and reduced environmental impact. The experimental results are consistent with the data obtained from the DFT calculations.

papers.title: Performance and Environmental Implications of CO2-Cured Nanoengineered Recycled-Aggregate Concrete with Treated Aggregates
papers.journal: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract The large-scale use of recycled aggregate (RA) in concrete is hindered by its high porosity and water absorption, which degrade mechanical and durability performance. This study introduces a novel approach that integrates nanocomposite modification and CO 2 curing to unlock the potential of recycled-aggregate concrete (RAC). Recycled coarse aggregate was treated and beneficiated with a colloidal nanosilica (CNS)–ultrafine fly ash (UFFA) composite and subjected to CO 2 curing to promote synergistic hydration–carbonation reactions. Thermogravimetric analysis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)-energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the formation of stable mineral phases, including vaterite, calcite, tobermorite [calcium silicate hydrate (C─S─H) gel], and magnesite polymorphs, indicating significant microstructural densification. RAC with 30%–50% modified RA and 3% CNS–15% UFFA exhibited superior phase stability and achieved a 19% reduction in global warming potential compared with the control mix. These findings highlight a scalable and sustainable pathway for producing high-performance RAC, demonstrating that nanoengineered CO 2 curing strategies can simultaneously enhance material quality and reduce environmental impact.
papers.summary: Abstract The large-scale use of recycled aggregate (RA) in concrete is hindered by its high porosity and water absorption, which degrade mechanical and durability performance. RAC with 30%–50% modified RA and 3% CNS–15% UFFA exhibited superior phase stability and achieved a 19% reduction in global warming potential compared with the control mix. These findings highlight a scalable and sustainable pathway for producing high-performance RAC, demonstrating that nanoengineered CO 2 curing strategies can simultaneously enhance material quality and reduce environmental impact.

papers.title: PRRSV infection induces mitochondrial damage and releases mitochondrial dsRNA to activate the NLRP3-dependent inflammatory response
papers.abstract: Abstract Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS), caused by the PRRS virus (PRRSV), remains one of the most economically significant infectious diseases affecting the global swine industry, resulting in annual losses exceeding US $1.2 billion in the USA alone. PRRSV infects porcine alveolar macrophages (PAMs) and induces profound mitochondrial dysfunction, leading to the release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). However, the mechanisms by which PRRSV-induced mitochondrial damage acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) to trigger inflammatory responses have not been fully elucidated. Here, we report that highly pathogenic PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) infection upregulates interleukin-1β (IL-1β) messenger RNA (mRNA) expression and protein secretion in a dose- and time-dependent manner. Transmission electron microscopy revealed progressive mitochondrial swelling, cristae disorganization, and matrix loss during HP-PRRSV infection. Using RNAscope combined with MitoGreen staining, we discovered that mitochondrial double-stranded RNA (mtdsRNA), generated from bidirectional transcription of mitochondrial DNA, is released into the cytosol during PRRSV infection. In vitro, transcription-driven mtdsRNA or mtdsRNA isolated from PAMs directly activated the NLRP3 inflammasome, inducing caspase-1 cleavage and IL-1β secretion. Mechanistically, the PRRSV-encoded nonstructural protein 11 (nsp11) inhibited NLRP3-dependent inflammatory responses by suppressing the oligomerization of the apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase recruitment domain (CARD) (ASC), thereby constraining excessive inflammation and establishing a delicate balance between pro-inflammatory signaling and viral immune evasion. Collectively, our findings identify mtdsRNA as a previously unrecognized mitochondrial DAMP that links PRRSV-induced mitochondrial injury to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, while also revealing a counter-regulatory role for nsp11 in modulating inflammation.

papers.title: SILVER NANOPARTICLES FROM BLACKTHORN EXTRACT AS A FILLER FOR PVA-BASED FILMS: HEAT RESISTANCE, PERMITTIVITY AND ACTION AGAINST PATHOGENS

papers.abstract: This paper reports the preparation of poly(vinyl alcohol)-based nanocomposites containing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) obtained by green synthesis. The nanoparticles were produced from an aqueous extract of blackthorn (Prunus spinosa) fruits and introduced at 3, 5 and 7 wt% into a blend of PVA and poly(4-(trifluoromethyl)benzyl methacrylate) (PTFBMA). The composites were treated hydrothermally and studied by FTIR, NMR, XRD, SEM-EDX, TGA/DSC, contact angle and impedance measurements. Adding AgNPs raised the glass transition temperature from 85 to 101 °C and the onset of thermal decomposition from 310 to 345 °C. The water contact angle reached 70.07° at 5 wt% AgNPs, and the dielectric constant and AC conductivity grew with filler content. The 5 wt% sample was the most active against Candida albicans.

papers.title: Gamma Irradiation-Induced Synthesis of Dextrin/N-Vinylpyrrolidone Biohydrogel for High-Efficiency Adsorptive Removal of Nitrofurantoin and Methylene Blue from Aqueous Media
papers.journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
papers.abstract: Biomedical pollutants, including pharmaceutical residues such as nitrofurantoin (NF) and medical dyes such as methylene blue (MB), are increasingly detected in surface water and wastewater, posing environmental and health concerns due to their durability and biological activity. In this study, dextrin/N-vinylpyrrolidone (Dex/NVP) biohydrogel was successfully synthesized by Co-60 gamma irradiation and evaluated as a green adsorbent for the removal of NF and MB from aqueous media. The optimized hydrogel, prepared with 5 wt% dextrin at an irradiation dose of 30 kGy, achieved a gel fraction of ≈ 90%. Structural (by FTIR and XRD), morphological(by SEM and AFM), and thermal (by TGA) characterization confirmed the successful formation of a porous, cross-linked hydrogel with a high swelling capacity (780–800%) and good thermal stability. Under the optimum adsorption conditions (pH 3.0, adsorbent dosage 0.05 g, and contact time 420 min), the hydrogel removed approximately 78% of NF and 98% of MB, with maximum Langmuir adsorption capacities of 40.93 and 42.51 mg g⁻¹, respectively. Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second-order model, while the Langmuir isotherm provided the best fit, indicating monolayer adsorption on homogeneous active sites. Frontier molecular orbital analysis further supported the contribution of hydroxyl, carbonyl, and amide functional groups to the adsorption process. These findings demonstrate that the radiation-fabricated Dex/NVP biohydrogel is a sustainable and environmentally friendly adsorbent with promising potential for wastewater treatment applications. papers.title: Development of Sustainable Thermoplastic Zein by Partial Substitution of Glycerol with Olive Oil or Oleic Acid: a New Route for Injection-Molded Biopolymers
papers.journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
papers.abstract: Thermoplastic zein formulations containing 25 wt% total modifier were processed by extrusion and injection molding. Glycerol was progressively replaced with oleic acid (OA) or olive oil (OO) at substitution levels ranging from 2.5 to 10 wt%, while maintaining the zein and total modifier contents at 75 and 25 wt%, respectively. The formulation containing 10 wt% OO could not be successfully processed. Partial substitution with OO increased tensile stiffness and strength, reaching 1294 MPa and 25.5 MPa, respectively, for ZEI-GLY-7.5OO, while maintaining elongation at break close to, but below, that of the glycerol-only control. Conversely, substitution with OA generally reduced tensile strength and elongation at break. All modified formulations exhibited lower impact strength than the control. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed low-temperature calorimetric transitions at 2.0–6.3 °C for the OA-containing formulations and − 17.4 to -14.2 °C for the OO-containing formulations, whereas DMTA showed a principal thermomechanical relaxation around 50–60 °C. Thermogravimetric analysis showed onset degradation temperatures of approximately 198 °C for the OO-containing materials, compared with 173 °C for the control and 154–172 °C for the OA-containing formulations. Water contact angles increased from 26° for the control to approximately 30–50° after OA or OO incorporation, indicating reduced surface wettability. Most formulations achieved complete disintegration within four weeks under simulated composting conditions, and all materials were completely disintegrated by week 5. Overall, among the compositions investigated, partial substitution of glycerol with OO produced a favorable tensile-property profile while retaining rapid disintegration. However, these responses reflect the combined effects of OO incorporation and the simultaneous reduction in glycerol content.

papers.title: Boehmeria nivea (Ramie) as a high protein forage crop for small ruminants focusing on agronomic potential, nutritive value, and animal performance
papers.abstract: Climate related stressors and resource limitations in livestock production are increasing in frequency, making the investigation of resilient, nutrient-dense forage alternatives critical. Boehmeria nivea (ramie) has been traditionally used for its fibre utility but has attracted scientific interest as a high-protein forage crop with strong agronomic adaptability. This review synthesises current knowledge on the botanical characteristics, growth ecology and agronomic practices for the cultivation of ramie as a forage species. Ramie is a vigorous perennial, deep-rooted crop and able to adapt to a wide variety of soils; it shows tolerance to moderate drought and several key pests and diseases, it thrives in warm humid conditions, making it suitable for low-input systems. Ramie possesses a very good nutritive profile with crude protein contents mostly between 15 and 24%, in vitro dry matter digestibility values ranging from 55 to 70% and a range of beneficial bioactive compounds. Comparative evaluations in goats and sheep have shown that ramie can support good dry matter intake. In specific feeding trials, partial replacement of conventional roughage with ramie was associated with a 12–18% increase in average daily gain in growing goats, while replacing 25% of the forage component with ramie was associated with an 8–10% increase in milk yield in dairy goats, alongside antioxidant and rumen-health benefits under the studied conditions. Its relatively low requirement for economic inputs and multiple uses makes it a promising forage within climate-smart agriculture frameworks, although long-term economic and life-cycle assessments are still limited. The integration of Boehmeria nivea into forage systems presents opportunities to enhance livestock productivity and resilience, but further interdisciplinary research is required to optimise management practices and critically evaluate its long-term zootechnical, environmental and economic impacts in low-emission livestock systems.

papers.title: Enhancing the Performance of Aqueous Lithium‐Ion Batteries via N‐Methylpyrrolidone Additive
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous lithium‐ion batteries (ALIBs) have garnered significant attention in the field of energy storage due to their inherent safety. However, their practical application is severely constrained by a narrow electrochemical window and electrolyte crystallization at low temperatures. In this study, a modified electrolyte employed the N‐Methylpyrrolidone (NMP) as the additive designated as P‐N2 was developed. Physicochemical characterization (DSC, Raman, and NMR) revealed that the introduction of the NMP component effectively restructured the Li + solvation sheath, thereby suppressing the activity of water molecules and lowering the freezing point. Electrochemical evaluations demonstrated that, at −20°C, full cells utilizing the P‐N2 electrolyte (LiMn 2 O 4 ||NaTi 2 (PO4) 3 /C) exhibited good rate performance and better cycling stability, retaining high capacity even after 1500 cycles. Further interfacial analysis (SEM/XPS) revealed that P‐N2 induced the formation of a dense solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, thereby elucidating the mechanism underlying the observed performance enhancement.

papers.title: Methane bursts during spring thaw in the permafrost region of Northeast China
papers.abstract: Spring thaw in permafrost regions is associated with episodic bursts in atmospheric methane concentration. In this study, these methane bursts were investigated across different permafrost types in Northeast China. MODIS data and Sentinel-5P methane observations were used to derive the thaw onset date and methane burst timing, respectively. Results showed that methane bursts exhibited distinct spatial and interannual variability. Methane burst date was delayed with increasing permafrost stability, and median burst dates occurred in early to mid-April in unstable permafrost, late April to early May in semi-stable permafrost and stable permafrost. Meanwhile, methane bursts generally occurred within 15 days after thaw onset. There was a consistent positive relationship between thaw onset date and methane burst date across all years, with regression slopes of 0.78–1.07. Notably, the median lag tended to shorten from 15 to 22 days in 2020 to 11 days in 2024, suggesting an increasingly rapid temporal response of methane bursts to spring thaw over the study period.

papers.title: Plasmonic Ag@ZIF-8 Monolith for Enhanced Visible-Light Photocatalytic Degradation of Methylene Blue
papers.abstract: Abstract Water contamination by organic dyes remains a major environmental challenge due to their toxicity, persistence, and resistance to conventional treatment methods. In this study, a plasmonic silver-modified metal–organic framework monolith was successfully synthesized via a sol–gel approach. Incorporation of Ag species during gel formation ensured homogeneous distribution within the ZIF-8 framework, which was followed by in situ chemical reduction to produce a reduced material denoted Ag0@ZIF-8. Comprehensive characterization confirmed the structural integrity of the ZIF-8 framework, with TEM revealing electron-dense silver domains and UV–vis DRS showing enhanced visible-light absorption associated with localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR). The photocatalytic performance of Ag0@ZIF-8 was evaluated through the degradation of methylene blue under visible light. The catalyst exhibited significantly enhanced activity compared to pristine ZIF-8 and the Ag+@ZIF-8 monolith, achieving a maximum degradation efficiency of 90.4 ± 1.0% under optimized conditions (pH 8, 60 mg of catalyst, 60 min irradiation). Kinetic studies confirmed pseudo-first-order behavior with a rate constant of 0.0358 min–1 (R2 = 0.9923). Scavenger experiments revealed that superoxide radicals (•O2–) played the dominant role in methylene blue degradation, with hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and photogenerated holes (h+) making secondary contributions. The Ag0@ZIF-8 monolith also demonstrated good reusability, retaining over 75% of its initial activity after five cycles. Overall, this work highlights the synergistic interaction between plasmonic silver species and the ZIF-8 monolith, resulting in enhanced visible-light-driven photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants, offering a promising strategy for wastewater treatment applications.

papers.title: A comparative study on the effects of clove oil, flaxseed oil, and almond oil as an additive on the lubricating characteristics of chemically modified used coconut oil
papers.abstract: Abstract Lubrication is widely associated with contact surfaces having relative motion to decrease friction and wear. The majority of locally available lubricants have petroleum products as a base, which are toxic to the environment. The excess usage of petroleum products is also causing drastic fossil fuel depletion, emphasizing the necessity of an alternative to these locally available lubricants. Due to superior tribological properties and biodegradability, vegetable oil‐based bio‐lubricants are considered potential alternatives. However, they also possess certain drawbacks, like poor cold flow properties and oxidative stability, which could be rectified by chemical modification processes and with the use of many eco‐friendly additives. In this study, the oil leftover from the cooking process, Used Coconut Oil (UCO), is chemically modified by means of epoxidation and the trans‐esterification process to form the Chemically Modified Used Coconut Oil (CMUCO). Clove oil, Flaxseed oil, and Almond oil are added separately to this CMUCO as additives to form the Modified Used Coconut Oils (MUCO 1, MUCO 2, and MUCO 3, respectively). The present study evaluates and compares the lubricant properties of MUCO 1, MUCO 2, and MUCO 3 with those of UCO and CMUCO. The analysis indicates that the incorporation of clove oil as an additive has shown an enhancement in the chemical, tribological, rheological, and thermal properties compared to CMUCO. Furthermore, MUCO 1 also shows improvements in the cold flow properties and oxidative stability, which were previously considered major drawbacks of CMUCO.

papers.title: Preparation and Investigation of Solvatomorphs of Anti-Tumor Candidate RA-XII
papers.abstract: RA-XII, a unique natural cyclopeptide, is a potential anti-colorectal cancer candidate by mainly inhibiting protective autophagy, SREBP-1-dependent lipid biogenesis and suppressing activation of the Akt-mTOR pathway in HCT-116 cells. However, there have been no investigations into its solid forms, and its poor solubility restricts its application in the development of clinical anticancer agents. Background/Objectives: To investigate and develop advantageous medicinal solid forms of RA-XII and further improve its solubility characteristics. Methods: Various recrystallization methods were used to screen crystal forms of RA-XII, and single crystals (Forms I, II and V) were obtained by the vapor diffusion method. The forms were characterized by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), spectroscopy (FTIR, Raman), thermal analyses (DSC, TGA) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Structural parameters were determined by single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). The solubility and intrinsic dissolution rate were determined in a pH 7.4 pharmaceutical buffer solution with water. Hirshfeld surface analyses, molecular electrostatic potential surface (MEPs) analyses and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to reveal differences in hydrogen bond interactions of the crystal structure. Results: Five solvatomorphs and an amorphous form of RA-XII were successfully obtained. Then, three single crystals of Forms I, II and V were obtained, and their conformations were investigated. Hirshfeld surface analyses and crystal structures revealed significant differences in hydrogen bonding interactions and molecular packing. Moreover, MEPs analyses and MD suggested the formation mechanisms of RA-XII solvatomorphs, in which the hydrogen bonding strengths increase between RA-XII and solvent molecules. Conclusions: Form I is physically more stable and exhibits great solubility in water. Form I possesses significant medicinal advantages. These findings provide valuable insights into understanding the solvatomorph mechanisms and the quality control of RA-XII.
papers.summary: RA-XII, a unique natural cyclopeptide, is a potential anti-colorectal cancer candidate by mainly inhibiting protective autophagy, SREBP-1-dependent lipid biogenesis and suppressing activation of the Akt-mTOR pathway in HCT-116 cells. However, there have been no investigations into its solid forms, and its poor solubility restricts its application in the development of clinical anticancer agents. Background/Objectives: To investigate and develop advantageous medicinal solid forms of RA-XII and further improve its solubility characteristics.
